- The ledger: 80 pairs, none differing, 14 unchecked. 11 of the 14 are the other calls of the
  three corporation routes, which the parity tool now reads.
- Staged and undone: the director's change. The store was copied with the server stopped and
  put back after, the settings read 0 and none again, and the copy is deleted.

**A server defect, fixed by a sub-agent** (eve.js `3ccbcef51`, on its local `main`, not pushed).
The server never sent `OnCorpAggressionSettingsChange`: the name was nowhere in its source. A
director's change was stored and answered to the caller, and no client's kept settings changed,
the caller's own included, until it changed corporation or logged in again. The fix sends the
notice, with the settings the call answers, to every session of that corporation. The sub-agent
wrote the test first and watched it fail (the caller's session was sent none), then broke the
fix two ways to see the test's "sends nothing" halves fail. I read the diff, restarted the
server and ran the director's change above.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The pilot's applications are not kept, though the client keeps them.** The BFF's
  pilot-training onboarding has an officer change a trainee's application and then reads the
  trainee's applications at once, on the trainee's own connection. The server's notice to the
  trainee and its answer to the officer travel on different connections, so a kept list could
  be a notice behind and the onboarding would say the offer was not made. I had built it kept,
  and withdrew that before committing.
- **The notice's address type is a choice.** No recording holds the notice, and the client does
  not read the address type. The sub-agent sent it as `corpid`, as two sibling notices are sent.
- **The choosing waits for the three.** It costs 6 ms and means a pilot handed to the page has
  its settings kept already.
- **The transport tests' stand-in sets the choosing's registry bind and calls aside** and counts
  registries apart from other objects. Without that, about thirty older tests that list what was
  bound, or name an object by its number, each needed changing, and would again for the next
  service a choosing binds. What is set aside is kept on the session and the new tests read it.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- **The members route differs between the transports in shape.** Member tracking comes as a
  cached call's wrapper through the gateway and as the rows themselves on the game port, and a
  packed row's 64-bit columns come as strings on one and as numbers on the other. No window of
  the page reads the route yet.
- **A call sent right behind the table of agents is answered late**: the registry's resolve
  82 ms after it reached the server when sent behind `GetAgents`, 1 ms when sent before it, and
  under 1 ms two seconds after login. In an earlier run the dogma location's resolve came in
  right behind the table, and the call after it came in 52 ms later. I did not look into why.
  What the choosing waits for is now asked first.
- **eve.js's `testStoreIsolationGuard.test.js` was red for the sub-agent while the live server
  ran**: 15 of 34 failed with "live gameStore changed", the store's write-ahead file the only
  thing changed. It scans none of the files the fix touched. Not run again with the server
  stopped.
- An older assertion in eve.js's friendly-fire test, that a denied call sends nothing, is made
  on a session no broadcast could reach. The sub-agent's new test covers the case with sessions
  that are registered.

**Not seen working.**

- A pilot's corporation changing under its session, with the settings and names read again:
  tests only.
- Another member's client getting the notice. The test corporation's two members are on one
  account, so only the caller's own session was seen to get it live. The server's test has two
  members' sessions and one of another corporation.
- The settings shown in the browser: no window of the page shows them.

**Not done.**

- The client's own keeping of its applications (above).
- The 11 other calls of the three corporation routes, read against the client.

Commit `75eb1a3`, pushed. The next of item 1 of the last list.

  name; its corporation's contacts, `GetCorporateContacts()` on the corporation's registry, unless

## 2026-10-09 — the alliance's registry, on the client's moniker for its alliance

Commit `bf038de`, pushed. The next of item 1 of the last list.

**What the retail client does** (the Tranquility recordings, searched first: `allianceRegistry`,
`GetAllianceContacts`, `GetRelationships`, `OnAllianceChanged` and four more names are in no file.
No recorded pilot was in an alliance. So this is `all_cso.py`, its four companions and
`eveMoniker.py` alone).

- The alliance service keeps one moniker, `Moniker('allianceRegistry', (session.allianceid, 1))`,
  and binds it for its own sake as it makes it, as the corporation's registry is bound.
- It makes it when something first wants it, which at login is the address book asking for the
  alliance's contacts, and makes and binds a new one at once when the session's alliance changes.
  With no alliance it cannot make one, and asks nothing.
- Everything of the session's own alliance is asked of the moniker. Six things asked about any
  alliance by its ID are asked of the service by name, and so is `GetAlliance(allianceID)` for
  an alliance that is not the session's.

**What the BFF did.** On the game port everything of `allianceRegistry` went by name.

**What was built.**

- The transport makes and binds the alliance's moniker and asks on it what the client asks on
  it, and by name what the client asks by name. `GetAlliance` goes to the moniker with nothing
  for the pilot's own alliance, however the BFF named it, and by name for another.
- The moniker is kept when the pilot moves, and made and bound again when the session's alliance
  changes.
- For a pilot in an alliance the address book's reads at the choosing bind the moniker and ask
  `GetAllianceContacts`, beside the other three.
- For a pilot in no alliance, what the BFF asks of the moniker's methods goes by name as before,
  and is in the ledger as the web's alone.
- Nine pairs are in the registry of the client's calls. The parity tool reads the six alliance
  routes.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 4 more, and one of the registry's brought up to it. 25 ways of breaking it were tried:
  24 are caught, and the one that survives changes nothing any entry can show today (which of
  two equal sets of arguments is sent for a pilot in no alliance).
- Suite: 9766 tests, 9742 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. No test process left behind.
- **Through the BFF, on the game port, by script, as Test Two (in an alliance), with the server's
  log for it:** at login the alliance's registry was resolved and bound, with the online state
  asked for between the two, and then `GetAllianceContacts` asked of the object. The six alliance
  routes read after, one of them twice (with the pilot's own alliance named, and with none): ten
  calls on that object and eight by name, as the client's would go, and no other bind.
- **On both transports, by script:** for Test Two the six routes are identical (four) or the
  same but for the form of a long number (two). Two passes, both 19 identical, 10 tolerated,
  2 moved, 3 divergent. For Test Pilot (in no alliance) all six are identical.
- **In the browser, on the game port, as Test Two:** chosen, 25 windows open, no failure shown.
  The server's log has the moniker bound and the contacts asked once for that session. No window
  of the page shows anything of an alliance (the Character Sheet still reads "Unknown
  alliance"), so nothing of it was seen there.

## 2026-10-09 — the notifications, asked at login and kept until they change

Commit `f5cc4cf`, pushed. The next of item 1 of the last list.

**What the retail client does** (the Tranquility recordings, searched first: `GetAllNotifications`
is in 7 files, `OnNotificationReceived` in 37, `GetUnprocessed`, `GetByGroupID` and
`MarkAsProcessed` in 2 each; then `notificationSvc.py` and `notificationUI.py`).

- As its character is chosen the notification window asks for all the pilot's notifications:
  `notificationMgr.GetAllNotifications(fromID=...)`, a keyword, the last notification the user
  cleared. In the recorded login it is nought, and the answer a `CRowset`.
- The service keeps that list, and two more it asks for when first wanted: the unread ones
  (`GetUnprocessed()`) and those of a group (`GetByGroupID(groupID)`).
- It works the server's three notices (`OnNotificationReceived`, `OnNotificationDeleted`,
  `OnNotificationUndeleted`) and its own marking and deleting into its lists in place.

**What the BFF did.** On the game port nothing was asked at login, and each read of the
notifications route asked for all three lists. The page's Activity window reads the route as it
opens and at each press of Refresh.

**What was built.**

- As a pilot is chosen the transport asks for all its notifications, from nought, and waits for
  the answer.
- The three lists are kept as answered. A read of one through the BFF is answered from what is
  kept, and asked for where nothing is.
- At any of the server's three notices, and after any of the pilot's own six writes, done or
  refused, all three are forgotten. An answer on its way at that moment is handed on and not
  kept.
- The transport tests that list what a choosing asks are held to one list now, which the first
  of them spells out. Ten had to change for this unit, as nine did for the last but one.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 3 more, and ten older ones changed as above. 28 ways of breaking it were tried, each
  of the three notices and each of the six writes among them, and all 28 are caught.
- Suite: 9769 tests, 9745 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. No test process left behind.

## 2026-10-09 — the calendar's two months and the contracts' login figures, asked at login

Commit `40ac63c`, pushed. The next two of item 1 of the last list, done together.

**What the retail client does** (the Tranquility recordings, searched first: `GetEventList` is in
10 files, `GetLoginInfo` in 7, the calendar's three notices in none; then `eveCalendarsvc.py` and
`contracts.py`).

- Its calendar service keeps a month's events once asked for, for the session. A minute timer
  asks for this month and the next soon after a character is chosen:
  `calendarProxy.GetEventList(month, year)`, at the proxy node. The recorded login has the two
  as calls 186 and 187.
- It works the server's `OnNewCalendarEvent`, `OnEditCalendarEvent` and `OnRemoveCalendarEvent`
  into the months it keeps, puts a personal event of its own making in itself, and forgets every
  month when the session's corporation or alliance changes.
- Its contracts service asks `contractProxy.GetLoginInfo()` once, when the notification window
  is ready (call 142 in the recorded login), to raise its own notices of contracts that want
  attention. It keeps nothing of the answer.

**What the BFF did.** On the game port neither was asked at login. The Activity window's read
asked for the month at every opening and every press of Refresh, and the Contracts window asks
for the figures each time it opens.

**What was built.**

- As a pilot is chosen the transport asks for the contracts' figures, then the notifications,
  then this month's events and the next's by the server's clock, and waits for them.
- The months are kept. A read of a kept month through the BFF is answered from what is kept,
  and another month is asked for when first wanted and kept.
- They are forgotten at any of the server's three notices, after any of the pilot's own seven
  writes that make, change or delete an event, done or refused, and in another corporation or
  alliance.
- The contracts' figures are asked for and not kept.
- The notifications' lists and the calendar's months are kept by one helper now
  (`src/gamePort/keptReads.js`), with tests of its own.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 8 more (3 of the transport, 5 of the helper). Two older ones changed: the tally's
  most-called pair is now called three times, so that it stays the most called, and the test of
  calls at the proxy node counts from after the choosing. The one list of what a choosing sends
  last has three more in it. 46 ways of breaking it were tried,
  each notice and each write of both services among them, and all 46 are caught.
- Suite: 9777 tests, 9753 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. No test process left behind.
- **Through the BFF, on the game port, by script, as Test Two, with the server's log for it:**
  at login, in order, the applications, the contracts' figures, the notifications, the two
  months, the table of agents. Then the calendar route read three times, in 6, 3 and 2 ms: the
  month was not asked for again. It lists one event, the server's own.
- **A personal event made, by script, on the game port:**

  | Step | The month asked of the server | Events in it |
  |---|---|---|
  | three reads before | no | 1 |
  | the event made | | |
  | the read after | once | 2 |
  | the read after that | no | 2 |
  | the gateway's own read | asked | 2 |

  The server sent the pilot no notice of its own event, which is what the client expects.

**What the BFF did.** Its names route answered from its static tables. Those did not have Test
Two's corporation or alliance, and the Character Sheet read "Unknown corporation" and "Unknown
alliance". Nothing of ours asked the game server for a name.

  know, and keeps every row for as long as the pilot is on.

  name and whose ID is a player owner's.
- A row names an owner only as the kind of thing its type says it is. With no pilot online the
  route says it does not know, so the page asks again.

  nought named "Item" and the ID.

## 2026-10-09 — training paused as the client pauses it, and the queue kept

Commit `0c0f2a4`, pushed. The first part of item 2 of the last list.

**What the retail client does** (the Tranquility recordings, searched first: `AbortTraining` and
the server's `OnSkillQueuePausedServer` are in one recording and its notes; then
`skillQueuePanelNew.py`, `skillsvc.py` and `skillQueueSvc.py`).

- Its queue panel pauses with one call, `skillHandler.AbortTraining()`, and only while a skill
  is in training.
- The server stops the skill and says so. The client takes the start and the end off every entry
  of the queue it keeps, and keeps the entries. It does not ask for the queue again.
- Its start button saves the queue as it stands, `SaveNewQueue(queue, activate=True)`.

**What the page did.** "Stop training" saved an empty queue. Training stopped and the queue was
gone.

**What was measured first**, by script on the game port, with the old page's routes:

| Step | The sheet's queue |
|---|---|
| two skills saved | training, the first from 8,000 points at 30 a minute |
| the pause | not training, both skills still on it, no start or end to either |
| two seconds on | the same |
| the queue saved again | training, the first from 8,001 points |
| paused again | not training, both skills still on it |
| a pause with nothing in training | answered, and nothing changed |
| the gateway's read of it | not training, both on it, the first from 8,002 points and marked as in training |

**What was built.**

- The Skills window pauses with the BFF's abort-training route and reads the sheet again.
- A paused queue is shown as paused: its skills still listed, each row saying "paused", and a
  "Start training" button that saves the queue as it stands. A queue that is training offers
  "Pause training". An empty queue offers neither.
- The call is in the registry of the client's calls. On the game port it goes to the skill
  handler's object, and what is kept is stopped by the server's notice, as the client's is.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 4 more (2 of the page's flow, 2 of the panel), and one of the transport's made longer.
  17 ways of breaking it were tried. One survived at first, every row saying "paused" whether
  paused or not, and led to a case. All are caught now.
- Suite: 9786 tests, 9762 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. No test process left behind.
- **In the browser, on the game port, as Test Two, with a paused queue of two skills staged:**
  the window read "Training is paused", listed Afterburner IV and Archaeology II as paused, and
  offered "Start training". Pressed: Afterburner IV trained, 20 h 41 m left, 8,006 of 45,255
  points at 30 a minute, and the button read "Pause training". Pressed: paused again, both
  skills still on the queue. The server's log has `SaveNewQueue` and then `AbortTraining` on the
  handler's object for the two presses. Logged out with the page's own button.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 19 identical, 10
  tolerated, 2 moved, 3 divergent, as it was.
- The ledger: 104 pairs, none differing, 20 unchecked, one the web's alone.
- Staged and undone: the queue and some seconds of training. The store was copied with the
  server stopped and put back after, the sheet read 52 skills, 385,914 points and an empty queue
  again, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The page can no longer throw a queue away with one press.** Emptying it is taking each skill
  off it. Whether the client's panel has a button to empty its queue I did not look.
- **The buttons' words are the page's own** ("Pause training", "Start training").
- **A paused entry's starting points are left as they were when the queue was last saved**, as
  the client leaves them. The gateway's read has the points the skill stopped at (8,002 against
  8,001 above). The page shows neither while the queue is paused.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- **The gateway's sheet marks a paused queue's first skill as in training**, with its rate. The
  game port's marks none.
- A pause with nothing in training is answered by this server and changes nothing. The page
  offers the pause only for a queue that is training, as the client's panel does.
- **`npm test` does not check the page's types.** A mistake in a test of mine was found by
  `npm run build:web`, which the browser check needs anyway. It is in the brief's list now.

**Not seen working.**

- A pause the server refuses: tests only.
- The new buttons on the gateway: not pressed there. Its sheet of a paused queue was read by
  script.

## 2026-10-09 — a walk in space on the game port, and the scanner's sites asked as the client asks

Commit `f05ca30`, pushed. Part of item 24 of the last list.

**The walk**, in the browser, on the game port, as Test Two in its Badger, the store put aside
first:

| Step | What the page showed |
|---|---|
| Undock | "In space", Muvolailen, 146 m/s; the ship's bar with hold, capacitor, shield, armour, hull and an empty rack |
| The space windows opened | Flight, Mining, Drones, Shots fired, Equipment, Scanner, each with its own readings |
| Warp to a belt 324,000 km off | "Warp Drive Active", the destination named, the distance counting down to 10 km, then "Engines stopped" |
| At the belt | 135 things in the tactical view; 16 sites in the Scanner |
| "Take me there and dock", the station it left | "Establishing Warp Vector", the warp, and docked |

No failure was shown at any step, and the last 400 requests the page made were each answered 200.

**What the walk found.**

- **Five calls nobody had read against the client.** Four are the client's as the BFF sends
  them: the menu's warp `CmdWarpToStuff('item', itemID, minRange=...)`, the autopilot's
  `CmdWarpToStuffAutopilot(destinationID)` and `CmdDock(stationID, shipID)` on the ballpark's
  object, and `beyonce.GetFormations()` by name. The recordings have each (30, 3, 24 and 30
  files), and each is in the registry now.
- **The fifth was not the client's.** The client's sensor suite asks for the sites it can see
  with `scanSvc.GetScanMan().GetFullState()`, on the object `GetSystemScanMgr()` answers, and a
  recording has it on that object. The scanner's route asked `scanMgr.GetFullState` by the
  service's name. **Fixed:** on the game port the route asks the scan manager's object, bound
  once, as the scanner's other calls do. The gateway's route is as it was.

**Proof of the fix.**

- Tests: 2 more (one of the transport, one of the route). 17 ways of breaking it were tried,
  and all 17 are caught.
- Suite: 9788 tests, 9764 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **In the browser, on the game port, undocked again on the new code:** the Scanner listed its
  16 sites, and the same after "Refresh scanner". The server's log has `GetSystemScanMgr` once
  and `GetFullState` twice on the object it answered, and none by name. Docked again with the
  page's Dock button, logged out with its own.
- The second walk's ledger: 72 pairs, none unchecked, none differing, none the web's alone.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 19 identical, 10
  tolerated, 2 moved, 3 divergent, as it was.
- Staged and undone, twice: the store was copied with the server stopped before each walk and
  put back after, the sheet read 52 skills, 385,914 points and an empty queue again, and the
  copies are deleted.

**A claim withdrawn.** Two entries ago I wrote that nothing of ours asks `station.GetGuests`,
`stationSvc.GetStationItemBits` or `map.GetStationInfo` "but the route that passes on any call".
The page's own docked panel asks all three, through that route, each time a pilot docks or is
chosen docked: the server's log of the walk has each twice. I had searched the BFF's source and
not the page's. The login report's "by a feature" is right for them. What I said of the column
in general stands: it marks a call that has an entry in the registry.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- **The formations are asked for three times in a session in space**: once by the park, as the
  client asks, and twice by the page's own route as its windows open and refresh. The park's
  own asking is not in the ledger.
- **In space the Agents window still lists the station's agents** ("2 at this station").
- **The page asks the BFF for its bots four times a cycle**, docked or not, with nothing
  running. That is between the page and the BFF: the game server is asked nothing for it.
- One more route asks `scanMgr.GetFullState` by name on the game port, with seven other reads.
  No window of the page reads it.
- The browser's console had some five hundred failed requests in it (502 and 500). They are
  from the hours before, each time the game server was stopped for a copy of the store: the walk
  itself had none.

**Not seen working.**

- Anything fitted: the Badger has no modules, so nothing was switched on, locked or shot at.
- The rest of item 24: an agent talked to in space, a ship boarded, a fleet formed there.

## 2026-10-09 — a fitted ship flown and mined with on the game port; the locked targets kept as the client keeps them; an afterburner switched on with no target

Commit `63ff463`, pushed. Part of item 24 of the last list.

**The walk**, in the browser, on the game port, as Test Two. The store was put aside first. By
script, through the BFF's own routes: a Venture given, boarded, and fitted with two Miner I and
a 1MN Afterburner I, all three online. Then, in the page:

| Step | What the page showed |
|---|---|
| Undock | "In space", the Venture's bar, a rack of three modules, each "click to switch on" |
| Warp to a belt | "Engines stopped" at the belt; 200 rows in the overview, 121 of them rocks |
| Lock a rock 22 km off | "Lock refused: That target is out of the module's range." |
| Approach it, lock again inside 16.5 km | "LOCKED" on the row and in the selected item's panel |
| Both lasers and the afterburner switched on from the rack | All three "active"; "Running 15s" in Equipment |
| A few cycles | Ore hold 0, then 24.15, then 400.35 of 5,000 m³ of Scordite II-Grade |
| All three switched off, the lock released | "click to switch on" again; "Nothing locked yet" |
| "Take me there and dock" | The warp, and docked |

Everything worked. The refusal at 22 km is the server's and is right: its figure for a
Venture's targeting range is 16,500 m, a lock at 15 km was taken and one at 22 km was not. The
client sends such a lock too and shows the server's refusal (`TryLockTarget` does not look at
the range).

**What the walk found, and what was done about it.**

- **The locked targets were asked for about once a second: 395 `GetTargets` in one short
  flight.** The client asks for them once, on undocking or on logging in in space, with
  `GetTargeters` beside it, and from then on goes by the server's `OnTarget` notices. A
  Tranquility recording of an undock has exactly that, after godma's prime. **Fixed:** the
  transport keeps both lists as the client's target service does (`src/gamePort/pilotTargets.js`)
  and the BFF's readings are answered from them. A list that is not known is asked for. The
  gateway's reading is as it was.
- **The afterburner was switched on with the locked rock as its target.** The page sends what
  is locked with every module. The client's button gives a target to an effect aimed at one and
  None to any other. **Fixed** at the transport: a target goes with a target effect alone.
- **Four calls nobody had read against the client**, all the client's as the BFF sends them and
  now in the registry: `CmdFollowBall` (the menu's approach; recorded as `(itemID, 50)`),
  `CmdSetSpeedFraction(1.0)`, `Board` on the ship's moniker, and `slash.SlashCmd` by name (no
  recording has one: it is read from the client's GM menus).
- **The refusal's words were wrong for a lock**: "out of the module's range", with no module in
  it. The server uses the one error for a lock and for a module. **Fixed** in the page: "That
  target is out of range. Get closer and try again."

**Proof.**

- Tests: 8 of the new module, 6 of the transport, 1 and some lines of the registry. 63 ways of
  breaking it were tried, and all 63 are caught. Three survived the first pass: two got a case
  each, and the third was a check that did nothing, which is gone.
- Suite: 9803 tests, 9779 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. The page builds.
- **In the browser, on the game port, the same walk again on the new code**, read beside the
  server's log of it:

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `GetTargets` in the flight | 395 | 1, right after the dogma bind at the undock |
  | `GetTargeters` | 0 | 1, right after it |
  | The lock shown on the page | from the next reading | from the server's `OnTarget`, 2.7 s after `AddTarget` |
  | The afterburner's `Activate` | `target=5020570318957` | `target=null` |
  | The lasers' `Activate` | the rock | the rock |
  | The far lock's refusal | "out of the module's range" | "out of range" |

  The ore hold went from 400.35 to 496.95 m³, the lock was released ("Nothing locked yet"), the
  ship docked, and the page was logged out with its own button.
- The second walk's ledger: 83 pairs, 174 calls, none unchecked, none differing, one the web's
  alone (below).
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 19 identical, 10
  tolerated, 2 moved, 3 divergent, as it was.
- Staged and undone: the store was copied with the server stopped and put back after. The
  sheet reads 52 skills, 385,914 points and an empty queue again, the ship is the Badger,
  docked where it was, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Mining, not shooting.** The list said "a thing locked and shot at". The pilot's station has
  sentry guns and a spawned hostile kills the test ship, so the walk locked a rock and mined it.
  The calls are the same ones a gun makes (`AddTarget`, `Activate` with a target, `Deactivate`).
  Something shot at is still on the list.
- **A list that is not known is asked for, where the client would show none.** The client's
  lists start empty and are only ever filled by its one asking and the notices. If that asking
  failed here, the page would show nothing locked while the server held a lock. So the
  transport tells "empty" from "not known" and asks when it does not know. On a flight where
  nothing fails that is the client's traffic exactly; the walk's log shows it.
- **Three small things the client does are not done**, each written at the top of
  `pilotTargets.js`: a target named before its ball has come is a target at once here; a ship
  that blew up goes when the server says it is lost, not when its explosion ends; and the lists
  stand when the ballpark is given a whole new state, where the client empties them.
- **The test stand-in's session now names a solar system to a pilot chosen in space**, as the
  server does. It named a station to every pilot. Two older tests of modules read "the last
  call made" and now read "the last switching on or off", since godma's asking for the targets
  comes in beside it. Two more used a docked `GetTargets` as any read of the dogma location's,
  and use another read now: docked, nothing is asked for the targets.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- **The BFF's routes for the menu's approach, keep at range and orbit send
  `CmdSetSpeedFraction(1.0)` first.** The autopilot does that before its own approach; the
  client's menu sends none. It is in the registry's note for the call, and on the list.
- `dogmaIM.QueryAttributeValue` is asked once for each module switched off, for how long its
  cycle is. The client never asks the server that.
- The Flight window read "GOTO · speed 100%" at the belt while the ship's bar read "Engines
  stopped": the window's ship state is as old as its last refresh.
- A reading of the targets that is refused while godma's own asking is also refused costs two
  askings, not one. No refusal of it has been seen live.
- A rack button does nothing for a plain click from a script: it takes a pointer going down and
  up. That is the page's "hold to overload", and a person's click works.
- My scratch folder for this session holds 33 older copies of the store, 1.9 GB, from before
  the copies were deleted as a rule. They are outside both repositories. I have left them.

**Not seen working.**

- Something shot at. An agent talked to in space, a ship boarded in space, a fleet formed there.
- What has the ship locked (`GetTargeters`) with something locking it: nothing locked the ship
  in either walk, and no window of the page shows it.

## 2026-10-09 — an approach, keep at range and orbit sent alone, as the client's menu sends them

Commit `b2ac320`, pushed. Item 25 of the last list.

**What the client does.** Its menu sends an approach as `CmdFollowBall(targetID, 50)`, keep at
range as `CmdFollowBall(targetID, range)` and an orbit as `CmdOrbit(targetID, range)`, each
alone. Only its autopilot opens the throttle first: `CmdSetSpeedFraction(1.0)`, then
`CmdFollowBall(gateID, 0.0)`. The recordings have all four so: a mission's flight with follows
and orbits and no speed call anywhere in it, and an autopilot's flight with the speed call
before each follow of a gate.

**What the BFF did.** Its three routes sent `CmdSetSpeedFraction(1.0)` before every follow and
orbit.

**What it does now.** On the game port the routes send the speed call only before an approach
with no range. That is the autopilot's, and it is what the page's own autopilot asks for (three
places in `flow.ts`, each with a range of 0). Through the gateway the routes are as they were.

`CmdOrbit` and `CmdStop` turned up unread in the walk's ledger. Both are the client's as the BFF
sends them, and both are in the registry now.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the routes (one for each transport), and 2 more lines of the registry's. 17 ways
  of breaking it were tried, and all 17 are caught. The first of them puts the rule back as it
  was, and the game port's test fails on it.
- Suite: 9805 tests, 9781 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. The page builds.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** as Test Two in its Badger: undocked, stopped, and from
  the stop each of the selected item's three buttons in turn.

  | Button | The ship's bar | Speed before, and some seconds after |
  |---|---|---|
  | Approach | "Approaching Caldari Sentry Gun II" | 11.1 m/s, then 78.8 |
  | Keep at range | "Keeping at Range Caldari Sentry Gun II - 10 km" | 10.9, then 95.4 |
  | Orbit | "Orbiting Caldari Sentry Gun II - 5,000 m" | 4.9, then 99.5 |

  The server's log of it: `CmdStop`, `CmdFollowBall … range=50`, `CmdStop`, `CmdFollowBall …
  range=10000`, `CmdStop`, `CmdOrbit … range=5000`, `CmdDock`. No `CmdSetSpeedFraction` in it.
  Docked with the page's own button and logged out with its own.
- **By script, on the game port,** the four forms one after another, each from a stop. The
  server's log: `CmdSetSpeedFraction fraction=1` then `CmdFollowBall … range=0` for the
  autopilot's; `CmdFollowBall … range=50`, `CmdFollowBall … range=5000` and `CmdOrbit …
  range=5000` alone for the menu's. The pilot's own ballpark read FOLLOW, FOLLOW, FOLLOW and
  ORBIT, each with the speed fraction at 1. That flight's ledger: 35 pairs, none unchecked, none
  differing.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 19 identical, 10
  tolerated, 2 moved, 3 divergent, as it was.
- Nothing was staged: the pilot undocked and docked where it was, in the ship it was in.

**A claim caught before it was committed.** I wrote in the reference that CCP's ballpark
library restarts a stopped ball when it is told to follow. It does not: it sets a stopped
ball's speed fraction to 1 for a go-to-point only. I had read the line off a search's listing
and put it under the wrong function. What is written now is what was measured: on this server a
stopped ship told to follow or orbit moves off. What Tranquility's server does there is not in
the library, and no recording I looked at has a follow straight after a stop.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The gateway's routes are left opening the throttle.** As with the other units, what the
  old transport sends is not changed.
- **A range of 0 is taken for the autopilot's.** The route cannot see who is asking. The
  client's menu never sends 0 for an approach (it is always 50 m) and the client's autopilot
  always does, so the range tells them apart. A bot of the page's
  that approaches with no range is sent as the autopilot is.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- The client's menu sends nothing when the ship is already following or orbiting that ball at
  that range. The BFF sends the command each time it is asked.
- A comment in the page's fleet companion says an approach "opens the throttle BEFORE it sends
  the follow, so a refused one leaves the hull under way". That is true of the gateway only
  now. The code beside it is right either way and is as it was.
- Right after the autopilot's approach the route's own answer read the ship as "STOP", and
  five seconds on as "FOLLOW": the answer is read before the server's word of the new mode has
  come.

## 2026-10-09 — an order the ship is already flying is not sent again

Commit `ffa6627`, pushed. The second half of item 25 of the last list.

**What the client does.** Its menu sends no approach, keep at range or orbit when its own ball,
in its own ballpark, is already in that mode, after that ball, at that range. Two recordings
were read for it: in each the same follow goes out three times within one second, before the
ballpark has heard of the first, and not again while the ship is flying it. Its autopilot does
not look, and always sends.

**What the BFF did.** It sent the order every time it was asked. The page's own loops ask
often.

**What it does now.** On the game port the three routes ask the pilot's transport, which has
the ship's own ballpark, and hold such an order back. The route's answer then says
`alreadySo`. The autopilot's approach is always sent. Through the gateway every order is sent,
as before.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 1 of the transport and 2 of the routes. The transport's and the game port's route's
  were watched to fail on the code as it was; the gateway's passed there, as it should. 32 ways
  of breaking it were tried, and all 32 are caught.
- Suite: 9808 tests, 9784 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Two in its Badger, undocked:

  | Order | First time | Some seconds later |
  |---|---|---|
  | Approach, 50 m | sent; the ship read FOLLOW | held back |
  | Keep at 5 km | sent; FOLLOW | held back |
  | Orbit at 7.5 km | sent; ORBIT | held back |
  | The same orbit straight behind a stop | sent; ORBIT | |
  | The autopilot's approach | sent | sent |

  The server's log has one `CmdFollowBall … range=50`, one `… range=5000`, one `CmdOrbit …
  range=7500`, then `CmdStop` and the orbit again, then `CmdSetSpeedFraction` and `CmdFollowBall
  … range=0` twice. The flight's ledger counts the same: 4 follows and 2 orbits, of 9 asked for.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 19 identical, 10
  tolerated, 2 moved, 3 divergent, as it was.
- Nothing was staged: the pilot undocked and docked where it was, in the ship it was in.

**Decision taken in the operator's place.**

- **An order is held back only if the pilot's last order was that one, or none.** The client
  goes by its ballpark alone. Its ballpark has not yet heard of a stop sent a moment before, so
  by its source an approach sent straight behind a stop is held back, and the ship is left
  stopped. A person rarely does that inside a second; the page's loops could. So here the
  transport also keeps the pilot's last order, and an order behind a different one is sent.
  That is one call more than the client would make, in a case the client gets wrong. I have not
  seen the client's case in a recording: it is read from its source.

**Not seen working.**

- In the browser. Nothing the page shows is changed by this: an order held back answers as one
  sent does, with the flight as it stands. Nothing in the page reads `alreadySo`.

## 2026-10-09 — what a container lists is kept until something may have changed it, and a claim withdrawn

Commit `12e0aa2`, pushed. Item 26 of the last list, as far as it went.

**A claim withdrawn.** In the last entry's list, and in my word to the operator, I wrote that the
page asks the server for the ship's and the hangar's lists "over and over", from a count: 62
`List` and 32 `ListByFlags` in one flight. Set beside the server's own log, 97 of that flight's
127 listings came within three seconds of the server's notice that an item had changed. The
page reads the holds again when it is told something changed, and a mining laser's cycle is
such a change. That is not asking over and over. The count was right and my reading of it was
not.

**What the client does.** Its inventory cache asks a container for a flag's items once and
from then on goes by the server's `OnItemChange` and `OnItemsChanged`, working each changed
item into what it holds. A whole mining mission recorded on Tranquility has twelve `List`
calls, one for each container and flag; a recording of one mining cycle has none.

**What was built.** On the game port the transport keeps each listing as the server answered
it, by the handle it was asked on and what was asked. Every listing is forgotten when anything
may have changed one: at either notice of an item, in another place or ship, and at any write
of the pilot's own, done or refused. What is forgotten is asked for when it is next wanted. The
gateway's listings are as they were.

**What it changes, which is small.** From the server's logs of two flights, one before and one
after:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| At a login, as the page's windows open | each of two containers listed two or three times at once | each listed once |
| After each notice of an item | two `List` and one `ListByFlags` | the same |

The second row is the difference from the client that is left: it asks nothing there. To match
it the notices have to be worked into what is kept, as its cache does.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 4 of the transport, each watched to fail on the code as it was. 20 ways of breaking
  it were tried, and all 20 are caught.
- Suite: 9812 tests, 9788 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** the staging itself: a ship and three modules given by GM
  command, the ship boarded and the modules fitted, each step reading the hangar after the one
  before. Each reading had what the step before had put there.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** as Test Two in a fitted Venture: undocked, warped to a
  belt, locked a rock and switched on both lasers. The ore hold read 0, 48.3, 72.45, 96.6,
  144.9 and on to 512.25 m³, a cycle at a time. Docked, the station's panel showed the ore in
  the hold; "to Hangar" and "Confirm move" answered "Moved 1 of 1", and the panel then showed
  the hold at 0 and the item hangar with the ore, 512.25 m³ in a stack of 3,415.
- The server's log of that flight: 100 listings, 31 notices of an item, and 4 listings with no
  notice before them, all four at the login.
- **On both transports, by script:** three passes of the parity tool. The first, straight
  after the server was started again, read 18 identical, 10 tolerated, 3 moved, 3 divergent;
  the other two 19, 10, 2 and 3, as it was.
- Staged and undone: the store was copied with the server stopped and put back after. The
  sheet reads 52 skills, 385,914 points and an empty queue again, the ship is the Badger,
  docked where it was, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Kept and forgotten, not kept and worked on.** The client's cache works each changed item
  into what it holds, by rules that differ for a ship, a hangar and a corporation's hangar.
  Getting one of those wrong shows a pilot an inventory that is not so. Forgetting at every
  notice cannot be wrong in that way, and costs a listing where the client asks none. That
  listing is what the page already caused.
- **A "Refresh" in the page no longer reaches the server when nothing has been said to
  change.** If this server ever changed a container without saying so, the page on the game
  port would show the old listing until the next notice of any item, the pilot's next write,
  or its next change of place or ship. The retail client would show the same. I have not seen
  such a case.
- **Any write of the pilot's own forgets the listings**, by the BFF's own list of what is a
  write, but for an order to the engines and a lock. Where I looked, the server's notice of a
  change had come by the time the call that caused it was answered, so there the notices would
  have been enough. This is for a write whose notice the server never sent.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- **The page's "to Hangar" sends `Add` with no quantity.** The client always sends one, the
  stack's size when the whole stack moves. The registry already says so, and the ledger marked
  that one call as differing. It is on the list.
- The dialog for that move said "Move 1 stack · not known to Station hangar?": the stack's
  volume is "not known" there, with the hold's reading of it beside it.
- A listing of everything (`flag=None`) and then of one flag are asked for separately. The
  client's cache counts a flag as listed once it has been given an item with it.
- A container's capacity is asked for each time. The client keeps that too, with rules of its
  own for when to forget it.

## 2026-10-09 — a whole stack is moved with its quantity

Commit `1d77a5e`, pushed. Item 27 of the last list.

**What the client does.** It adds an item to a container with `Add(itemID, sourceLocationID,
qty=, flag=)`, and the quantity is the stack's size when the whole stack moves. Of 22 `Add`
calls read from the recordings, 21 carry a quantity, 3,822 for a hold of ore among them. One
carries `qty=None`; I did not find the path that sends that.

**What the BFF did.** Its three routes that move one item send no quantity for a whole stack.
The registry already said so, and the ledger marked each such call as differing: the last
walk's "to Hangar" was one.

**What it does now.** On the game port the transport fills the quantity in, from the item's
row in a listing the pilot holds (the listings kept since the last entry): the row's stack
size, or its quantity, and 1 for a thing that is one of a kind. A quantity the caller gave is
the caller's. An item in no listing held goes as it came, and is still marked.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 1 of the transport, 1 of the kept answers, and the registry's own widened. All three
  were watched to fail on the code as it was. 19 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 19 are
  caught. Two survived the first pass and each got a case: a stack of nothing, and a move that
  names no item.
- Suite: 9814 tests, 9790 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** as Test Two, docked, with 100 Tritanium given by GM
  command: the item hangar listed "Tritanium 1 m³ · stack 100"; "to Cargo" asked "Move 1 stack
  · 1 m³ to Ship cargo?"; "Confirm move" answered "Moved 1 of 1", and the hangar then read
  "Nothing here but your ships".
- That session's ledger has the one `Add` as reshaped, and nothing differing. The last walk's
  had its `Add` as differing.
- **On both transports, by script:** five passes of the parity tool. Four read 19 identical,
  10 tolerated, 2 moved, 3 divergent, as it was. One read 18, 10, 3 and 3; the third moved
  route was not there on the two passes after it, and I did not capture which it was.
- Staged and undone: the store was copied with the server stopped and put back after. The
  sheet reads 52 skills, 385,914 points and an empty queue again, the ship is the Badger,
  docked where it was, and the copy is deleted.

**Not seen.**

- **The quantity itself on the wire.** The server's log names the item, the source and the
  flag of an `Add` and not its quantity. That 100 went out rests on the transport's test, which
  reads what is sent, and on the ledger counting the live call as reshaped.
- The other two routes that move one item (cargo to and from the hangar by its own route, and
  the ore hold unloaded). They go through the same shaping. The first lists the place itself
  only in a structure, and the second not at all: both go by what the page listed to show the
  item.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- The dialog for a move said "1 m³" for the Tritanium and "not known" for the ore in the last
  walk. The ore's volume was on the page beside it.

## 2026-10-09 — an attribute's value answered from what godma holds

Commit `a1f082a`, pushed. From the fitted ship's walk: the one call in it that the client never
makes.

**What the client does.** It never asks the server for an attribute's value. Its own dogma
location answers, from what `GetAllInfo` brought and each change the server has told of since.

**What the BFF did.** Each time a module still running out its cycle was switched off, it
asked the server `dogmaIM.QueryAttributeValue(itemID, 73)` for how long the cycle is. The
server's log of the two earlier flights has that call once in each, at the afterburner's
switching off.

**What it does now.** On the game port the transport answers from what godma holds of the
item, priming godma first as the client's is primed, and asks the server only for an item, or
an attribute of one, that godma holds nothing of. The gateway's route is as it was.

**Measured first, since the route wants the real cycle and not the type's.** What godma holds
is the server's own figure: for a fitted Venture and its three modules, all 195 attributes
`GetAllInfo` gave were what the server answered for the same items when asked attribute by
attribute (116, 27, 26 and 26, none differing). The same at the pilot's own Badger: 109, none
differing.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the transport and 1 of the registry. The transport's main one and the registry's
  were watched to fail on the code as it was; the third, for a godma that cannot be primed,
  passed there, as it should. 12 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 12 are caught. One
  survived the first pass and got a case: another call that names the same two numbers.
- Suite: 9817 tests, 9793 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** as Test Two in the fitted Venture, undocked: the
  afterburner switched on from the rack, and off three seconds later. The route's answer to
  the switching off had `"stopped":true` and `"cycleMs":8500`, as before, and the Equipment
  window read "Running 8.5s". The server's log of the flight has the `Activate` and the
  `Deactivate`, and no `QueryAttributeValue`.
- That session's ledger has no `QueryAttributeValue` in it. (It has `QueryAllAttributesForItem`
  four times, as the web's alone: those are my own comparison's.)
- **On both transports, by script:** three passes of the parity tool. The first, straight
  after the server was started again, read 18 identical, 10 tolerated, 3 moved, 3 divergent;
  the other two 19, 10, 2 and 3, as it was.
- Staged and undone: the store was copied with the server stopped and put back after. The
  sheet reads 52 skills, 385,914 points and an empty queue again, the ship is the Badger,

## 2026-10-09 — the parity tool's "moved" and "divergent" made to mean what they say

Commit `37e34f7`, pushed. Items 30 and 31 of the last list, and two of the three routes the tool
has called divergent all along.

**Which route it was.** Six passes with each pass's "moved" lines kept: the route that now and
then read "moved" is `/api/bridge/contracts`, by `searchTime`, 0 on one transport and 10000 on
the other. That is how long the server took over the search, which it answers beside what it
found. The two routes that read "moved" on every pass, skills and planets, both did so by
`serverNowMs`: the server's own clock at the read, a second apart because the two reads are.

None of the three is data that moved. The tool already leaves out fields that differ on every
request by design, and these two are now among them.

**The two "divergent" routes that were not.** The journal and industry read "divergent" for a
tuple spelt two ways: the gateway hands on the server's own `{type:"tuple"}` where the server
built one, and the game port has every tuple off the wire as an array. The tool is right that
no shared reader takes both. But the page's reader for each of those two places does
(`decodeJournal` and `decodeJournalRow`; `decodeFacilities`). The tool now knows those two places, by route and by where in the answer, and
calls a tuple spelt two ways there tolerated. Anywhere else it is divergent still.

**What a pass reads now.**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| identical | 19, now and then 18 | 21 |
| tolerated | 10 | 12 |
| moved | 2, now and then 3 | none |
| divergent | 3 | 1 |

The one left is the corporation's members route, which does differ in shape between the two
transports. It was on the list and still is.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the tool, each watched to fail on the code as it was. The page's reader of a
  facility is now given the game port's spelling in its own test (it was given the gateway's
  alone; the journal's reader had both). 14 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 14 are
  caught. Three more, of the two patterns, were not tried the first time: a shell had halved
  the backslashes in what they looked for. The sources were as they were, and they went in
  again from a file.
- Suite: 9819 tests, 9795 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. The page builds.
- **On both transports, live:** three passes with the tool as it is now, each 21 identical, 12
  tolerated, 1 divergent. The journal reads "tolerated, tuple-read-either-way ×2" and industry
  "tolerated, tuple-read-either-way ×9".
- Nothing was staged.

**Decision taken in the operator's place.**

- **A tool's verdict was changed, not what it measures.** Nothing the two transports answer is
  different for this. What changed is which differences the tool counts as which. Each change
  is held to one thing: two field names for the clock and the search's time, and two places in
  two routes for the tuple, each with the reader that takes it named beside it and a test of
  that reader. A tuple spelt two ways anywhere else still fails a pass.

**Still as it was.**

- A read that takes what it reads (`GetSkillChangesForISIS`) would read "moved" for whichever
  transport asks second, when there is something to take. And the first route of a pass can
  carry a notice from login. Neither was seen in these passes.

## 2026-10-09 — the members route's one real difference, and a clean pass of the parity tool

Commit `e106f8d`, pushed. Item 11 of the last list.

**What the difference was.** The corporation's members route was the last the parity tool
called divergent. Set side by side, its two answers differ in shape in one cell of each row:
`blockRoles`, `0` through the gateway and `false` on the game port. The row's own descriptor
says the column is a BOOL. The wire carries a bit there, and the game port has it as the
boolean it is; the gateway prints the server's own value for the column. So the game port's is
what the retail client is given, and neither transport is wrong about the member.

The rest of what the last list said of this route was already taken care of: the gateway's
cached-call wrapper is opened by the tool as the page opens it, and a 64-bit column spelt as a
string or a number is a spelling the page's shared reader takes.

**What was done.** The comparison takes a BOOL column of a packed row, spelt as a boolean on
one side and as 0 or 1 on the other, for one value in two spellings, and says so too if the two
are not the same boolean. Any other column, any other number, and anything outside a packed row
are as they were. The page has a shared reader for it, `unwrapBool`, beside `unwrapLong` and
`unwrapReal`.

**A pass now reads 21 identical, 13 tolerated: nothing moved, nothing divergent, and the tool
exits 0.** The members route still prints two
`moved?` lines, for the pilot's own logon time in the corporation's tracking, which each pass
sets by logging the pilot on.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 1 of the comparison and 1 of the page's reader, each watched to fail on the code as
  it was. 15 ways of breaking them were tried, and all 15 are caught. One survived the first
  pass and got a case: nothing on one side and a boolean on the other.
- Suite: 9821 tests, 9797 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. The page builds.
- **On both transports, live:** three passes, each 21 identical, 13 tolerated, and a fourth
  for the tool's exit, which was 0. The members route reads "tolerated: long-form ×28, bare-bigint-string ×20, bool-form ×2, value ×2".
- Nothing was staged.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The tool was taught the spelling, and neither transport was changed.** The gateway could
  be made to print `false`, or the game port `0`. The first is the old transport, which this
  loop leaves as it is; the second would make the new one say something other than the wire.
- **`unwrapBool` has no reader using it yet.** No window of the page reads the members route.
  It is there, with its test, so that the tool's "a shared reader takes either" is true the
  day one does.

**Not done.**

- `docs/game-port-parity-report.md`, the report of raw calls, uses the same comparison. It was
  not made again.

## 2026-10-09 — the formations asked for once, and the report of raw calls made again

Commits `4bb760d` and `3577410`, pushed. From item 11 of the last list, and the small ones around the walk.

**The report of raw calls** (`docs/game-port-parity-report.md`) was made again, as Test Pilot.
It reads 138 identical, 14 tolerated, 4 divergent, 15 refused alike, 4 moved, of 175 compared.
Yesterday's read 139, 14, 4, 15 and 4 of 176. The comparison's new knowledge of a BOOL column
changed nothing in it: none of these reads has one that differs. What changed is the BFF's
own list of calls, which the harness reads from its source: `account.GetJournal` and
`charMgr.GetHomeStation` were among the reads it could make and are now among those it
cannot, and `skillHandler.GetImplants` went the other way. Its four divergent reads are the two tuples the page's readers
take either way (the journal, the facilities) and two of the proving grounds' events, whose
dates are bytes spelt two ways. Nothing in the page reads those dates.

**The formations.** `michelle.AddBallpark` asks `beyonce.GetFormations()` each time it makes a
ballpark, and the client's object cache answers every asking after the first: a Tranquility
recording of a flight through several systems has "returning a cached result" at each ballpark
it adds. So the server is asked once.

On the game port each ballpark asked the server for itself, and the BFF's own route asked again
whenever the page wanted them. The 17:00 hour of this server's log has nine askings for four
ballparks. Now the first asking is sent, counted in the ledger as the client's own, and kept
for the pilot. A ballpark made later, and the BFF's route, are answered from it. An asking that
fails is not kept. The gateway's route is as it was.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 3 of the transport, and the older one that asked for the formations through the BFF
  now reads the park's own asking in the ledger. 8 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 8
  are caught; the first two put each half back as it was. One survived the first pass and got
  a case: another call of the same service, by name.
- Suite: 9824 tests, 9800 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Two: undocked, the BFF asked for the formations
  twice; docked, asked once; undocked again, asked once more; docked. Each answer had the same
  two formations. The server's log of it has two ballparks bound and one `GetFormations`. The
  ledger has it once, as the client's own.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 21 identical, 13
  tolerated.
- Nothing was staged: the pilot undocked and docked where it was, in the ship it was in.

**Not watched to fail the usual way.** My first run of the new tests failed for a name the test
file did not have, not for the code. What shows they can fail is the breakages: with either
half put back as it was, they do.

**Seen and not repaired.**

- **This is one cached method call kept by hand.** The client's object cache does the same for
  every call the server marks as cached. The transport has no such cache of its own: each
  thing kept so far has its own keeping. It is on the list.

## 2026-10-09 — the session keeps cached method calls, as the client's object cache does

Commit `267c82c`, pushed. The item added by the last entry: the object cache as a thing of the
transport's own.

**What the client does.** Where the server answers a service's method with a
`CachedMethodCallResult`, the client's object cache keeps the answer, for as long as the
answer's own details say: never checked again, checked always, good for the run, good for a
time, or good until midnight. Its log says "returning a cached result" where the cache
answered. Across the Tranquility recordings that is seventeen methods, the mission messages 800
times and the formations 43. The server tells the client when an answer has changed, by
calling one of two methods on it.

**What the session did.** It opened such an answer and kept nothing: every call was sent. The
server's two calls were answered and nothing was done for them.

**What it does now.** It keeps and answers as the client does, for a call by a service's name
or to the proxy's node, and forgets what the server names in either call. The transport does
not count a call the cache answered, since none is sent. This server marks some three dozen
methods as cached.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 5 of the session and 1 of the transport, each watched to fail on the code as it was.
  33 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 33 are caught. Three survived the first pass:
  one because a test's helper had hidden the case it was for, and two that got a case each.
- Suite: 9830 tests, 9806 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, the same thing before and after:** thirteen of a docked
  pilot's routes read twice in one session, and the server's log counted for each reading.

  | | First reading | Second reading |
  |---|---|---|
  | Before | 31 calls | 29 |
  | After | 31 | 26 |

  The three the cache answered the second time: `account.GetEntryTypes`,
  `marketProxy.GetCharOrders` and `marketProxy.GetMarketOrderHistory`. (The two fewer that both
  have are a bind and the implants, kept by other means.)
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, both 21 identical, 13
  tolerated.
- Nothing was staged.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **On the game port the page now shows some things as old as the client would.** A pilot's
  own market orders and the market's history are good for as long as this server says, minutes
  at a time, as on the retail client. Through the gateway they are asked each time, as before.
- **One of the pilot's own writes forgets every answer kept.** The client's own code names the
  cached calls a write of its changes, and the server names the rest. I have not read every
  write of the client's for what it names. Forgetting everything asks again for what had not
  changed and never answers with what had. An order to the engines and a lock forget nothing,
  as with the listings.
- **An answer due a check with the server is asked for afresh.** The client sends the call
  with the version it holds and may be told its copy is good. This server can answer so. It is
  the next piece, and on the list.

**Not done.**

- A bound object's cached answers are not kept. The client keeps those too.
- The server may name several cached calls at once by a part of their arguments. Only a whole
  match is forgotten.
- The formations are still kept by hand as well. With the real session the cache has them.
- No live check of the server's two calls. This server makes one of them of a client in one
  place, after a change to saved fittings. I did not exercise it; the tests give the session
  the call as the server would frame it.

## 2026-10-09 — a cached answer due a check is asked for with the version held, and CacheOK is taken for it

Commits `bc4f95d` (the check) and `de87769` (the parity tool), pushed. The first piece of item 8
of the last list: the object cache's check with the server.

**What the client does.** When an answer it holds is due a check, the client sends the call all
the same, with the version it holds where every other call carries a `1`:
`machoVersion=[when, checksum]`. The server answers with a new answer, which is kept in place
of the old one, or with the exception `CacheOK`. Then the copy held is the answer, and it is
good from that moment. An answer held inline has a version of its own. An answer that is a
reference to a cached object has none, and its version is the object's.

I looked in every folder of the Tranquility recordings first. The client made 64 such checks
there and the server answered 61 of them `CacheOK`:

| Service | Checks | Answered `CacheOK` |
|---|---|---|
| `shipKillCounter` | 27 | 25 |
| `structureDirectory` | 25 | 24 |
| `standingMgr` | 7 | 7 |
| `fwWarzoneSolarsystem` | 2 | 2 |
| `agentMgr` | 2 | 2 |
| `map` | 1 | 1 |

Tranquility answers so for a reference too: the warzones' states came first as a reference with
no version of its own, the check went out with the object's stamp and checksum, and `CacheOK`
came back.

**What the session did.** An answer due a check was asked for afresh, with a `1`.

**What it does now.** It makes the check as above, and keeps no answer it has no version for.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 5 of the session, each watched to fail. One is on the server's own recorded bytes of
  an answer that is a reference. 15 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 15 are caught.
- Suite: 9835 tests, 9811 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on a game-port session of its own whose clock the script moves:**

  | Call | Good for | Inside that time | Past it, before the server's fix | Past it, after |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `standingMgr.GetStandingCompositions`, held inline | 5 minutes | at 4 minutes, nothing sent | at 6, sent with the version; `CacheOK`; nothing sent after | the same |
  | `corporationSvc.GetAllCorpMedals`, a reference | 1 hour | at 59 minutes, nothing sent | at 61, sent with the object's version; a whole new answer of the same checksum | at 61, sent with the object's version; `CacheOK`; nothing sent after |

  The answer was the same at every asking in each run.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool after the game-port BFF was
  restarted on this code, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated. See below for the pass before them.
- Nothing was staged. The script selects Test Pilot on a session of its own and logs it off.

**A server defect, fixed by a sub-agent** (eve.js `342a366a6`, on its local `main`, not pushed).
EveJS answered the check of an answer that is a reference with a whole new answer, where
Tranquility answers `CacheOK`. It compared the version sent against the result's own version,
and a reference has none. Six of the server's services build answers so, the formations and the
corporation's medals among them. The fix reads the version as the client's shared code does (`CachedMethodCallResult.GetVersion`):
the object's, for a reference. The sub-agent wrote six tests and saw four of them fail before
the fix. I read the diff, ran its tests, restarted the server and ran the script above again:
the last column of the table.

**My first build had the same mistake from the other side.** It read the result's own version,
and for a reference sent `[0, None]` at the very next asking. Every test passed, each on an
answer I had made up with a version of its own. Recording the frames again from the real server
(`scripts/capture-game-frames.js`) showed it: the second asking of the medals went out, where
nothing should have been sent.

**A claim of mine put right.** The reference said the client's cache answered
`GetItemKillCountPlayer` 61 times across the recordings, the warzones' states 55 and the
structures' map 42. Those counted two kinds of line as one. Answered outright they are 34, 53
and 17; the rest were checks with the server. The reference now has both counts.

**A defect of the parity tool, found on the way.** The first pass after the BFF's restart read
"20 identical, 13 tolerated, 1 moved", and I had printed its last line only. I restarted the BFF
and ran it again with the whole output kept: the contracts route, on `searchTime`, the server's
own measure of how long a search took. The tool was meant to leave that out since two entries
ago, and did not. The server's answer has it as a dict's entry, and my test of the leaving-out
had it as an object's own field, a shape no answer has. The test now uses the shape both BFFs
answered, printed off them; it failed with "moved" on the tool as it was. 7 ways of breaking
the fix were tried and all 7 are caught, one after a case was added for it. The two passes
above were the first two after another restart. Before the fix two of two first passes had
shown it. The brief has the lesson.

**Found for the next piece.** The client's object cache has a function for forgetting several
calls by a part of their arguments (`__ListPartialMatch`), and nothing in the client calls it.
So that is off the list. What the client's own code does name is some sixty-five places, most
of them on a notice from the server: `OnOwnOrdersChanged` forgets seven of the market's calls,
`OnCorporationMedalAdded` and `OnMedalIssued` the medals'.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **EveJS was restarted to take the fix.** The store was not changed.
- **The recorded frames were made again, twice,** with their own script, once on the first
  build and once on the corrected one. The second is what is committed.
- **The sub-agent's test runner swept its own stale temp stores.** It removed 171 directories
  from the machine's Temp folder, each untouched for more than a day, 0.4 MB in all. Some were
  named `evejs-web-*`. Nothing of this loop's scratch was among them.

**Not done.**

- A bound object's cached answers are not kept.
- One of the pilot's own writes still forgets every answer kept. The client names them.
- The formations are still kept by hand as well.
- No live check of the server telling the client to forget an answer.

## 2026-10-09 — a cached answer is forgotten when the client's own code would name it, and an order can be taken down on the game port

Commits `ee2dfb7` (the order's number) and `b69495a` (the names), pushed. The first piece of
item 8 of the last list.

**What the client does.** Some cached answers are good for the whole run: this server answers a
pilot's own market orders so. What makes the client ask again is a name, from the server or
from the client's own code, which names cached calls at 62 places. I read them all. They are
of three kinds: on a notice from the server (the pilot's orders changed, a medal, asset
safety, a station, a kill right, a calendar event), on a change to the session (another
corporation, a militia), and beside one of its own calls. The reference has the tables.

The Tranquility recordings have no order taken down or repriced, no notice of a pilot's orders
changing, and no line of the client's cache being told to forget: I looked in every folder.
This is built from the client's code.

**What the transport did.** One of the pilot's own writes forgot every answer the session's
cache held. That asked again for what no client would, and it hid a real fault: nothing but
the forgetting made a pilot's orders fresh after a buy.

**What it does now.** It names what the client's code names, when it names it
(`cachedCallsNamed.js`): seventeen notices, two changes to the session, and the six such calls
the BFF can make. A write names nothing else. What a container lists is still forgotten at a
write, as before.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 12 of the table, 4 of the transport (one in place of the old one), and one of the
  session's made longer for the key. The transport's four and the session's were watched to
  fail on the code as it was. The table's passed at once, being new, so the breakages are what
  show they can fail.
- 54 ways of breaking it were tried and all 54 are caught. Three survived the first pass and
  were code that did nothing, which is taken out.
- Suite: 9852 tests, 9828 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, the same walk before and after,** as Test Pilot at Jita, with
  the server's log counted between steps. The market's three cached calls are the type's book,
  the pilot's orders and the order history.

  | Step | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | The market read twice | all three sent, then none | the same |
  | A buy order placed; the route reads the pilot's orders at once | sent, and the order is in it | the same: the notice had named it |
  | The market read again | the book and the history sent | the same, each named by the notice |
  | A write the client names nothing beside (`/giveitem`), and the market read again | all three sent | none sent |
  | The order taken down | refused | done; the pilot's orders sent, and the order gone from them |

- **In the browser, on the game port:** the page's Market window. Tritanium found, an offer to
  buy one at 0.01 ISK placed: "That went through. You were actually charged 100.01 ISK." "Your
  orders" listed it open, 1 of 1, at once. "Take it down…": "That went through. 0.01 ISK was
  returned to your wallet." and "You have no orders open right now.", with the order among
  those finished.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the
  first after a restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**A defect of the game port's, found by the walk and fixed** (`ee2dfb7`). No order could be
taken down on the game port. The BFF's route has the order's ID as the text the page sent. On
the wire that was a string, and the server read a string as order 0: "order 0 not found", told
to the pilot as the market being offline. Repricing sent the ID the same way. The registry now
has both calls and sends the number, as the client has it off the order's row. 9 ways of
breaking that were tried and all are caught, one after a case was added. It is still not the
client's call in two things the server does not read, and the ledger notes both: the route
names no region for a take-down, and sends nought for a repriced order's date of issue.

**A long is one number to the cache however it is spelt.** The BFF spells a long as
`{type: "long", value: "5"}`, the wire as a number. A call made with the one and a name given
with the other made two keys, so the name would have forgotten nothing. Found by a test of the
transport, before anything live.

**Two things of the server's, not fixed, for the operator.**

- **The market daemon that is running is older than its source.** It refuses an order at Test
  Two's station: "station 60000004 does not exist in market database". A commit of 2026-10-06
  in `eve.js` (`8dd49cbec`, not mine) allows orders at stations the seed leaves out, and the
  binary on disk is from August. I did not rebuild or restart it: it is not this loop's
  process. So the market was checked as Test Pilot at Jita.
- **A refusal for that reason reads "Market is currently offline"** to the pilot. The server's
  own log has the cause.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Three cancelled orders of Test Pilot's are left in the market daemon's own database**
  (1129, 1130 and one more, each a buy of one Tritanium at 0.01 ISK, each taken down). The
  store was put back, and the daemon's database is not part of it. To take them out I would
  have had to stop a process I did not start.
- **On the game port the page now shows what the client's cache would.** After a write the
  client names nothing beside, an answer the server marked as good for a time is not asked for
  again until then. Before, every write asked again for everything.
- **Rows are left out of the table where the BFF cannot make the call.** The file lists them
  and why.

**Not done.**

- The names that need an item's owner, flag and station (four callers), the names given on a
  refusal, and the names that hang on what a window holds.
- A bound object's cached answers are not kept.
- The formations are still kept by hand as well.
- No live check of the server telling the client to forget an answer.
- An order's take-down and reprice are not yet shaped from the order's own row.

## 2026-10-09 — an order is taken down and repriced with what its own row has

Commit `182fb22`, pushed. The first piece of item 9 of the last list.

**What the client does.** It takes an order down with the order's ID and the region it is in,
and reprices one with nine arguments, all but the new price off the order. The order is a row
of the pilot's own orders, which its object cache keeps.

The Tranquility recordings have none of the market's order calls: I looked in every folder.
The only market calls there are the wallet's. So this is built from the client's code, and
the calls were made first as the client makes them, on a session of a script's own, to see
this server take them. It did: None to each, the price changed, and the notices said
"Modified" and "Cancelled".

**What the transport did.** It sent what the BFF's routes gave it: nought for the region, a bool
for the side, where the pilot is for the station, and nought for the date of issue. The server
reads only the order and the new price, so both calls worked and neither was the client's.

**What it does now.** It reads the order's row out of the pilot's orders the session keeps and
sends what the client sends, each value as it came off the wire. Where the session keeps no
orders it asks for them first, as the client has them before it touches one. An order in no
such list goes out as it came, and the ledger says it differs.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 3 of the registry and 2 of the transport, each watched to fail on the code as it was.
  The transport's use the server's own list in shape and in kinds of value, read off a
  game-port session: the names some text and some bytes, the ID and the date longs.
- 32 ways of breaking it were tried and all 32 are caught. Three survived the first pass: two
  got a case each, and one was code that did nothing, which is taken out.
- Suite: 9857 tests, 9833 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, the same walk before and after,** as Test Pilot at Jita: a buy
  order placed, repriced from 0.01 to 0.02 ISK, taken down, with the pilot's orders read after
  each. The walk reads the same both times. The call ledger does not:

  | Call | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `marketProxy.CancelCharOrder` | differs | reshaped |
  | `marketProxy.ModifyCharOrder` | differs | reshaped |
  | `marketProxy.GetOrders` | unchecked | same |
  | `marketProxy.GetNewPriceHistory` | unchecked | differs |
  | `marketProxy.PlaceBuyOrder` | unchecked | differs |
  | `marketProxy.GetCharOrders` | 4 calls | 4 calls |

  No asking was added: the orders were kept each time one was touched.
- **In the browser, on the game port:** the page's Market window. An offer to buy placed, "Your
  orders", "Change the price…" to 0.02: "That went through. You were actually charged 100.01
  ISK." and the order listed at 0.02 ISK at once. Then taken down: "That went through. 0.02 ISK
  was returned to your wallet." and no orders open.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the
  first after a restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**The last two rows of that table are news, not faults fixed.** Both calls had never been set
beside the client. A type's price history is asked by the client in two halves and by the
BFF's route in one. A buy order goes out without the broker's fee the client's window names.
Both are on the list.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Four more cancelled orders of Test Pilot's are left in the market daemon's own database**,
  seven with the last entry's three. Each was a buy of one Tritanium at 0.01 or 0.02 ISK, each
  taken down. The store was put back; the daemon's database is not part of it.
- **The transport may ask for the pilot's orders before an order is touched.** One call the
  BFF's route did not make, where the session keeps none. The client has made it by then.

**Not done.**

- Selling, buying several and the plex orders are not tried on the game port.
- A buy order's fee, and the history's other half.
