## 2026-10-09 — a sale's items go out as the client's, so that something can be sold on the game port

Commit `67cbb13`, pushed. The next piece of item 9 of the last list: selling.

**What the walk found.** Nothing could be sold on the game port. The BFF's route gives a sale's
item as a plain object. Through the gateway that is handed on as it is. The wire has no such
value, and the sale was refused: "marketProxy.PlaceMultiSellOrder was given an argument that
cannot be sent: Cannot marshal value".

**What the client does.** Its sale window makes each item a `util.KeyVal` with eight keywords
(`sellMulti.py` 501), and sends them in a list with whether it is for the corporation, for how
long, and the broker's fee rate the window showed, or None for a sale at once. The recordings
have none of this: I looked in every folder for the market's order calls last entry, and for
a KeyVal the client wrote this time. So it is built from the client's code.

**What the transport does now.** The registry has the call and makes each item the client's
KeyVal, in a list.

**The order of a KeyVal's fields.** They go to the wire in the order the client's Python keeps
the keywords, which is not the order written, and not the order a plain function would have
them in either. I asked the client's own Python (the oracle the fixture is built with): for
the sale's eight it answers `itemID, typeID, rawBrokerFeePercentage, price, officeID,
stationID, delta, quantity`. The model in `py27.js` had the pieces for it. It now has the
function, and the fixture's builder asks the oracle for this case with every keyword set it
has: all 409 agree.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 3 of the registry, 1 of the session on the real marshal, and 1 of the order against
  the client's Python. The registry's and the session's were watched to fail on the code as
  it was; the order's failed for want of the function. The session's shows both halves: the
  route's plain object is refused by the marshal, and the shaped call is read back off the
  wire as a list of `util.KeyVal` with its fields in the oracle's order.
- 26 ways of breaking it were tried and all 26 are caught.
- Suite: 9862 tests, 9838 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, the same walk before and after,** as Test Pilot at Jita: ten
  Tritanium given, one of the stack offered for sale at a price nobody pays, for a day.

  | Step | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | The sale | 400, "cannot be sent" | done; charged 29,215.11 ISK |
  | The pilot's orders | none | the order, selling, 1 left |
  | The order taken down | | done; a stack of one back in the hangar |

- **In the browser, on the game port:** the page's Market window. "Offer to sell…" one of 19 at
  987,654.32 ISK for a day: "That went through. You were actually charged 29,215.11 ISK."
  "Your orders" listed it open, selling, 1 of 1. Taken down: "That went through. Nothing was
  taken from your wallet." and no orders open.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the
  first after a restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**Not the client's call yet, and the ledger says so.** Two of the item's eight fields the
client's window works out: how far the price is from the type's average (`delta`) and the
broker's fee rate (`rawBrokerFeePercentage`). A route has neither, and I did not make them up:
the item goes out with six, and the call reads "differs". So does an order that stands with no
fee rate named. The server reads neither. Working out the fee rate as the client does is the
same job as a buy order's ninth argument, and is on the list.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Two more cancelled orders of Test Pilot's are left in the market daemon's own database**,
  nine in all: each a sale of one Tritanium, each taken down.
- **The fixture of the client's Python was built again,** with its own script, to add the new
  case. It gained three keyword sets (406 to 409) and a `constructed` answer for each.

**Not done.**

- The broker's fee rate, for a buy order and for a sale.
- Buying several, and the plex orders, are not tried on the game port.
- A type's price history in both halves.

## 2026-10-09 — an order names the broker's fee rate, worked out as the client works it out

Commit `5c30a0f`, pushed. The next piece of item 9 of the last list.

**What the client does.** It names the broker's fee rate when it places an order: a buy
order's ninth argument, a sale's fourth for an order that stands, and a field of each item of
a sale. It works the rate out itself, from the pilot's Broker Relations and the standings the
station's owner and that owner's faction have to the pilot. The server works it out too, and
refuses an order whose named rate is not its own. The recordings have no order placed, so
this is from the client's code.

**What the BFF's routes did.** They named no rate, since they could not know it. The server
takes an order with none named.

**What the transport does now.** It works the rate out from what it keeps (the skill's level
in effect, the two standings, and the station's owner and its faction from the game's static
data) and the registry names it. Where it cannot be worked out, none is named, as before.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the sums, 2 of the registry and 2 of the transport. The registry's and the
  transport's were watched to fail on the code as it was. The sums are held to the client's
  own Python, to the last digit, over 105 cases: I had the oracle do the same sums in the
  same order and kept its answers.
- 38 ways of breaking it were tried and all 38 are caught. Five survived the first pass. Three
  got a case each. One was a check that did nothing a later check did not, and the two were
  made one. One was not a breakage: the skill's part of the sum is the same number either way
  round for every level there is, which I checked for all six.
- Suite: 9868 tests, 9844 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **The server asked first.** On a session of a script's own, a buy order naming a rate that
  was plainly wrong (0.5) was refused, `MktBrokersFeeUnexpected2`, and the server said its own:
  2.96 percent. The rate worked out for Test Pilot at Jita is 0.0295803: no Broker Relations,
  the owner's faction at 1.399 to the pilot, the owner at nothing. The last entry's sale was
  charged 29,215.11 ISK on 987,654.32, which is that rate.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Pilot at Jita: a buy order placed, repriced and
  taken down, and one Tritanium offered for sale and taken down, each with the rate named.
  All taken. In the call ledger:

  | Call | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `marketProxy.PlaceBuyOrder` | differs | reshaped |
  | `marketProxy.PlaceMultiSellOrder` | differs, for two fields and the fee | differs, for one field |

- **In the browser, on the game port:** the page's Market window. An offer to buy placed:
  "That went through. You were actually charged 100.01 ISK." Listed open at once, and taken
  down: "That went through. 0.01 ISK was returned to your wallet."
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the
  first after a restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **An order on the game port can now be refused for its fee rate where it could not before.**
  If the rate worked out here were ever not the server's, the server would refuse the order
  and say so, as it does to the retail client. Through the gateway no rate is named still.
- **Five more cancelled orders of Test Pilot's are left in the market daemon's own database**,
  fourteen in all.

**Not done.**

- A structure's rate. The client asks the server for a structure's base
  (`structureSettings.CharacterGetService`), and no skill applies there.
- A system the militias have upgraded: the client lowers the rate by a tenth a level there
  and asks the war's manager for the level. This server does not lower its own rate for it.
- A sale item's `delta`, from the type's average price.
- The page still shows the fee as an estimate at the base rate and says it cannot see the
  pilot's skills or standings. The BFF now can.

## 2026-10-09 — the page shows the broker's fee the pilot will pay

Commit `36447f9`, pushed. A piece of item 9 of the last list.

**What the page did.** The Market window's order form showed the broker's fee as an estimate at
the base rate of 3 percent, and said the app could not see the pilot's trading skills or its
standing with the station's owner. Since the last entry the transport can.

**What it does now.** The Market read says the rate for the station the pilot is docked at. On
the game port the transport works it out as the client does; through the gateway nothing
does, and the read says none. With a rate the order form works the fee out at it, with the
same floor, heads it "Broker's fee" and says what it was worked out from and at what
percentage. With none it shows the estimate and its warning, as before.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 1 of the transport, 2 of the BFF's route, 1 of the parity tool, 2 of the fee and its
  words, and 1 of the page's flow. All but the last were watched to fail on the code as it
  was; the last passed when it was written, the code being there by then.
- 25 ways of breaking it were tried, from the BFF's route to the page's store, and all 25 are
  caught.
- The page's source type-checks and builds.
- Suite: 9875 tests, 9851 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** as Test Pilot at Jita: an offer to buy 1000 Tritanium
  at 50 ISK. The form showed "Broker's fee 1,479.02 ISK" and "worked out at your own rate,
  2.96%, from your Broker Relations skill and how this station's owner regards you". The
  estimate would have been 1,500.00. Placed: "That went through. You were actually charged
  51,479.02 ISK.", which is the 50,000.00 set aside and that fee. Taken down: "50,000.00 ISK
  was returned to your wallet."
- **By script, on both transports:** the Market read says 0.0295803 on the game port and none
  through the gateway. Two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the first after a
  restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated: the Market read was tolerated already, and has the
  rate beside what it had.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The gateway BFF was restarted on this code.** It had run older code since early in the
  session, and said nothing of a rate where it now says none.
- **Through the gateway the page shows the estimate still.** The rate could be worked out
  there too, from two more reads. I left the gateway's routes as they are.
- **One more cancelled order of Test Pilot's is left in the market daemon's own database**,
  fifteen in all.

**Not done.**

- The fee shown for a repriced order. The client's window shows it, with the discount the
  Margin Trading skill gives (`skilllimits.py` 35). The page says only that there is a fee.
- The sales tax, which the client's sale window shows beside the fee.

## 2026-10-09 — a type's price history is asked in both halves and joined as the client joins them

Commit `87a6305`, pushed. A piece of item 9 of the last list.

**What I found.** The page's price history for a type was one row. The client asks a history
in two halves, an old one and a new one, and joins them. The BFF's Market read asked the new
half alone. On this server the new half is the last day and nothing else: the server puts
every day but the last in the old half.

**What the client does.** `GetOldPriceHistory(typeID)`, then `GetNewPriceHistory(typeID)`, then
`GetHistoryRowList`: the old half's days in order; a day with no trade between two of them
filled in at the average of the day before; the same from the last of the old half up to
yesterday; then the new half as it came, or a row for now where there is none. The
recordings have no price history asked. This is from the client's code.

**What is done.** The Market read asks both halves and hands both on. That is in the BFF's
route, so on both transports. The page joins them as the client does, oddities and all: a
filled day has 2 for the quantity and 2 for the orders, nothing is filled in before the first
day, and the new half goes last whatever its days are.

**Two more things the walk showed, both fixed.**

- **Every day of the history was named a day early.** A history's day begins at midnight by
  the game's clock, which is UTC. The page named it by the reader's own calendar, and here
  that midnight is the evening before.
- **The table would have stopped the page.** It was keyed by a row's day. The joined history
  can have a day twice, as it has on this server, and a keyed list with a key twice is an
  error the page does not recover from. It is keyed by a row's place now. I saw this before
  it happened, from the data, and did not let it.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the BFF's route, 4 of the join and the day's name, 1 of the page's flow, and the
  registry's changed for the two halves. All were watched to fail on the code as it was.
- 34 ways of breaking it were tried and all 34 are caught.
- The page's source type-checks and builds.
- Suite: 9882 tests, 9858 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on both transports:** for Tritanium at Jita the read hands on 29 days in the old
  half and 1 in the new. In the call ledger both halves read "same"; the new half read
  "differs" before, for being asked alone. Two passes of the parity tool, both 21 identical,
  13 tolerated.
- **In the browser, on the game port:**

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Rows of the type's price history | 1, by what the read handed on | 61 |
  | The new half's day | 9/7/2026, by the reader's calendar | 9/8/2026, by the game's |

  The "before" row count is from the read, which had the new half alone: I did not open the
  page before the change. The day's name before is from the page, on the first build of this,
  which still named days by the reader's calendar.

  The 61 are the old half's 29 days, then 31 days carried at 100.00 ISK from 8 September to
  yesterday, then the new half's day, 8 September, last. That is what the client's own join
  makes of what this server answers.
- Nothing was staged. Both BFFs were restarted on this code.

**For the operator: the market's history stops a month ago.** The daemon's last day for
Tritanium is 8 September, the day its seed was built, I take it. So a month of days is filled
in at the last average, in the page as it would be in the retail client. I did not look for
whether the daemon is meant to add days as time passes.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The gateway's route changed with the game port's.** One read more for a type's history,
  through either. The fault was the route's own, and the page was wrong through both.
- **The page shows the filled-in days as the client's list would,** with 2 for what was
  traded. I did not mark them as filled in.
- **A history's day is named in UTC; the page's other dates are not changed.** An order's date
  and a trade's are still by the reader's calendar. The game shows all of them by its own.

**Not done.**

- A sale item's `delta`, which is worked out from this history.
- The page's other dates in the game's time.

## 2026-10-09 — a sale's item carries how far its price is from the type's average, and the sale is the client's call

Commit `81a5ab4`, pushed. A piece of item 9 of the last list.

**What the client does.** Its sale item has eight fields. The one still missing here was how far
the price is from the type's average over a week. The entry of the client's sale window asks
the market for that average when it is made: the two halves of the type's price history,
joined as the last entry has it, and of the rows no older than a week the sum of average
times quantity over the sum of quantity. With nothing traded in the week it is the type's base
price over its portion size. It is rounded to the hundredth.

**What the transport does now.** A sale asks for the two halves for each of its items that has
no such figure of its own, as each entry of the client's asks, and works the figure out. The
item goes out with all eight fields, and with the fee named the sale is the client's call.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 4 of the sums, 1 of the registry and 3 of the transport. The registry's and one of
  the transport's were watched to fail on the code as it was. The other two of the transport's
  passed when written: one is for what must not change, and one was added for a breakage that
  had survived. The sums are held to the client's own
  Python over ten made-up histories, to the last digit: I had it do the same sums in the same
  order, and kept its answers with the histories it was given.
- 41 ways of breaking it were tried and all 41 are caught. Five survived the first pass. Two
  were checks made twice, now made once. Three got a case each: one after I had written the
  case wrongly and seen it fail for that, and one where the source also had a line doing the
  same job twice, which is gone.
- Suite: 9890 tests, 9866 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Pilot at Jita: one Tritanium offered for sale, and
  taken down. The server's own log has, in order, `GetOldPriceHistory`, `GetNewPriceHistory`
  and then `PlaceMultiSellOrder`, and the sale was taken. In the call ledger:

  | Call | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `marketProxy.PlaceMultiSellOrder` | differs, for one field | reshaped |
  | The walk's whole ledger | 1 pair differs | none differs, none unchecked: 31 the same, 6 reshaped |

- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the
  first after a restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not in the browser.** Nothing the page shows changes with this. The page's sale was seen
  there four entries ago, through the same route.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A sale on the game port makes two calls more than the BFF's route asked for**, for each
  item: the two halves of the history. The client makes them when its entry is made, before
  the sale. Here they are made as the sale goes.
- **One more cancelled order of Test Pilot's is left in the market daemon's own database**,
  sixteen in all.

**Not done.**

- The page does not show the average, nor how far the price is from it. The client's sale
  window shows both.
- The server reads neither the average nor the delta, so nothing here says the figure is the
  one Tranquility would want. It is the client's sum, held to the client's Python.

## 2026-10-09 — a saved fitting is applied as the client applies it, so that one can be applied at all

Commit `4ab196e`, pushed. Not an item of the last list: found by looking for the fault the sale
had, somewhere else.

**How it was found.** A sale could not be made on the game port because the BFF's route gave
an item as a plain object, and the wire has no such value. I looked for other routes that hand
a plain object on. One writes it out at the call, the sale, which is done. Eleven take one,
or a list of them, from the page's request. Two of those the page itself uses: applying a
saved fitting, and launching commodities from a planet. This entry is the first.

**What was wrong.** No saved fitting could be applied on the game port: "invbroker.FitFitting
was given an argument that cannot be sent: Cannot marshal value". The page's scripted refit
uses the route.

**What the client does.** It applies a fitting on the ship's own inventory, which its inventory
cache asks the location's manager for, with seven arguments: the ship, the ship's type, the
hangar's items to fit from by type, where the pilot is docked, the fitting, the cargo, and
whether to fit rigs. The items are a `defaultdict` of sets. The fitting is a KeyVal of six
dicts. The recordings have no fitting applied: I looked in every folder. This server's own
inventory log has the call from an earlier day, with its arguments already read into plain
values, which shows the seven and not their wire form.

**What the transport does now.** The registry makes the three plain objects what the client
sends, and names the ship's type from godma. The transport applies the fitting on the ship's
own inventory and not on the manager the route has.

**What is worked out and not seen.** How a `defaultdict` and a `set` go to the wire. I asked
the client's own Python how it reduces each: a call of `collections.defaultdict` with `set`,
and its items after; and a call of `set` with a list. This server sends a set to the client
in that form, and reads that form of both. I fed what the registry makes to the server's own
reader and it read the items out. No recording has either on the wire.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the registry and 1 of the transport, each watched to fail on the code as it was.
  The orders in them (the KeyVal's six fields, a dict's keys, a set's items) are the client's
  Python's, asked for the very names and numbers the tests use.
- 30 ways of breaking it were tried and all 30 are caught. One survived the first pass: the
  test compared two objects that differ either way, and now names the one it must be.
- Suite: 9893 tests, 9869 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, before and after:**

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | The route, as Test Pilot at Jita | 400, "cannot be sent" | 200; the server says the module failed to load |
  | The same through the gateway | | 200; the same answer |
  | The route, as Test Two at its station | | 200; nothing failed to load, the module left the hangar, the ship's fitting names it |

  Test Pilot has no skill for the module I gave it (a mining laser), and the server will not
  fit it: the same through either transport. Test Two has the skill for an afterburner. The
  server's log for that one has `GetInventoryFromId` on the manager, then `FitFitting` on the
  object that answered. In the call ledger both read "reshaped", and the walk has no call
  that differs and none unchecked.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool, the first of them the
  first after a restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not in the browser.** The page's use of this route is its scripted refit, which I did not
  run. The route is the one it calls.
- The store was saved before and put back after, and the copy is deleted.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A fitting applied on the game port asks for the ship's inventory each time.** The client
  asks once and keeps it. One call more than the client makes, for each fitting after the
  first.
- **A route's fitting has the modules alone.** The other five dicts go out empty, as for a
  fitting with no drones, charges, fighters, ice or implants. A saved fitting that has some is
  applied without them, on either transport: that is the route's, and the page's.
- **The oracle's script left a file behind when a snippet of mine failed,** in the machine's
  Temp folder. I removed it.

**Not done.**

- The other routes that take a plain object from the page. They are on the list now.
- The page's own refit, and its Ready Fit window, walked in the browser on the game port.

## 2026-10-09 — a colony's commodities are launched and moved as the client sends them, so that they can be at all

Commit `4be3d32`, pushed. The first of item 9's routes, and the other planet route with it.

**What was wrong.** Nothing could be launched from a colony on the game port, or moved from one
pin of a colony to another: "planetMgr.UserLaunchCommodities was given an argument that cannot
be sent: Cannot marshal value". The BFF's two routes give the commodities as a plain object, and
the wire has no such value. The page uses the first: the Planetary Industry window's Haul
button writes a script whose first step launches what a command center holds. Nothing of the
page uses the second.

**What the client does.** Both calls go to the planet's own object (`clientPlanet.py` 412 and
448). A launch has the command center's pin and a dict of the quantities to launch by type. A
move has a list of pins, from the one the commodities leave to the one they reach, and a dict
of the quantities by type. I looked in every folder of the recordings. One file names the
second call, in a note's table, to say the walk it describes did not use it. No recording has
either on the wire.

**What the transport does now.** The registry makes the plain object a dict, in the order the
client's Python keeps those types, and the path a list.

**What is worked out and not seen.** The order of the dict's entries. For 2073, 2268 and 9848
the client's own Python says 9848, 2073, 2268, and the registry's model of it agrees. The
server reads a dict in whatever order it comes, so nothing it answered shows the order.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the registry, each watched to fail on the code as it was.
- 15 ways of breaking it were tried. 14 were caught at first. The one that was not: a move whose
  commodities were the client's dict already and whose path was an array went out with the
  path as it came. A case was added, and all 15 are caught.
- Suite: 9895 tests, 9871 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, before and after,** as Test Two, whose colony on Muvolailen I
  has a command center and a launchpad:

  | | Game port before | Game port after | Gateway |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Nothing in the colony: a move | 400, "cannot be sent" | | 409, the server's `RouteFailedValidationExpeditedSourceLacksCommodity` |
  | Nothing in the colony: a launch | 400, "cannot be sent" | | 409, the server's `CannotLaunchCommoditiesNotFound` |
  | 100 Aqueous Liquids and 50 Microorganisms on the launchpad: 30 and 20 moved to the command center | 400, "cannot be sent"; nothing moved | 200, two times; the launchpad has 70 and 30, the command center 30 and 20 | 200, two times; 30 and 20 more moved |
  | 10 and 5 launched from the command center | 400, "cannot be sent"; nothing launched | 200, one time; the command center has 20 and 15, the wallet is down 11.25 ISK | 200, one time; 10 and 5 fewer, the wallet down 11.25 ISK |

  The gateway's staged run was on what the game port's had left: it started from 70 and 30 on
  the launchpad and 20 and 15 in the command center, and ended at 40 and 10, and 40 and 30. I
  ran it first 47 seconds after the game port's and the server refused both, the move because
  the launchpad may not send again for five minutes and the launch because the command center
  may not launch again for one. I ran it again when the five minutes were up.

  The server's log has both calls on the planet's bound object. In the call ledger both read
  "reshaped", and that walk has no call that differs and none unchecked (34 pairs: 30 the same,
  4 reshaped).

  The answers are the same but for one known form: the times come from the game port as longs
  and from the gateway as bare strings of digits, which the parity tool counts and tolerates.
  The page reads neither answer.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, the first of
  them the first after the game-port BFF's restart, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not in the browser.** The page's use of the launch is a step of a script the Haul button
  writes, and the script goes on to undock a hauler and fetch what was launched. I did not run
  it. The route is the one that step calls.
- The launchpad's commodities were staged by an edit of the store with the server stopped. The
  store was saved before and put back after: the colony is empty again and the wallet reads
  what it read. The copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it, and the game-port BFF

**A mistake of mine, and what it cost.** I ran the parity tool as Test Pilot first. It read 23
identical, 10 tolerated and 1 moved, twice, and I took that for a fault of this change: the
count I had written down as clean is 21 and 13. It is Test Two's. Test Pilot is in no alliance,
so three of the alliance's reads are refused on both transports alike, and its notifications
have no number the two transports print differently. I found that out from the server's log,
which has the alliance's calls on a bound object in the earlier passes and on the service in
these. The brief says now that the count is one pilot's, and gives the other's.

What is real in Test Pilot's passes: `/api/bridge/flight/status` read "moved" both times, with
a notice in the game port's answer and none in the gateway's (`OnServerBrainUpdated` once,
`OnModuleAttributeChanges` once). That is item 33's, and is written there.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **What is no quantity of a type is left out of the dict.** A key that is not a whole number

**Not done.**

## 2026-10-09 — the Planetary Industry window's Haul, walked in the browser on the game port

Commit `4b950aa`, pushed; eve.js `c30983877`, on `main`, not pushed. From item 9: the first of the
three mended routes to be used in the page itself.

**Why this and not the next route.** The list's next were the other routes that take a plain
object. I looked: the page uses none of them. Three iterations running I had written "not in
the browser" under a mended route. So this one uses the page.

**What the Haul button does.** It sends the ticked colonies' launchpads up into their customs
offices. Then it starts a run on the BFF's own bot: launch what the command centers hold, get
into a ship with a planetary hold, undock, empty the customs offices, collect the launches,
fly back, unload, and get back into the first ship.

**The first walk.** As Test Two, with 200 Aqueous Liquids staged on the launchpad, 100 more and
50 Microorganisms in the command center, and an Epithal given. The run finished in two and a half
minutes and said so. It had not collected its own launch. Its log has "Reading your planet
launches", then the flight home.

| Read of the pilot's launches | Answer |
|---|---|
| Through the gateway BFF | one row: launch 910000000000, its container, where it is |
| Through the game-port BFF | nothing, and no error |

The server's log, once in that run and once at each of my two reads after it:

```
[PKT] ERR planetMgr GetMyLaunchesDetails() The value of "value" is out of range. It must be >= -2147483648 and <= 2147483647. Received 910_000_000_000
```

**The server's fault.** It numbered launches from 910,000,000,000 and sends the launch's ID in
a 32-bit column. From a pilot's first launch on, the list could not be put on the wire, and a
game client was answered nothing. The gateway does not marshal, and showed the row. The column
is right: Tranquility's recordings have the same descriptor, with the ID as a 32-bit integer
(`Archive/Open PI Panel - adding route.txt`, 649). Their lists are all empty, so no launch's
own number is recorded.

A sub-agent mended it in eve.js: launches are numbered from 910,000,000, and a launch stored
under an old number is given a new one when the store is read, keeping its container and its
place. I read the change and ran its test file myself: 34 tests, 34 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled.
Four of them are new and push the handler's real answer through the server's own encoder, one
of those through the packet dispatcher. The sub-agent reports each failed on the code as it
was, with the line above.

**The page's faults the walk showed.**

- **An answer of nothing was taken for no launches.** The page's read says in its own comment
  that it must never mistake "could not read" for "no launches", and it did: only a named
  error counted. An answer of nothing is unread now. The collecting block tries ten times,
  then says the launches could not be read and stops, where it used to go on.
- **A launch was warped to as an item, by its container's ID.** The client's journal warps to
  a launch by the launch's own ID: `CmdWarpToStuff('launch', launchID)`, with no range
  (`journal.py` 453). The page has a route for it now, and the block uses it.
- **Three planet calls were unchecked in the ledger.** `GetPlanetsForChar` and
  `GetMyLaunchesDetails` are in the recordings, each by name and with nothing.
  `DeleteLaunch(launchID)` is the journal's Remove on a launch; no recording has one.

**The second walk,** on the mended server and the new page, from the same staging:

| Step | What the bot's log has | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Export | (the window) "Launched 200 units from 1 colony into their customs offices" | |
| Launch | launch 50 and 100 from the command center | ok |
| Board | board the Epithal | ok |
| Undock, warp to the customs office, empty it | | ok |
| Launches | "Reading your planet launches", then **warp to launch 910000000** | ok |
| Collect | collect launch 910000000 from its container | ok |
| Home | set course, dock, empty holds (5 stacks), board the Badger | ok |

Three minutes. Afterwards, read by script on the game port: the hangar has the 200 from the
customs office, 160 Biofuels that were in the office before (the store as it stands has them
there), and the launch's 100 and 50; the pilot
has no launches listed; the colony is empty; the wallet is down 162.50 ISK. The server's log
for the warp reads `CmdWarpToStuff char=140000002 type=launch target=910000000 minRange=0`, and
has no `[PKT] ERR` in those minutes. The Bot Manager lists the run as finished.

The call ledger for that BFF's whole life (the board's reads and the run): 49 pairs, every call
of them the same or reshaped, none that differs and none unchecked. The first walk's ledger had
the two planet reads unchecked, beside others from parity passes run on that BFF before it.

**Proof.**

- Tests watched to fail on the code as it was: 2 of the BFF's route, 3 of the page's read and
  its warp, 2 of the collecting block with two more of its own changed to the new warp, 1 of
  the registry's, and the bot log's own check that every action has a sentence. 2 more were
  written after the code and seen to catch its breaking: they hold the page to carrying out
  every action a bot can decide on. Nothing did before, for this action or any other.
- 27 ways of breaking it were tried, in three passes, and all 27 are caught. One line I had
  added could have no effect, by the code around it, and I took it out again.
- Suite: 9905 tests, 9881 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. The page's type check passes.
- **In the browser, on the game port:** the two walks above, by the window's own buttons.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, the first of
  them the first after both BFFs were restarted, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not through the gateway BFF.** The haul was not run there.
- The store was saved before each walk and put back after: the colony is empty, the wallet
  reads what it read, the hangar has the Badger alone. Both copies are deleted. EveJS was
  restarted four times for it and runs the mended code now. I took Test Two off the window's
  board again, and the pane is back to its own size.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Where the server's launches are numbered from, and what becomes of old ones.** 910,000,000
  is the sub-agent's choice: no recording has a launch's number. A store's old launches are
  renumbered when it is read, and still answer to their old numbers. eve.js's `UPDATING.md`
  says so.
- **A haul that cannot read its launches stops, in space, and says why.** Before, it flew home
  and reported that it had finished. On the server as it was, every haul with a launch in it
  would stop there.
- **A row with no launch ID is still warped to as an item.** The page's reader keeps such a row
  if it has a container. No server answer I have seen has one.
- **The new route names no range.** The client names none for a launch. The other warps of the
  page's bots name the autopilot's.
- **One haul bot is saved in the game-port BFF's library** ("Planetary: haul"), as the button
  saves it. It is in that BFF's own data folder, not in the store, and I left it.

**For the operator.**

- eve.js `main` is five ahead of its origin, not pushed: `16d95626a`, `59d2ac81e`,
  `3ccbcef51`, `342a366a6`, `c30983877`.
- The sub-agent reports `server/tests/testStoreIsolationGuard.test.js` red on the unchanged
  tree as well, 13 or 14 tests of it, a different set each run, nearly all saying the live
  store's `gamestore.sqlite-wal` changed during the test. The live server was running. It is
  not in `doc/TEST_BASELINE.md`. I did not look into it.

**Not done.**

## 2026-10-09 — a launchpad's goods go up into a customs office on the pilot's own session, as the client sends them

Commit `051b504`, pushed. From item 10: the first half of moving the haul's export to where the
client makes it. The page does not use it yet.

**What is wrong, and still is.** The haul sends its launchpads up before its bot starts. The
BFF logs a second game-port client in for that, selects the pilot on it, waits three seconds,
makes its calls and hangs up. A third of a second later the bot logs the same pilot in again.
The server's log of the last haul has it: a connection whose first call after the select is
`map.GetSolarsystemItems`,
then `planetOrbitalRegistryBroker.GetTaxRate` by the service's name, `invbroker` bound with
the office's ID, and `ImportExportWithPlanet` on that. None of it is in the call ledger, and
the pilot is docked the whole time.

**What the client does.** It makes the transfer at the office, in space, from the office's
window. Tranquility's recording of an export has the calls on the wire, and I read them from
its bytes:

| Step | On the wire |
|---|---|
| The office's inventory | `GetInventoryFromId(officeID, 0)`, on the inventory manager's bound object |
| Its tax rate | `MachoResolveObject(systemID)`, then `MachoBindObject(systemID, ('GetTaxRate', (officeID,), {}))`: a Moniker made for the call, three times in the one export |
| The transfer | `ImportExportWithPlanet(pinID, {}, {2398: 100.0}, 0.20000000149011612)`, on the office's inventory |

A note that lies beside that recording says `GetInventoryFromId(officeID, 8)`. The byte is
`\x08`, the marshal's code for the integer nought. I took the bytes' word.

**What is built.** A route of the BFF's, `/api/bridge/planet/customs/export`, that makes the
rate's call and the transfer on the session the pilot holds. In space only: the client has no
office to open while docked, and its registry Moniker is for the system the session is in
space in. The registry has the two calls, and the transport makes the registry's Moniker anew
for each call, bound by that system and carrying the call.

The web gateway's list of calls has no `ImportExportWithPlanet`, and the transport took that
list for its own. It has a short list of its own beside it now, with this one call on it.

**Proof.**

- Tests, each watched to fail on the code as it was: 3 of the registry, 3 of the transport, 4 of
  the route, and the write list's own. Two older tests of the registry were brought in line
  with a new service made on a Moniker and a second list of calls.
- 42 ways of breaking it were tried. 40 were caught at first. The two that were not were checks
  that could not matter: a rate's kind looked at twice, and a list refused twice. Each is
  looked at once now.
- Suite: 9915 tests, 9891 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. One test failed on the first
  run: a generated file pins the BFF's list of writes, and I had not run its script. Run, its
  change is the one pair.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Two, with 200 Aqueous Liquids and 50 Microorganisms
  staged on the launchpad:

  | Where | The route's answer | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Docked | 409, not in space | nothing moved |
  | At the office, after an undock and a warp to it | 200, tax rate 0.05 | the office has 120 and 50 more, the launchpad 80, the wallet is down 42.50 ISK |

  The server's log of it: `invbroker` bound for the system with `GetInventoryFromId` for the
  office, then `planetOrbitalRegistryBroker` resolved and bound with `GetTaxRate` for the
  office riding on the bind, then `ImportExportWithPlanet` on the office's own object. In the
  ledger the rate's call and the transfer both read "reshaped", and that BFF's whole ledger
  has no call that differs and none unchecked (41 pairs).
- **Through the gateway BFF,** at the office: 403, "not on the web-call allowlist". Nothing
  moved.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, the first of
  them the first after both BFFs were restarted, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not in the browser.** Nothing of the page calls the route yet.
- The store was saved before and put back after: the colony is empty, the pilot is docked, the
  wallet reads what it read. The copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The route refuses a docked pilot, though this server would take one.** I tried it by the
  old way in the hauls before: the server makes the transfer for a pilot sitting in a station.
  The client cannot ask it from there.
- **The quantities go as whole numbers.** Tranquility's recording has a float, because its
  colony's pins hold floats. This server's pins hold whole numbers, and a client sends back
  what it was given.
- **The rate goes as it was answered,** with no kind forced on it.
- **The game port has a list of calls the gateway has not.** One call. The other way was to add
  the pair to the server's gateway list, which is the server's to change and is not a fault
  of it.
- **A route that sends goods up only.** What comes down from an office the page takes as it
  takes anything out of a container.

**For the operator.**

- eve.js `main` is level with its origin. Its own record says it was pushed from this
  checkout at 18:42 and at 19:13 today. I did not push it, and the sub-agent says it did not.
  The last entry's "five ahead, not pushed" was true when I read it and is not now.
- Two things of this server's seen in passing, neither looked into: it makes a customs transfer
  for a docked pilot, and its colony pins hold whole numbers where Tranquility's hold floats.

**Not done.**

- The haul still sends its launchpads up the old way. Using the route from the haul's own lap,
  at the office, is the next thing on the list.
- The office's own reads as the client's window makes them.

## 2026-10-09 — a haul sends its launchpads up at the customs office, on the pilot's own session

Commit `d443332`, pushed. Item 10's first: the other half of the last entry.

**What was wrong.** A haul sent its launchpads up before its bot started: the BFF logged a
second game-port client in, selected the pilot on it while docked, made calls that are not the
client's, and hung up a third of a second before the bot logged the same pilot in. The last
entry built the client's own way of it as a route. This one makes the haul use it.

**What the page does now.** For a pilot on the game port:

- The Haul button sends nothing up. The BFF answers that the run will, and makes no second
  login. The window says: "The haul has started on the server. It sends each colony's
  launchpads up at its customs office."
- The haul's collecting block goes to an office when it holds the pilot's goods, as before, or
  when its planet's launchpads do. At the office it sends each launchpad up, one at a time,
  through the route, and then empties the office.

**How an office's planet is known.** The client reads it off the office's slim item
(`customsOfficeItem.planetID`, `importExportUI.py` 94). The game port's snapshot passes that on
for an orbital now. This server's own recording of an undock, which the tests use, has eight
offices and eight planets, and each office names a different one of them. The web gateway's
snapshot has no such field: I read its row builder.

**A pilot on the gateway** is sent up the old way, by the second login, as before. At the
office its launchpads are empty by then, and its offices do not say their planets, so nothing
is tried there.

**Proof.**

- Tests watched to fail on the code as it was: 5 of the collecting block, 1 of the snapshot from
  the server's own recording, 1 of the page's reading of it, 2 of the page's calls, 1 of what
  the button's answer is summed up as, 1 of the window's words, 1 that the page carries the new
  action out and reads the colonies for this block, 1 of the transport's seam, 1 of the BFF's
  answer for a pilot on the game port, and the bot log's own check. Not seen to fail first, and
  seen to catch the code's breaking: 2 more of the block that say what it must not send up, 1
  through the real runner for a launchpad the server refuses, and 2 that the BFF's answer
  still wants what it wanted and that a gateway pilot is still sent up the old way.
- 46 ways of breaking it were tried. 45 were caught at first. The one that was not was a check
  that could not matter, and it is gone.
- Suite: 9934 tests, 9910 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. The page's type check passes.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** by the Planetary Industry window's own buttons, as Test
  Two, with 200 Aqueous Liquids and 50 Microorganisms staged on the launchpad, 100 and 50 in
  the command center, and an Epithal given. The bot's log:

  | Step | Result |
  |---|---|
  | launch 50 and 100 from the command center | ok |
  | board the Epithal, undock, warp to the customs office | ok |
  | **send 2073x50, 2268x200 from the launchpad up into the customs office** | ok |
  | empty the customs office | ok |
  | warp to launch 910000000, collect it | ok |
  | set course, dock, empty holds (6 stacks), board the Badger | ok |

  Three minutes and eight seconds. Afterwards, read by script: the colony's two pins are empty,
  the pilot has no launches listed, the wallet is down 175.00 ISK, and the hangar has the
  launchpad's 200 and 50, the launch's 100 and 50, and the 160 Biofuels the office held.

  The server's log of those minutes has one connection and one select, the bot's, where the
  haul before had two of each. It has the registry resolved and bound with `GetTaxRate` riding
  on the bind, then `ImportExportWithPlanet` with four arguments on the office's own object,
  and no `[PKT] ERR`. The call ledger of that BFF's whole life has both calls, and no call that
  differs and none unchecked (51 pairs).
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, the first of
  them the first after both BFFs were restarted, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not through the gateway BFF.** A haul was not run there.
- The store was saved before and put back after: the colony is empty, the wallet reads what it
  read, the hangar has the Badger alone. The copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it.
  I took Test Two off the window's board again, and the pane is back to its own size.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The old way is kept for a pilot on the gateway.** The gateway's list has no such call, so
  there is no other way there.
- **Everything a launchpad holds goes up,** as before. The hold of the ship that comes for it
  is not asked.
- **A launchpad the server refuses five times is left,** and the office is emptied all the
  same. The refusals are in the bot's log. The block also says how many it left when it ends,
  and I found that the runner never shows a block's last sentence, this one or any other's:
  that is on the list.
- **The button's words before it is pressed are as they were.** They say the launchpads go up
  and then the run starts, which is now the other way about for a pilot on the game port. The
  page does not know which transport a pilot is on until it asks.
- **The BFF's answer for such a pilot names each planet with no system and no name.** The page
  shows neither.
- **The transport's new question is named as a read** (`getSelectTransport`). The fence around
  the transport takes any other name for a write and looks for a pilot to hold.

**Not done.**

- An office read only where the ship is at it, and read as the client's window reads it.
- The second login for a pilot on the gateway.

## 2026-10-10 — a pilot's colonies and launches are asked for once and kept, and a wrong word of mine taken back

Commit `cf61e7d`, pushed. From item 10.

**A correction first.** Two entries ago I wrote that the client "makes the transfer at the
office", and one entry ago I planned an office "read only where the ship is at it", as a thing
"no client can" do from elsewhere. Both are wrong. I had one recording, whose pilot was at the
office, and made a rule of it. The client's customs window has three callers: the office's own
menu in space, the Planets window's list of colonies, and a launchpad in the planet's view. It
wants only that the office's slim item be in the ballpark, and this server's ballpark has every
office of the system from the undock on. So a client can read an office, ask its rate and make
the transfer from across the system.

What stands: the route refuses a docked pilot, as the window must (no ballpark); and a haul
that sends its launchpads up when it is at the office does nothing a client cannot. What does
not stand is the plan to read offices only at them. It is off the list, and the reference says
where the window opens from. Whether Tranquility's server takes the transfer from across the
system is in no recording.

**What this entry builds.** The client asks for a pilot's colonies once and for its launches
once, and keeps both (`planetSvc.py` 65, `planetUISvc.py` 170). The page's haul asked for each
at every reading. The transport keeps both now, as it keeps the notifications and the calendar:

| Forgotten at | As the client |
|---|---|
| the server's `OnPILaunchesChange` | forgets its launches |
| the server's `OnMajorPlanetStateUpdate` | changes its own list of colonies |
| the pilot's own `DeleteLaunch`, done or refused | asks for the launches afresh |
| the pilot's own `UserUpdateNetwork`, on the planet's object, done or refused | changes its own count of the colony's pins |

Either forgets both lists, so the colonies are asked for more often than a client asks, and
never later. A write made on an object did not reach what the transport keeps until now: the
two services that had kept reads are written to by name.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 2 of the transport, each watched to fail on the code as it was.
- 13 ways of breaking it were tried. 12 were caught at first. The one that was not: a refused
  change to a colony left the lists kept. A case was added, and all 13 are caught.
- Suite: 9936 tests, 9912 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, before and after,** as Test Two: the route read five times, a
  launch made from the command center, the route read three times, the launch removed, the
  route read three times. What the page was answered was the same both times: no launch, then
  one, then none. What the server's log has:

  | Call | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `planetMgr.GetPlanetsForChar` | 11 | 3 |
  | `planetMgr.GetMyLaunchesDetails` | 11 | 3 |

  After, each was asked at first, again behind the server's `OnPILaunchesChange`, and again
  behind `DeleteLaunch`. The call ledger has three of each, read "same".
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, the first of
  them the first after both BFFs were restarted, both 21 identical, 13 tolerated.
- **Not in the browser.** Nothing of the page changed: the route is the one the haul's blocks
  read, and it answered as before.
- The store was saved before and put back after: the colony is empty and the wallet reads what
  it read. The copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it.

**Found on the way, and on the list now.** The page's read of a colony's pins, which the haul
makes every two seconds, never asks the pilot's session anything: the BFF answers it from the
web gateway's snapshot of the store, on either transport. The client asks the planet's own
object. That is the larger gap, and it is the next item.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Both lists are forgotten at any of the four,** which is how the transport's other kept
  reads go. The client keeps its colonies through all four and changes them itself.
- **A launch made does not forget them by itself.** The server's notice does, as in the client.
  This server sends it before it answers the launch.
- **A read with something sent beside it is not kept.** It is no call of the client's.

**For the operator.**

- The first select through the game-port BFF after an EveJS restart, made as soon as the
  gateway answered (fifteen seconds in), answered 502, "the game server is unreachable". Eight
  seconds later it went through. I did not look into which side was not ready. The brief says to wait.

**Not done.**

- A colony's pins read as the client reads them.
- The offices' listings kept: one collecting step bound an office 13 times and listed one 37
  times.

## 2026-10-10 — a held pilot's colonies are read as the client reads them, on the pilot's own session

Commit `1bfd24c`, pushed. Item 10's first.

**What was wrong.** The page's read of a pilot's colonies, with every pin and what it holds,
never asked the pilot's session anything. The BFF answered it from the web gateway's snapshot
of the store, on either transport. A haul makes that read every two seconds. The server's log
of five reads of the route had six requests for the snapshot and no call of the planet
manager's.

**What the client does.** It asks the planet manager for the planets it has colonies on, and
each planet's own object for its colony (`GetPlanetInfo`, `clientPlanet.py` 83) and, where it
shows what a planet carries, for that (`GetPlanetResourceInfo`, 644), each with nothing.
Tranquility's recordings have the colony's read riding the planet's bind. The client keeps the
colony and reckons what it makes by itself, and asks again when the server says the planet's
state changed.

**What the BFF does now,** for a pilot on the game port: those calls, on the pilot's own
session. The answers are made into the row the snapshot's colonies are, so the page is
answered in the form it had. A pilot on the gateway is read from the snapshot as before.

**What the transport keeps.** A colony by its planet, for a minute. Nothing here reckons a
colony, so a kept one would fall behind what the colony makes; a minute is my figure for how
far. It forgets every colony at the server's `OnMajorPlanetStateUpdate` and `OnRefreshPins`,
and after the pilot's own change to a colony, launch, moving of goods between pins, or sending
of goods through a customs office. What a planet carries it keeps.

**Proof.**

- Tests watched to fail on the code as it was: 1 of the registry, 2 of the transport, 3 of the
  route, 1 of the parity tool. Not seen to fail: 6 of the module that makes an answer into a
  row, written with it, whose first fixture is this server's own answer, printed through the
  game-port BFF; and 1 that a gateway pilot is still read from the snapshot, which held before
  as after.
- 49 ways of breaking it were tried. 46 were caught at first. The three that were not, each
  given a case: anything asked of a planet's object with nothing was kept; a planet with no
  colony stopped the planets after it; and the colonies were not put in order. All 49 are
  caught.
- Suite: 9950 tests, 9926 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, before and after,** as Test Two with goods staged on both
  pins: the route read five times. What the page was answered is the same but for one figure,
  the time the colony is reckoned up to, which is the stored one before and now after. What
  the server's log has for the five reads:

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | requests for the gateway's snapshot | 6 | 1 |
  | `planetMgr.GetPlanetsForChar` | 0 | 1 |
  | the planet's object bound, with `GetPlanetInfo` riding | 0 | 1 |
  | `GetPlanetResourceInfo` on it | 0 | 1 |

  The one request for the snapshot that is left is not this route's: it was there in the
  count of six.
- **In the browser, on the game port:** the Planetary Industry window's Haul, by its own
  buttons, from the same staging. The run did what it did before, each thing once: launch
  from the command center, board, undock, send the launchpad up at the office, empty the
  office, collect the launch, home, six stacks unloaded. Three minutes and eight seconds. The
  server's log of those minutes has `GetPlanetInfo` four times, twice riding a bind, and three
  notices from the server of a change to a colony; no `[PKT] ERR`; and three requests for the
  snapshot, where the log of the haul before has thirty. The call ledger has no call that
  differs and none unchecked (53 pairs).
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, the first of
  them the first after both BFFs were restarted, both 20 identical, 14 tolerated. The row that
  changed is this route's: "tolerated, client-reckoned ×1". Before the tool was told of it, the
  one pass I ran read "1 moved", for that figure.
- The store was saved before and put back after: the colony is empty, the wallet reads what it
  read, the hangar has the Badger alone. The copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it.
  Test Two is off the window's board again, and the pane is back to its own size.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A colony is kept a minute.** The client keeps it for as long as it has the planet, because
  it reckons the colony itself. That reckoning is on the list. Until it is done, a colony is
  asked for more often than a client asks, and what the page shows of what a colony has made
  is at most a minute old.
- **Every colony is forgotten at any of the changes,** not the one planet's.
- **The clean count of a parity pass is 20 and 14 now.** The colonies route differs in one
  figure by design: the client's read has the colony reckoned up to now, the stored row up to
  when it was last reckoned. The tool names it. Anything else of a colony that differs is
  still listed, though under "tolerated" where it is beside that figure: read the whole pass.
- **A planet the manager lists with no colony of the pilot's on it is left out,** and the
  manager answering no list is "not read".
- **The older route that asks a planet's object with the planet named again** is left as it
  is, and the ledger reads it "differs". Nothing of the page uses it.

**Not done.**

- The three snapshot requests a haul still makes, and the other reads of the page's that are
  answered from the snapshot for a held pilot.
- A planet's object bound twice in one haul.
- A colony reckoned as the client reckons it.

## 2026-10-10 — a station's guests and its own item are kept as the client's station service keeps them

Commit `b777a54`, pushed. Item 1's next.

**What was wrong.** Every read the page made of who is in the station asked the server
`station.GetGuests`, and every read of the station's own item asked it
`stationSvc.GetStationItemBits`. And the page did nothing with the server's word that a pilot
had docked or left: the guests it showed were those of its last read, until Refresh was
pressed.

**What the client does** (`eve/client/script/ui/station/base.py`). It asks for the guests while
it has no list, or the list it has is another station's (99 to 103), and from then on changes
its own list: `OnCharNowInStation` adds a pilot who is not a guest yet (86), and
`OnCharNoLongerInStation` takes one out (93). It asks for the station's item while it has none,
or the one it has is not the station the session is in (573, 586). It lets both go when the
session leaves the station.

**What the recordings have.** `GetGuests` is in 29 files (a structure's among them) and
`GetStationItemBits` in 25. As read in `Logging in then renaming ship.txt`: both calls with
nothing beside them, the guests a list of `[charID, corpID, allianceID, warFactionID]`, the
item a tuple of owner, station, operation and the station's type, and each notice carrying one
guest's four. In `Archive/Logging In.txt` one answer to `GetGuests` is logged, and 92 arrivals
and 122 leavings told to the client.

**What the transport does now** (`src/gamePort/pilotStation.js`, and `stationRead` in
`pilots.js`). The same, for a read asked as the client asks it. The first asking in a station
is sent, noted in the ledger, and kept; a later one is answered from what is kept, the guests
as the notices have changed them since. Two askings at once of guests not yet had ask once.
Leaving the station lets both go. The page reads the guests again at either notice
(`web/src/app/flow.ts`), and that read is answered from what is kept.

**Proof.**

- Tests watched to fail on the code as it was: 5 of the transport and 2 of the page's flow.
  The transport's file and the flow's were put back to the commit before, the tests run (5 of
  252 failed, and 2 of 2), and the files restored. Not seen to fail: 7 of the new module,
  written with it.
- 33 ways of breaking it were tried. 28 were caught at first. Of the five that were not, two
  were checks that could not matter, and were taken out: that the pilot is in a station before
  a read is looked for among the kept, and that the item answered has anything in it. Three
  were each given a case: the guests counted as had for a pilot in no station; what is read
  being the kept rows themselves; and a notice that is neither of the two, naming a guest. The
  31 left are all caught.
- Suite: 9964 tests, 9940 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, before and after,** as Test Pilot docked in Jita, with Test
  Three chosen and let go beside it: the guests read four times and the item twice. What the
  page was answered is the same. What the server's log has:

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | `station.GetGuests` | 4 | 1 |
  | `stationSvc.GetStationItemBits` | 2 | 1 |
  | `OnCharNowInStation` sent to the pilot | 1 | 1 |
  | `OnCharNoLongerInStation` sent to the pilot | 1 | 1 |

- **In the browser, on the game port:** Test Pilot brought online by the page's own buttons,
  the Inventory & Ship window open, its Guests reading "1 in station", Test Pilot alone. A
  script chose Test Three through the same BFF, held it ten seconds and let it go. The page,
  read five times a second and with no button pressed, went to "2 in station" with Test Three
  of Elysian Industries under Test Pilot, and ten seconds later back to "1 in station". The
  server's log of that time has the two notices going out, 0.2 s before each change in the
  page, and no `GetGuests` and no `GetStationItemBits`.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, after both BFFs
  were restarted on this code, both 20 identical, 14 tolerated.
- Nothing was staged, so there was no store to put back. The page was logged out by its own
  button, and the pane is back to its own size.

**A defect of the server's, found here and fixed.** EveJS sent a guest's four with a nought
where the pilot has no alliance, or no war faction. Tranquility's recordings have None there:
in `Archive/Logging In.txt`, of the 92 arrivals told to the client, 85 are `[char, corp, None,
None]`, 6 have an alliance and None, and 1 has both; none has a nought. A structure's guests
have None in the same places.

A sub-agent fixed it in eve.js: commit `3cdc14973` on `main`, not pushed. It is one function
(`buildGuestIdentityTuple`, `server/src/services/_shared/guestLists.js`), from which the
station's list, the station's two notices, a structure's list and a structure's notice all
take a guest. By its report, 8 tests of its three files failed before the change. I read the
diff, ran the three files with the isolated runner (14 tests, 14 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled),
and restarted EveJS. Read again on the game port: Test Pilot is `[140000001, 1000044, null,
null]` and Test Three `[140000003, 98000000, 99000000, null]`, in the list and in each notice;
`GetGuests` asked once and `GetStationItemBits` once; no `[PKT] ERR`. Two parity passes after
the restart: 20 identical, 14 tolerated. The page reads a nought and None alike as "none", so
what it shows is as it was.

**For the operator, of the server.**

- **eve.js `main` is one commit ahead of origin**, `3cdc14973`. I do not push eve.js.
- **Two more of the server's differ from the recordings, and are not fixed.** A guest's four
  go out from EveJS as a tuple, in the station's list and in its two notices; Tranquility
  sends a list (the notice's bytes in `Logging in then renaming ship.txt`, line 3672, are a
  list of four inside the one-tuple of arguments). And EveJS addresses a structure's two
  notices by `clientID` where Tranquility's packets say `structureid` (the sub-agent's
  reading; I did not read those packets). The client's code takes a guest's four apart the
  same way from either (`base.py` 87, 94, 104). I left both, as changing nothing a client
  does; they are on the list.
- A harness test of eve.js (`harnessStructureScenarios.test.js`) reads a guest's places
  through a number, so it passes with a nought or with None. The sub-agent left it.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **An answer that is no list is handed on as it came, and nothing is kept of it.** The next
  asking is sent.
- **A read with anything beside it is sent as it is asked,** and nothing is kept of it. The
  client sends neither call with anything.
- **The transport does not ask by itself as a pilot docks.** It keeps from the first asking
  the page makes. When the client first asks in a station I did not measure.
- **The list is kept in the transport, not in the page.** The page asks the BFF again at each
  notice: one request more of the BFF, none of the server.
- **The gateway's BFF is as it was:** its read of the guests asks the gateway each time.
  Whether its page is told of an arrival I did not look at.

**Not done.**

- `map.GetStationInfo` and `officeManager.GetMyCorporationsOffices`.
- A structure's guests, which the client keeps in the same way from `structureGuests.GetGuests`
  and the two notices of a structure.
- `docs/game-port-login-calls.md` made again.

## 2026-10-10 — a corporation's offices are kept as the client's office manager keeps them

Commit `fe5be58`, pushed. Item 1's next.

**What was wrong.** Every read the BFF made of the offices a pilot's corporation rents asked
the server `officeManager.GetMyCorporationsOffices`: the corporation hangar's read, the list of
offices the bot builder shows, and each place of a move that names a corporation hangar. And
the page did nothing with the server's word that the corporation had rented an office or given
one up: its corporation hangar stayed as last read until Refresh was pressed.

**What the client does** (`eve/client/script/ui/services/corporation/officeManager.py`). It
asks for the corporation's offices while it has none (41), and keeps them. It lets them go at
`OnOfficeRentalChange(corporationID, officeID)` where the corporation is the session's (72),
and when the session's corporation changes (62). Its inventory window draws its tree again at
that notice, where the corporation is the session's (`invWindow.py` 1435).

**What the recordings have.** The call is in 11 recordings, once in each, with nothing beside
it. In `Renting Corporate Office - Opening Each hanger division.txt` and `Unrenting Corp
Office.txt` the notice comes twice, once addressed by `stationid` and once by `corpid`, each
with the corporation and the office; after it the client asks for the offices once. The answer
is a list of rows of eleven values, the station the second and the office the ninth.

**What the transport does now** (`pilots.js`, `KEPT_UNTIL_CHANGED`). The same: the first
asking is sent, noted in the ledger and kept; a later one is answered from what is kept. The
offices are let go at the notice where it names the corporation the session is in, and in
another corporation. Another corporation's office lets nothing go. The page reads its
corporation hangar again at the notice, where the corporation is its pilot's and the hangar is
open (`web/src/app/flow.ts`).

**Proof.**

- Tests watched to fail on the code as it was: 4 of the transport, 1 of the page's flow. Not
  seen to fail: 1 of the page's flow, that another corporation's office, another notice and a
  hangar never opened read nothing, which held before as after.
- 27 ways of breaking it were tried, and all 27 were caught. Before the pass I took out two
  checks that could not matter (that the corporation named is a number, in the transport and
  in the page) and added one case (another read of the office manager's is asked each time).
- Suite: 9970 tests, 9946 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port, before and after,** as Test Three and as Test Two: the
  offices read four times and the corporation hangar twice. What the page was answered is the
  same. The server's log has `GetMyCorporationsOffices` six times before, for each pilot, and
  once after.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** from a staged start (below): Test Two online in Jita by
  the page's own buttons, the Inventory & Ship window open on its Corp hangar tab, which read
  "Your corporation has no office at this station." A script of its own session, as Test Three,
  rented the corporation an office there, and twelve seconds later gave it up. The page, read
  five times a second and with no button pressed, showed the seven divisions 0.7 s after the
  rent was sent, and the first sentence again 0.6 s after the office was given up. In all that
  time the page's session asked the server for the offices three times: as the window opened,
  after the rent, and after the giving up. No `[PKT] ERR`.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, after both BFFs
  were restarted on this code, both 20 identical, 14 tolerated.
- **The staging, and its undoing.** The store was saved. Test Three gave up the corporation's
  office in Jita, on a session of the script's own. Test Two was moved to Jita with the GM's
  `/tr me 60003760`. The first rent was refused, `NotEnoughMoney`: the corporation's wallet
  held nothing and the rent is 10,000. Test Three then gave its corporation 20,000
  (`account.GiveCash`), and the rent was taken. After the check the store was put back (the
  script compared it with the copy: the same), and read again: Test Two is in Muvolailen, the
  corporation's one office is in Jita, and Test Three's corporation hangar there opens. The
  copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it. The page was logged out by its own
  button, and the pane is back to its own size.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The offices are let go only at a notice of the session's own corporation,** as the client
  does. The other reads the transport keeps are let go at any notice of their kind.
- **An answer on its way when the notice comes is handed on and not kept.** The recording of
  the renting has the second notice arriving while the client's asking is out, and no second
  asking after it. The transport asks once more than that, and is never behind.
- **The page reads the corporation hangar again only where it has it open,** and takes no
  other part of what the client's lobby does at the notice.
- **The staging called `UnrentOffice` and `RentOffice` by name, with nothing.** The client
  calls both on the station's own object (`officeManager.py` 117, 122). EveJS takes either.
  Nothing built here sends them.

**For the operator.**

- **Nothing of the BFF's rents an office in a station.** The one route named for it
  (`/api/bridge/corp-office/rent-at-structure`) reads the offices and stops at
  `stockCompatibility.structureServices()`, which refuses by design, and the gateway client
  refuses `officeManager.RentOffice` the same way. I took that as decided and left it.
- **EveJS sends `OnOfficeRentalChange` to every session, twice**
  (`corporationNotifications.js`, `notifyOfficeRentalChange`: `sendNotificationToAllSessions`
  for `stationid` and again for `corpid`). Tranquility's two packets are addressed by station
  and by corporation. That a pilot in neither is told nothing on Tranquility I infer from the
  addressing; no recording can show it. Not fixed; it is on the list with the two of the last
  entry.
- **The session's scratch folder holds 33 older copies of the store,** from earlier
  iterations; the folder is 1.9 GB. This iteration's copy is deleted; I left the older ones.
- eve.js `main` is still one commit ahead of origin (`3cdc14973`).

**Not done.**

- The station's own offices, which the client asks of the station's object and keeps
  (`GetCorporationsWithOffices`, `officeManager.py` 34): nothing of ours asks for them.
- Renting an office and giving one up as the client does, on the station's object, with the
  price asked first.
- `map.GetStationInfo`; a structure's guests; `docs/game-port-login-calls.md` made again.
