## 2026-10-10 — a station's offices are read as the client's lobby reads them, of the station's own object

Commit `47b60b3`, pushed. Item 1's next.

**First, what needed nothing.** `map.GetStationInfo` was next on the list. Asked three times
through the game-port BFF, the server's log has it once, with one `GetCachableObject` behind
it: the transport's object cache answers the second and third with nothing sent, as the
client's does. Nothing was changed. What I saw beside it is below, for the list.

**What was missing.** The retail lobby lists the corporations with an office in the station
and says how many offices are free. Nothing of ours read either, and the transport had no
object for the station's offices at all.

**What the client does** (`officeManager.py`, `dockedUI/offices.py`). It makes a Moniker for
the office manager by the station or structure the session is docked in (50), and keeps it
while docked there. On it, it asks for the corporations with offices while it has none (34),
letting them go at any `OnOfficeRentalChange` (71) and out of the station (58, 66), and for
the count of free offices each time the lobby lists them (136), but not in a structure (133).
The lobby lists them when its Offices tab is shown and at each office rented or given up.

**What the recordings have.** `Receiving Corp Roles.txt` has the bind, there by a
structure's ID: `MachoResolveObject(ID)`, then `MachoBindObject(ID, ('PrimeOfficeItem', (),
{}))`, the first call riding. The recordings of an office rented and of one given up have
`GetCorporationsWithOffices` and `GetEmptyOfficeCount` on the bound object, each with an empty
tuple, answered with a set of corporation IDs and with 8. Each has the notice twice and the
two reads once.

**What was built.**

- The transport binds the office manager's Moniker by where the pilot is docked, keeps the
  corporations as the client does, and asks for the count each time (`pilots.js`,
  `stationOffices`; `retailCalls.js`). The corporation's own offices are still asked by name.
- `GET /api/bridge/station/offices` hands both to the page, asked in the lobby's order, for a
  pilot on the game port. In a structure no count is asked for. A pilot on the gateway is
  answered "not available", with nothing asked: the gateway's list has neither read.
- The station panel's Services tab has an Offices block: how many are rented and free, and
  the corporations by name. It lists them when the player presses its button, and from then
  on at each office rented or given up.
- A call the registry says the client sends with nothing is now counted as differing when it
  carries a keyword, not only an argument. That reaches the four planet reads too.

**Proof.**

- Tests watched to fail on the code as it was, all 18: 3 of the transport, 1 of the registry
  (run against the registry of the commit before), 5 of the route, 4 of the page's flow, 5 of
  the panel as it renders.
- 69 ways of breaking it were tried, and all were caught: 65 in one pass, and after the last
  change the flow's 5 again with 4 more. Before the pass I took out two checks that could not
  matter and added two cases (a keyword beside the read; one structure to another).
- Suite: 9988 tests, 9964 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Three in Jita: the route read three times. The
  server's log has one `MachoResolveObject`, one `MachoBindObject`, and `GetEmptyOfficeCount`
  three times on the object bound; the corporations rode the bind and were not asked again;
  nothing by name; no `[PKT] ERR`. Seven corporations, 17 free. As Test Two in Muvolailen: one
  corporation, 23 free. Through the gateway BFF: "not available", and nothing asked.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** from a staged start (below): Test Two online in Jita
  by the page's own buttons, Inventory & Ship open on Station services. The Offices block
  read "Not listed yet". Its button pressed, it read "7 rented · 17 free" over seven names in
  order, Elysian Industries among them. A script on a session of its own, as Test Three, gave
  up the corporation's office and twelve seconds later rented it again. With no button
  pressed the page went to "6 rented · 18 free" without Elysian Industries, and back to seven
  and 17, each within 0.3 s of the call that caused it.
- **A difference found in that check, and closed.** At each of those two changes the page's
  session asked for the free offices twice, where the recordings have it once: the server
  tells the change twice, and the page listed at each telling. The client's panel does not
  load again while it is loading. The page now lists one at a time. Run again from the same
  start, the server's log has, for each change, the corporations once and the count once.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, both 20
  identical, 14 tolerated.
- **The staging, and its undoing.** The store was saved. Test Two was moved to Jita with the
  GM's `/tr`. Test Three gave its corporation 30,001 ISK in two gifts, and gave up and rented
  the office twice, at 10,000 a time. After the check the store was put back (the same as the
  copy), and read again: Test Two is in Muvolailen, and Jita has its seven offices and 17
  free. The copy is deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it. The page was logged out by its
  own button, and the pane is back to its own size.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The page lists the offices when asked, not at docking.** The client lists them when its
  Offices tab is shown. Listing them with the panel would ask at every docking what a client
  asks only when someone looks.
- **A notice during a listing lists nothing more,** as in the client. Two changes close
  together can leave the block one change behind until the next notice or press.
- **A gateway pilot sees "This pilot's connection does not carry a station's offices".**
- **The corporations are sorted by name on the page** (the client sorts their names in lower
  case), and by ID in the route's answer, a set having no order.
- **`officeManager` is now a service whose calls go to the station's object on the game
  port,** all but the corporation's own offices. `officeManager.RentOffice`, which the
  gateway's list has, would go there too, as the client sends it. No route sends it.

**For the operator.**

- **eve.js `main` was pushed to origin at 21:14 on 2026-10-09, local time, not by me.** It is
  level with origin, at `3cdc14973`.
- **The page is handed 322 KB for one yes or no.** At every load of the station panel it asks
  the BFF for `map.GetStationInfo`, and reads from the answer only whether it came as the
  cached envelope. On the game port the BFF hands it the whole table of stations each time
  (321,917 characters of JSON, from the transport's cache), and the answer to the page's
  question is "no" there. Not changed; on the list.
- EveJS has an NPC corporation (1000002) with an office in Muvolailen's station.

**Not done.**

- The lobby's buttons: rent, give up, move the headquarters, release impounded items, and
  the reads behind them (`PrimeOfficeItem`, `HasCorpImpoundedItems`, `GetPriceQuote`).
- A structure's panel on the page has no Offices block.
- A structure's guests; `docs/game-port-login-calls.md` made again.

## 2026-10-10 — an office is rented and given up from the station panel, as the client's lobby does both

Commit `773e5bc`, pushed. Item 1's next: the lobby's buttons.

**What was missing.** The web client could not rent its corporation an office in a station, or
give one up. The panel listed a station's offices and had no button.

**What the client does** (`dockedUI/offices.py`, `officeManager.py`). The lobby loads its
buttons before its list. The rent button is there for a pilot whose session has the renting
role, where the corporation has no office in the station; the other for a director, where it
has one. Finding the corporation's office here primes the office's item once for the
station's Moniker (106); where there is none, a player's corporation is asked whether it has
items impounded (143). To rent, it asks the price for the session's corporation (114), asks
the player, and rents at that price (117). To give up, it asks the player and sends
`UnrentOffice()` (122).

**What the recordings have.** `GetPriceQuote(98838096)` on the station's object, answered the
long 100113; a question with that price and thirty days; `RentOffice(100113)`, answered None
after the server's two notices. `UnrentOffice()` with an empty tuple, answered None, also
after the two notices. After the notices the lobby asks, in order: the corporation's offices,
`PrimeOfficeItem` (rented) or `HasCorpImpoundedItems` (given up), the corporations with
offices, and the count free.

  the price for the pilot's corporation; the rent, with the price the player was shown; the
  giving up. Each for a pilot on the game port, docked in a station, with the role the

  shows the price and thirty days before "Rent it and pay"; "Give up the office" asks before
  "Give it up", and warns where the page's corporation hangar holds anything.

  there for the transport's object cache, as the client does.

## 2026-10-10 — a pilot chosen in a station has the lobby's reads asked as the client's lobby asks them

Commit `2304e88`, pushed. Item 1's next was the hangar's and the ship's lists. What was done
is the part of a docked login that stands before them, and the lists themselves are measured
and left: see "Not done".

**What was measured first.** `docs/game-port-login-calls.md` was made again from a bare login
on the game port. It read as it had: 29 kinds of call at login, 13 left to a feature, 10 to a
route, 48 never asked. Of the 13, four are the lobby's: the server's log of a retail client
logging in docked, with nothing opened, has `officeManager.GetMyCorporationsOffices`,
`stationSvc.GetStationItemBits`, `station.GetGuests` and `map.GetStationInfo`, each once. Its
log of a retail client logging in in space has none of the four. The game port asked them
only when the page showed a panel that wanted them.

**What the transport does now.** As a character is chosen in a station it asks the four, in
the order the retail log has them among themselves (`pilots.js`, `lobbyRead`). As a pilot
docks it asks the station's item and its guests, which the client has let go by then, and not
the other two, which the client has still. A pilot in space is asked none. Each is kept as its
own service keeps it (the last three iterations' work), so what the page reads of them after
is answered from what was kept. Each fails for itself.

**Proof.**

## 2026-10-10 — crimewatch is asked as the client's crimewatch service asks it, and what it answers is kept

Commit `a49fe22`, pushed. Item 1's next: crimewatch's two binds of a docked login.

**What the client does** (`crimewatchSvc.py`). It asks crimewatch for its states where a change
of session has the place or the character in it (94), and again where the pilot is in space and
the change has the system or the ship in it (116): the first for the combat timers, the
engagements and who is flagged, the second for the safety level. It asks for the pilot's own
security status while it has none (590), and from then on goes by what the server says of it
(598). Each asking is on a Moniker made for the call.

**What the logs have.** The server's own log of a retail client logging in docked has the
states once and the status once. Its log of one logging in in space has the states twice,
0.16 s apart, and the status once. Tranquility's recording of a docked login has both, each
riding a bind by `(stationID, 15)`.

**What was wrong.** The game port asked crimewatch nothing unless a route of the BFF's did, and
then every read made a Moniker and asked.

**What the transport does now.** It asks at the client's moments: at the choosing, and at every
change of session after it, by the same two rules. It keeps the states as last answered, and
lets them go at the server's word of a timer, a flag or an engagement (eleven notices) and at
the pilot's own safety level. It keeps the security status as the client does. A read of either
through the BFF, by name or on a Moniker's handle, is answered from what is kept.

**Proof.**

- 6 new tests of the transport and one written again. All 7 watched to fail on the code as it
  was.
- 58 tests of the transport failed when the choosing first made its two Monikers: they hold
  a session to the exact binds and objects a test causes. The stand-in session now
  lists and counts crimewatch's Monikers apart, as it already counted the corporation
  registry's, and those tests are as they were. Two tests were changed for what changed under
  them.
- 33 ways of breaking it were tried, and all were caught. Before the pass I took out three
  checks that could not matter and added two cases.
- **The pass left one breakage in the source, and I found it by looking.** I had put a time
  limit on the tool that was shorter than it needed; it was cut off mid-run and did not put
  the file back. The before-and-after comparison said the tree differed. I matched the source
  against the list of breakages, found the one, put the line back, confirmed the comparison
  and the tests, and ran the twelve left in three parts with no limit to cut them off.
- Suite: 10016 tests, 9992 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped. Run before the live checks
  and again after the last change.
- **A bare login on the game port,** Test Pilot, docked: the server's log has crimewatch's
  resolve and its two binds, the states and then the status, after the skill handler and
  before the corporation registry's bind, where the retail log has them. The report made
  again: 36 kinds of call at login where there were 34, 7 left to a feature where there were
  9.
- **A walk, by script, on the game port:** Test Pilot undocked through the BFF and docked
  again. The server's log has the states once at the choosing, twice at the undock (0.05 and
  0.06 s after the session's change), and once at the docking. No `[PKT] ERR`.
- **The BFF's crimewatch route read twice:** neither the states nor the status was asked
  again; its two other reads were, each on a Moniker of its own.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, both 20
  identical, 14 tolerated.
- The walk was staged and undone: the store saved before, put back after (the same as the
  copy), Test Pilot read docked in Jita again, the copy deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for
  it.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The states are let go at a notice, not changed by it.** The client works each timer, flag
  and engagement into what it holds. Here a read after one asks the server again: once more
  than the client, and never behind it.
- **Nothing of the page shows any of it.** The page has no safety level, no combat timers and
  no security status of its own. This unit is the transport's alone, and there was nothing to
  prove in a browser. The HUD's part is on the list.
- **The status is asked at the choosing, with the states.** The retail logs have it a second
  or so later; which of the client's windows asks it there I did not find.
- **The stand-in's separate list for crimewatch's Monikers** is a change to the tests' own
  stand-in, made so that 58 tests need not each be told of two binds they are not about. Their
  assertions are untouched.

**For the operator.** eve.js is as it was, level with origin at `3cdc14973`.

**Not done.**

- The safety level, the combat timers and the security status shown on the page.
- The ship's two binds of the same login (`GetDirtTimestamp(shipID)`, twice, on Tranquility):
  the hangar's dirt on the ship's model, which nothing of ours draws.
- The login's inventory, as the last entry has it.

## 2026-10-10 — the ship's safety level and the pilot's combat timers are on the workspace header

Commit `a23d67c`, pushed. Item 1's next: what the transport keeps of crimewatch, shown.

**What was missing.** The page said nothing of the ship's safety level or of a combat timer. A
decoder for crimewatch's states had been in the page since July with nothing reading it.

**What the client shows.** Its crimewatch service holds five timers (weapons, PvP, NPC,
criminal, disapproval), each a state and the time it ends, and the safety level. A timer's
state is its kind's idle state, one above it while its cause goes on, two above while it
counts down, three and more where it is inherited (`crimewatch/const.py`); the criminal's says
criminal or suspect by its state. The HUD has the safety button in space, and the timers
wherever the pilot is.

**What was built.**

- `GET /api/bridge/crimewatch`: crimewatch's states as they came, with the BFF's clock beside
  them. One call on the pilot's own session, on either transport.
- The page reads it as a pilot comes online, at each of the eleven notices of a timer, a flag
  or an engagement, and at each change of place, system or ship.
- The workspace header says "Safety Full", "Partial" or "None" in space, and each running
  timer anywhere: "Weapons 0:42", "PvP 14:20", "Suspect", counted down once a second to the
  server's clock (`web/src/space/crimewatch.ts`).

**Proof.**

- 17 new tests: 6 of the module that reads the states, 2 of the route, 5 of the page's flow, 4
  of the header as it renders. Watched to fail on the code as it was: the route's 2, the
  header's 3 of 4 (the fourth, that nothing is said docked or before a read, held before as
  after), and the flow's 5, run against the commit before. Not seen to fail: the module's 6,
  written with it.
- 42 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time, and all were caught. Before the
  pass I took out two checks that could not matter and added two cases.
- Suite: 10033 tests, 10009 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** from a store saved first: Test Pilot online by the
  page's own buttons, docked. The header read "Docked" and nothing of safety. Its Undock button
  pressed: 1.7 s later the header read "In Space" and "Safety Full". Its Dock button pressed:
  the header read "Docked" again, and the safety level was gone. The server's log of that time
  has crimewatch asked its states four times: once at the choosing, twice at the undock, once
  at the docking. That is the client's own count; the page's reads added none. No `[PKT]
  ERR`.
- **By script, on the committed code:** the route read three times on the game port, the
  states asked of the server once; on the gateway's BFF the route answers in the same form.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, both 20
  identical, 14 tolerated. (Run before the mistake below, on BFFs started from the same text
  the commit has.)
- The store was put back after (the same as the copy), Test Pilot read docked in Jita, the
  copy deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it. The page was logged out by its own button,
  and the pane is back to its own size.

**A mistake of mine, and how it was put right.** To see the flow's tests fail on the code as
it was, I put seven source files back to the commit before and ran them. That is safe on
work that is committed. This work was not: the files I overwrote held the whole of the page's
part, and `git checkout` gave back the commit's, not mine. Nothing had been lost from the
scratch folder: every change had been made by a script kept there. I applied the scripts
again to the seven files, and added the two import lines I had put in by hand. Then I checked
the result four ways: the typecheck; every text the breakage list looks for found in the
sources exactly once (30 of 30); the page built again and its 35 files compared with the ones
built before the loss, each the same byte for byte; and the whole suite. The commit is that
tree.

**Not seen.** A timer running, and its countdown ticking, in the browser: starting one takes a
fight, and I have no way to stage one safely. They are tested on states in the server's own
form with the client's own state numbers, and on nothing live.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The safety level is said in space only,** as the client's button is on the ship's HUD.
- **The words are mine,** the timers' and the levels'. The client draws dials.
- **A timer is counted to the BFF's clock at the read,** which is the server's machine's.
- **A timer counting down to a time already past is not shown.** The server has not said it is
  over; there is nothing left of it to show.
- **The page reads again at any change of place, system or ship,** docked or not. The client
  asks at a change of ship only in space. On the game port the extra read is answered from
  what is kept.
- **The safety level cannot be set from the page yet.**

**Not done.**

- The safety level set from the page (`SetSafetyLevel`, on the BFF's list of writes with no
  route).
- The notices worked into what the transport keeps, as the client works them: today a read
  after a notice asks the server once.
- Who is flagged, and the engagements, shown.

## 2026-10-10 — the ship's safety level is set from the workspace header, and kept as the client keeps it

Commit `7671d31`, pushed. Item 1's next: crimewatch's rest, the first of it.

**What was missing.** The header said the safety level and could not change it. And where it was
changed (the route was there since the plumbing sweep), the transport let go of everything
crimewatch had said, so that the next read asked the server its states again: a call the
client never makes after a set.

**What the client does.** No recording on Tranquility has `SetSafetyLevel` (every folder
searched), so this is from the code and its seven callers.

- `crimewatchSvc.SetSafetyLevel(level)` (342): the one level, on crimewatch's Moniker; then
  the service has that level as its own and tells the button. It asks nothing after. A refusal
  is raised before the line that keeps the level.
- The HUD's button (`shipSafetyButton.py`) opens a selector of three: None, Partial, Full.
  A press on a level lower than the one now puts a confirm button beside it, and until that is
  pressed or gone no other button answers. Any other press sets at once, the level now among
  them. When the level changes, the selector closes.
- Held at Full (`IsSafetyLockedToFullLevel`, 148): in space, in a system of the safest class
  of security (0.95 and above), or while a structure is controlled in high security. Then the
  level the service has is Full whatever the server said (`_UpdateSafetyLevel`), and the two
  other buttons are locked.
- For an alpha clone in high security the None button is locked (`IsSafetyAlphaLocked`).

**What was built.**

- The transport: once the server has taken a level, it is put in the fourth place of the
  states kept, and nothing is asked (`pilots.js`, `safetyLevelSet`; `keptReads.js` learnt to
  amend what it keeps, behind any read begun before). A refused set changes nothing kept.
- The route (`POST /api/bridge/safety/set-level`): what is not 0, 1 or 2 is refused
  (`INVALID_SAFETY_LEVEL`). It used to be sent as Full, and the page would have gone on
  believing it had set what it asked for.
- The page: the header's safety badge is a button in space. It opens the selector: the three
  levels, the one now marked, each with a line of what it lets the ship do. A lower level
  wants "Confirm" (with a "Cancel" beside it); a higher one is set at once. The level set is
  the level shown, with nothing read after. In a system of the safest class the header says
  Full and the other two cannot be pressed (`web/src/ui/SafetyChooser.svelte`,
  `SafetyMenu.svelte`, `web/src/space/crimewatch.ts`).

**Proof.**

- 16 new tests and 2 changed: 2 of what is kept and amended, 2 of the transport (and its test
  of the notices, which had the old forgetting in it), 1 of the route, 4 of the selector's
  rules, 3 of the page's flow, 4 of the header and the selector as they render (and the
  header's test of the level's word, which reads a button now). Seen to fail on the commit
  before, after this one was made: 11 (what is kept, 2; the transport, 3; the route, 1; the
  flow, 3; the header, 2). Not seen to fail: the selector's rules (4) and the selector as it
  renders (3), written with what they test.
- 70 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time, and all were caught. The
  chooser's were tried again after it was made a popover. The two new files are not seen by
  `git diff --stat`: each was compared with its copy in the scratch folder after each pass.
- Suite, before the live check and again on the tree that was committed: 10049 tests, 10025
  pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Two, docked: read Full; set Partial; three reads
  said Partial; a level of 5, of `"1"` and of none were each refused, and one unconfirmed;
  after a logout and a fresh login the server said Partial; set Full again. The server's log
  of those 0.3 s: at each login crimewatch asked its states once and the status once, and one
  bind for each set. Six reads of the route, and the states asked of the server twice, once at
  each login. No `[PKT] ERR`. The same script through the gateway's BFF printed the same lines.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** from a store saved first, Test Pilot online by the
  page's own buttons. Docked, the header had no safety button. Undock pressed: "In Space" and
  a button "Safety Full". Pressed: the selector, None, Partial and Full, Full marked.
  Partial pressed: "Confirm Partial" and "Cancel" beside it, all three levels unpressable, and
  the header still Full. Cancel pressed: the three pressable again. Partial and then Confirm
  Partial pressed: the header read "Safety Partial" and the selector was shut. Opened again,
  Partial was marked; Full pressed: "Safety Full" at once, with no confirming. The server's
  log has one bind of crimewatch at each of the two sets (03:40:45.653 and 03:40:55.950 UTC)
  and none between the first press of Partial and the confirming of it; no states asked after
  either. The page's own requests: two posts to the route, both 200, and no read of
  `/api/bridge/crimewatch` after them.
- **A fault the live check found.** The selector first opened underneath the page's floating
  windows: at three points of it, another window was the thing on top. Those windows are in a
  layer above the whole workspace, and nothing in the header can be raised over them. The
  selector is now a popover of the browser's, in its top layer; at the same three points it
  was the thing on top.
- Then, with the selector left open, Dock pressed: the header read "Docked", the button and
  the selector were gone, and nothing was thrown. Undock pressed again: the button was back
  and the selector shut. The header asked the map for the system's security once
  (`POST /api/map/security`). No `[PKT] ERR` in the server's log of those nine minutes.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, both 20
  identical, 14 tolerated.
- The store was put back after (the same as the copy), Test Pilot read docked in Jita, the copy deleted. EveJS was restarted twice for it. The
  page was logged out by its own button, and the pane is back to its own size.

**A claim of mine taken back.** The last entry said `SetSafetyLevel` was "on the BFF's list of
writes with no route". It had a route, `/api/bridge/safety/set-level`, from the plumbing
sweep; nothing of the page called it. I had not searched `src/server.js` for the method.

**Not seen.**

- The level held at Full, live. No system of this server's data is in the safest class: the
  highest of 5334 is 0.949794, and the systems that were 1.0 are 0.949 in it. The rule is
  tested on a made-up security of 1 and on the class's edge. Whether the client's own table
  (`res:/staticdata/systems.static`) has any at 0.95 or above was not read.
- The selector shut by a press elsewhere, or by Escape: that is the browser's own doing for a
  popover, and a script's click does not set it off.
- A refusal said in the selector. It is rendered in a test.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The selector is a popover of the browser's** (`popover="auto"`), so that it closes on a
  press elsewhere as the client's does on losing the keyboard, and is over every window.
- **A "Cancel" beside "Confirm".** The client's confirm button goes away when it loses the
  keyboard; a page says how to let it go.
- **Each level has a line saying what it lets the ship do.** The words are mine. The client
  says it in a paragraph above the buttons and in hints.
- **What is no level is refused by the route,** where it was sent as Full before.
- **A system whose security the page has not read yet holds nothing.** The client always knows
  it. The page asks for it as the pilot enters space, once.
- **The None level is not locked for an alpha clone.** That wants the clone's grade, which the
  client asks once at login (`subscriptionMgr.GetCloneGrade`) and nothing of ours asks.

**Not done.**

- The alpha clone's lock, and `subscriptionMgr.GetCloneGrade` at login.
- The level held at Full while a structure is controlled: the page controls none.
- The map's security set beside the client's own table.
- The notices worked into what the transport keeps; who is flagged, and the engagements, shown.

## 2026-10-10 — crimewatch's notices are worked into what the transport keeps, and a timer was seen running

Commit `8daaba5`, pushed. Item 1's next: crimewatch's rest, the notices.

**What was missing.** At each of crimewatch's eleven notices the transport let go of the states
it kept, and the next read asked the server again: a call the client never makes after a
notice. And no timer had ever been seen counting on the page, for want of a safe way to start
one.

**What the client does** (`crimewatchSvc.py` 222 to 288; the two notices Tranquility's
recordings have were read first, in every folder).

- Each of the five timers' notices carries `(state, expiryTime)`, and the service has that
  timer in that state from then on. Recorded: `OnNpcTimerUpdate` in 17 files, 86 times, by
  `charid`, as `(400, None)`, `(401, None)` and `(402, a long)`.
- `OnSystemCriminalFlagUpdates(newIdles, newSuspects, newCriminals)`: the idle are flagged no
  more, then each criminal is a criminal, then each suspect a suspect. Recorded in 6 files, 9
  times, by `solarsystemid2`, each of the three a `set`.
- The engagements' four set, re-time, leave open or take out the entry of the other pilot.
- `OnSystemDisapprovalFlagUpdates` changes who is disapproved of, which the states do not say.
- After none of them is the server asked anything.

**What was built.** `src/gamePort/crimewatchStates.js`: the states a notice leaves, in the
form they came in. The transport amends what it keeps with it at each notice and asks
nothing. States or a notice in a form it does not read are let go, and the next read asks:
never behind the client, as before. `keptReads.js`: an amendment that makes nothing of what is
kept, or that fails, lets that one answer go and fails for nobody (an amendment nobody waits
for must not be able to end the BFF). The page is as it was: it reads the route at each
notice, and on the game port the route now answers from what is kept.

**Proof.**

- 10 new tests and 2 changed: 7 of the module, 1 of what is kept, 2 of the transport (and
  its test of the old letting go, which now holds states that are not read; and one line of
  the safety level's test). The module's "walk" is this server's own: fourteen notices as
  they came, and after each the server's own answer to compare with. Seen to fail on the
  commit before, after this one was made: 4 (what is kept, 1; the transport, 3). Not seen to
  fail: the module's 7, written with it.
- 49 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time, and all were caught. The new
  file and its tests were compared with their copies after each pass.
- Suite, before the live check: 10059 tests, 10035 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24
  skipped.
- **A safe way to start a timer:** the GM's `/cwatch <npc|weapon|pvp|suspect|disapproval>
  <seconds>` and `/cwatch clear`, in space. Docked, the server sets the timer and tells the
  pilot nothing.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Two, from a store saved first: undock; an NPC, a
  weapons and a PvP timer of a few seconds; each run out; a suspect's flag and a disapproval;
  both run out; dock. The same walk was made on the code before and on this. Printed after
  each step: the notices that had come and what the crimewatch route said. The two printouts
  are the same line for line (38 lines, the times aside): the states the transport amends are
  the states the server answered when it was asked each time. The server's log: on the code
  before, crimewatch asked its states 13 times in that walk; on this, 4 (the choosing, the
  undock's two, the docking). No `[PKT] ERR`.
- **In the browser, on the game port,** Test Pilot online by the page's own buttons and
  undocked by the header's. `/cwatch npc 40` sent from the page's own session at 04:03:40
  UTC: 3.6 s later the header read "NPC 0:37", and 5 s after that "NPC 0:32". With weapons,
  PvP and a suspect's flag added: "Weapons 0:20", "PvP 0:25", "NPC 0:23", "Suspect 0:12", and
  4 s later 0:16, 0:21, 0:19 and 0:08. Then each left the header as it ran out, the suspect's
  first, and the header read "In Space" and "Safety Full" alone. The server's log of it:
  states asked 3 times (the choosing, the undock's two) and none through ten notices. No
  `[PKT] ERR`. Dock pressed: "Docked", and the
  states asked once more, for the docking.
- **On both transports, by script:** two passes of the parity tool as Test Two, both 20
  identical, 14 tolerated.
- The store was put back after (the same as the copy), Test Pilot and Test Two read docked where they were, the copy deleted.
  EveJS was restarted twice for it. The page was logged out by its own button, and the pane
  is back to its own size.

**This server beside Tranquility.** The timers' notices are as recorded: `(state, expiry)` by
`charid`, the expiry a long or None. The flags' notice is by `solarsystemid2` as recorded, and
its three are tuples where Tranquility sends three sets. The client reads either. Added to
the list for a sub-agent (item 60), with two things nothing of ours shows the truth of: who is
disapproved of and the engagements go by `clientID` (no recording has either), and a docked
pilot is told nothing of its timers.

**Measured, not explained.** The GM command's own reply says more seconds than it was given
("NPC 53s" for 40, "NPC 14s" for 5). The timer in the notice ended when it was asked to: the
page counted 40 s, and the idle notice came 5 s after the 5.

**Not seen.**

- An engagement's notices, live: an engagement takes two pilots and a duel. They are tested
  on made-up pilots and times in the notices' form as the client's handlers take them.
- A notice the module could not read, live. None came.
- A timer whose cause goes on (`(401, None)`), live: the GM's command sets counting ones.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The page still reads the route at each notice,** and does not work the notice into its
  own store. On the game port that read is answered from what is kept, and the server sees
  nothing; on the gateway it is how the page learns of the change at all.
- **Who stays flagged keeps its place in the set, and the new come after.** A set has no
  order; this one is written as a list on the wire, and something has to be chosen.
- **A notice in a form that is not read lets the states go,** rather than leaving them as
  they were. The client's handler would raise and keep what it had; a read after it here
  asks the server.
- **The suspect's flag was set at Jita's undock** for the browser check, the pilot being
  there. It ran twelve seconds. Nothing shot at the ship. A criminal's was not tried.

**Not done.**

- Who is flagged, and the engagements, shown on the page.
- The states told to the page by the notice itself, with no read of the route.

## 2026-10-10 — the clone's grade is asked at login as the client asks it, and None is locked for an alpha clone

Commit `ee253d3`, pushed. Item 1's next: one of the 47 kinds nothing of ours asked, and the lock
that wanted it.

**What was missing.** The retail client asks its account's clone grade as it logs in. Nothing
of ours asked it, so the page could not know an alpha clone from an omega, and the safety
selector let an alpha press None in high security, which the client's does not.

**What the client does.** No recording on Tranquility has `GetCloneGrade` (every folder
searched; the recordings begin after the login). This server's log of a retail client's login
has it, as the call before the character selection's first.

- `gameui.OnSessionChanged` (449): with `userid` in the change, the clone grade service is
  primed: `sm.RemoteSvc('subscriptionMgr').GetCloneGrade()`, by the service's name and with
  nothing (`clone_grade_svc.py` 125). It is kept, and asked again only where there is none
  (113).
- `OnSubscriptionChangedServer(new_state)` (243): the grade is what the notice says.
- The grade is 0, an alpha clone's, or 1, an omega's (`clonegrade/const.py`).
- `crimewatchSvc.IsSafetyAlphaLocked` (162): an alpha clone in a system of high security or
  above. Then the selector's None button is locked (`SecurityButton.IsAlphaLockedAndRed`),
  and nothing else is. Held at Full comes first where both are so.

**What was built.**

- The transport asks the grade once the account is on the session, before the selection's
  three calls, and keeps it; the notice changes it; a read of it with nothing is answered
  from what is kept. A grade that could not be read does not fail the choosing, and is asked
  for when it is next wanted. The pair is on the game port's own list: the gateway's has no
  call of the subscription manager's.
- `GET /api/bridge/clone-grade`: `{available, cloneGrade}`. A gateway pilot is answered
  `available: false`, with nothing asked.
- The page reads it once as a pilot comes online (`store.station.cloneGrade`) and takes the
  notice's word after. The safety selector goes by it: for an alpha clone in high security
  None cannot be pressed, and a line says why (`safetyLocks`, `SafetyMenu.svelte`).

**Proof.**

- 10 new tests and 6 changed: 2 of the transport, 2 of the route, 1 of the grade itself, 1 of
  the lock's rule, 2 of the page's flow, 2 of the selector and the header as they render;
  changed, the registry's list of the game port's own pairs, the transport's tally, and four
  of the selector's that are handed the two locks now. Seen to fail on the commit before,
  after this one was made: 8 (the transport, 3; the route, 2; the flow, 2; the registry, 1).
  Not seen to fail: the grade's own, the lock's rule and the two renders, written with what
  they test.
- 47 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time, and all were caught.
- Suite, before the live check: 10069 tests, 10045 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **By script, on the game port,** as Test Two: the server's log has `subscriptionMgr
  GetCloneGrade()` as call 7 of the pilot's session, answered 1, and `GetCharacterSelectionData`
  as call 8. The route read three times said `{available: true, cloneGrade: 1}` each time, and
  the grade was asked of the server once. Through the gateway's BFF the route said
  `{available: false, cloneGrade: null}` three times.
- **The login's report made again** (`docs/game-port-login-calls.md`): at login 37 kinds (it
  was 36), never 46 (it was 47). Three lines of it changed.
- **In the browser, on the game port, as an alpha clone,** from a store saved first and the
  server started with `EVE_CLONE_GRADE=alpha`: the route said `cloneGrade: 0`. Test Pilot
  online by the page's own buttons and undocked in Jita, a system of high security. The

**Not seen.**

## 2026-10-10 — the plan's cutover begun: what the BFF still asks the web gateway, tallied

Commit `99c3c5b`, pushed. Not from the Next list: from the plan.

**Why this, and not the next of item 1.** The brief says to take the next unit from the log's
"Next", or failing that the earliest unfinished "done when" in the plan. Next had sixty-one
items, every one of them about a feature making the client's calls, and none of the plan's two
unfinished phases: the cutover (Phase 5: "the only gateway routes the BFF calls are the
account-level ones") and the one WebSocket (Phase 6). Both are conditions of "done", and by the
rule as written neither would ever have been reached. Phase 5 was last mentioned in this log
on 2026-10-08. So the plan was read again, and the cutover begun where it has to begin: with
a measure of it.

**What was missing.** Nothing said what the BFF asks the web gateway. The parity tool counts
gateway sessions for one pilot in the server's log; the calls the BFF makes with no session
held, and its account-level reads, were counted nowhere.

**What was built.**

- `src/gatewayLedger.js`: a tally of every call made on the gateway client, by the client's
  function; for a call or a bind by pair and whether a session the gateway holds was named;
  for a read of one character, whether that character was online on the BFF then. Each row is
  classed against the plan's 2.3: a held pilot's own, a call as a pilot not logged in,
  account-level, a read of an online pilot that the plan keeps for offline ones, a route the
  plan does not keep, the chat edge.
- The gateway client counts itself (`eveGatewayClient.gatewayLedger`), beneath the seam that
  sends a pilot to its transport, so the store's reads are counted too and a pilot on the game
  port leaves no row of its own. `app.locals.gatewayLedger` is the same tally. A test's
  stand-in for the gateway has none.
- `scripts/gateway-ledger-report.js` writes a walk's tally as
  `docs/game-port-gateway-ledger.md`, with one line saying what still stands before the
  cutover. The check BFFs write the tally to `gateway-ledger.json` in their data folders.

**The first measure.** The parity tool's 34 routes as Test Two through each BFF; then, on the
game-port BFF, Test Pilot in the browser: online by the page's own buttons with the 25 windows
the page opened again, undocked and docked by the header's.

| | The gateway BFF (the 34 routes) | The game-port BFF (the 34 routes, and the browser's walk) |
|---|---|---|
| A held pilot's own | 100 rows, 147 calls | none |
| A read of an online pilot | `/skills`, once | none |
| A route the plan does not keep | `/snapshot`, twice (one of an online pilot) | `/snapshot`, 6 times, each of a pilot not online |
| A call as a pilot not logged in | none | none |
| Account-level | 9 calls | 93 calls: `/account` 49, `/characters` 22, `/status` 12, `/skills` 8 (each of a pilot not online), `/character-status` 2 |
| The chat edge | 1 | 2 |

For a pilot on the game port, then, through a login with every window open, an undock and a
docking: nothing of the pilot's own goes to the web gateway. What stands in the report is the
`/snapshot` read, which the plan's list of what stays does not name.

## 2026-10-10 — the cutover's first three steps: the snapshot and the skills read where they are asked, and the calls made as a pilot not logged in

Commit `1261c13`, pushed. Next's head: steps (a), (b) and (c) of Phase 5.

**(a) The snapshot.** Five call sites, each read.

| Asked by | Of whom |
|---|---|
| The select's check that the account owns the character (`eveStore.getCharacterForAccount`); the structure searches use the same check for a pilot chosen there | a pilot about to be chosen, or named and not held |
| `/api/roster/planets`, `/api/roster/stock` | each pilot a planetary board lists, online or not |
| The customs haul's plan (`src/server.js`, by the pilot hauled for) | that pilot, before anybody is logged in for it |
| `/api/bridge/planets`, the gateway's branch | the held pilot, when it is the gateway's |

All but the last are of pilots the retail protocol cannot be asked of: it sees only the
character logged in. The last is a held pilot's own panel, and on the game port that route
reads the colonies as the client does and never reaches the snapshot.

**(b) The skills.** `skillSheetFor` is the held pilot's sheet: on the game port made from what
the transport keeps of the skill handler's answers, on the gateway `/skills`. That is the one
read of an online pilot the gateway BFF's tally had. The other askers are a roster's board
(`/api/roster/training`, `/api/roster/planets`), mining preparation, and the training queue's
review and read: each of a pilot of the account that nobody need be flying.

**(c) The calls made as a pilot who is not logged in.** Every place the BFF calls or binds
through the seam was read (27 places; a call goes to the web gateway whenever it names no
session). Those that name none are the plan's list of 2.3 and nothing else: the structure
directory's checks and names, the fleet's parking and delivery checks, a training pilot's
corporation fittings, the corporation's reads in training onboarding and settings, and the
generic route's and the account's own calls where the seam sends them to the gateway.

**What was changed.** The tally counts the snapshot as it counts the skills: account-level for
a pilot who is not online, a read of an online pilot otherwise. The plan's 2.3 names it. No
route was changed: nothing read asked the wrong thing.

**The measure, again,** from a store saved first and both check BFFs started fresh: the parity
tool's 34 routes as Test Two; five reads asked by script with no pilot chosen (the structure
search, the training settings, two roster boards, and the generic route twice); then Test
Pilot in the browser with 25 windows open, undocked and docked again.

| A read of an online pilot | 2 (`/skills`, `/snapshot`) | none |
| A route the plan does not keep | none | none |
| A call as a pilot not logged in | none | 6: `corpRegistry.GetMember` 3, `GetCorporation` 2, `config.GetMultiOwnersEx` 1 |

The report (`docs/game-port-gateway-ledger.md`) is of the game-port BFF's. It says one thing

## 2026-10-10 — the cutover's step (d): hosted bots on the game port, and a rock no bot there could see

Commit `428af02`, pushed. Next's head: step (d) of Phase 5.

**The measure.** Three saved bots run on the server for pilots on the game port, from a store
saved first, each started by the page's own start (`web/src/bots/startRun.ts`) from a script
that printed the approval the page asks for: "Safe return home" and "Dock, refit, and repair"
as Test Pilot, "Mine and haul cycle" as Test Two through an undock and four warps. The
gateway's tally after them: nothing of a pilot's own, no read of an online pilot, no call as a
pilot not logged in; 79 account-level calls. The server's log of those four minutes: 378 calls
on the game port, no gateway session, no `[PKT] ERR`. The report
(`docs/game-port-gateway-ledger.md`) is of that walk and the last one together.

**What the measure found.** The mining bot said "Belt empty" at each of four belts and went on
to the next. The same bot as the same pilot through the gateway's BFF, from the same store:
"Approaching a rock", then "Locking on". A bot knows something to mine by the mining fields of
its row in the space snapshot (`isMineableRock`: what it yields, or its belt). The gateway puts
those on an asteroid's row from the server's own scene. The game port's snapshot, made from
our own ballpark, had neither: every rock was there, as an asteroid, and none was something to
mine. Mining was not possible for a pilot on the game port, by a bot or by the page's own
loop. No test had a rock in it, and every live check in space had been at a station or a gate.

**What a client knows of a rock.** Its slim item: a type, a group, the Asteroid category, a
name. The type is the ore: this server stamps an asteroid's slim item with the type it yields,
whatever it is drawn as (`asteroidService.js`, `miningResourceSiteService.js`,
`miningRuntimeState.js`: `slimTypeID` and `miningYieldTypeID` are set from the same record in
each). Which belt a rock belongs to is not sent. How much is left is not in the ballpark: the
client learns it from a survey scan.

**What was built.** The game port's row for an asteroid says `miningYieldTypeID` (its own
type), and `beltID` and `remainingQuantity` as null, which the bots read as "not known"
(`src/gamePort/spaceProjection.js`).

**Proof.**

- 1 new test, with a real rock's values (one of the 121 at that belt), seen to fail on the
  commit before. 7 ways of breaking the change were tried, and all were caught.
- Suite: 10078 tests, 10054 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **The same bot again, on the game port:** "Leaving the station", "Flying to the belt", "In
  warp", "Approaching a rock", "Locking on", "Approaching a rock": the phases the gateway's run
  went through. Left to run on: "Heading home", a warp, and paused with "No mining equipment
  was found fitted to this ship", which is so (Test Two flies a Badger). The server's log of
  that run: two warps, an orbit, a target added, a docking, each a packet on the game port;
  196 calls, no gateway session, no `[PKT] ERR`.
- **Every rock, on both transports.** With Test Two left at the belt, the space snapshot read
  through each BFF in turn: 121 asteroids each, and for every one the same ID, type, group,
  what it yields, its grade and its family, the two lists equal byte for byte. The gateway's
  rows had a belt and a quantity besides (`40176404`, `160000`); the game port's have null.
- The store was put back after each run (five saves and restores in all, each the same as its
  copy), the copies deleted, both pilots docked where they were.

**Not seen.**

- A laser cycling on a rock for a bot on the game port: the pilot's ship has none. It wants a
  ship staged with one fitted.
- A gas cloud. Its group is in the Celestial category, and the game port's row calls it a
  celestial; what the gateway calls it was not looked at.
- "Dock, refit, and repair" past its second step: it paused for a saved fitting to be picked,
  on either transport, and was stopped.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **I approved three bots' runs** from a script, reading each prompt first: two that "may
  spend or commit ISK; move, consume, or expose items", one that may "move, consume, or expose
  items", each for fifteen minutes, on test pilots, from a saved store.
- **What is left in a rock is "not known" on the game port** until a survey scan says, and its
  belt is never known. The bots choose among rocks without either. A number made up from the
  rock's radius would be the client's own guess, and was not made.
- **The default's change waits.** This was the measure it was waiting on, and it found mining
  broken. One more thing of that size may be there: before the default changes, a mining ship
  is to be staged and a bot left to fill its hold on the game port.

**For the operator.**

- As before: the default's change to `gameport` is the next step of the plan, and I will make
  it when a bot has mined on the game port. `EVEJS_PILOT_TRANSPORT=gateway` undoes it.
- eve.js is as it was, level with origin at `3cdc14973`.

## 2026-10-10 — a bot mines on the game port as it does through the gateway, and three more things its snapshot does not say

No commit of code: a measure, and a reading. Next's head: step (d) of Phase 5, the rest.

**The measure.** From a store saved first, a Venture was staged for Test Two through the
game-port BFF's own routes (the GM's `/giveitem`, the boarding, two Miner I and an afterburner
fitted), and that state saved too. "Mine and haul cycle" was then run on the server for five
and a half minutes on each transport in turn, each from the staged state.

| | The game port | The gateway |
|---|---|---|
| The bot's phases | Leaving the station, Flying to the belt, In warp, Approaching a rock, Locking on, Approaching a rock, Mining | the same, in the same order |
| From start to the first "Mining" | 52 s | 50 s |
| Mining until it was stopped | 279 s | 281 s |
| In the ore hold after | 8692 Veldspar III-Grade, 869.2 of 5000 m³ | 8690, 869 of 5000 m³ |

The server's log of the game port's run: 402 calls on the game port, the two lasers' `Activate`,
one `AddTarget`, an orbit and a warp, no gateway session, no `[PKT] ERR`. Mining by a hosted
bot works on the game port, and to within two units of ore in 8692.

**The reading.** The rock was a field the gateway's row has and ours had not. So the two row
makers were set side by side, field by field (`projectSpaceEntity` in the gateway's runtime,
`projectEntity` in `src/gamePort/spaceProjection.js`):

| Row | The gateway says | The game port says | Who reads it in the page |
|---|---|---|---|
| a drone | `controllerID`, `controllerOwnerID`, `droneActivity`, `targetEntityID` | none of the four | the Drones panel, the overview, the mining bot: whether a drone in space is this ship's |
| a ship | `npcEntityType`: "npc", "concord" or "drifter" | null, always | the overview, the tactical view, a ship's stance, the fleet's companions |
| a ship | `compressionFacility`: its range and type lists | null, always | the mining bots' compression step |
| a ship | `capacitorRatio` of another's ship | null | (a client is not sent another ship's capacitor) |
| an asteroid | `miningYieldTypeID`, `beltID`, `remainingQuantity` | the first, since `428af02` | the mining bots, the overview |

The first three are gaps like the rock's. A retail client is told each another way: a drone's
controller, activity and target by the drone service's notices; what an NPC is by its type's
group and its owner; a compression facility by its slim item
(`compression_facility_typelists`). None of them is built here yet.

**Proof.** The two runs above, live. The store was put back after (the same as the copy), both
copies deleted, both pilots docked where they were. Nothing of the repository was changed.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The default's change waits for those three.** I said it would be made when a bot had
  mined on the game port. It has, and the reading that followed found three more things a
  pilot on the game port cannot do as one on the gateway can. Each is a step now, and the
  default changes after them.
- **The audit was by reading the two row makers,** not by a walk: a walk finds what it happens
  to pass, and nothing had passed a drone.

**For the operator.**

- eve.js is as it was, level with origin at `3cdc14973`.


### Next

**First, the plan's own next phase: the cutover (Phase 5).** Its measure is the tally of what the BFF asks the
web gateway (`docs/game-port-gateway-ledger.md`; a check BFF writes `gateway-ledger.json` in its data folder).
In this order:

- (a), (b), (c): done 2026-10-10 (the snapshot's and the skills' call sites read; every unheld call found to
  be one the plan names). Left of (c): the structure directory's reads, a fleet's parking and delivery
  checks and a training pilot's corporation fittings made live, each wanting something staged (a structure,
  a mining operation, a training corporation's fittings);
- (c2) the generic route with no pilot held: for an account on the game port, what is not the selection
  screen's is refused by the BFF itself, by the list the gateway refuses it by today, and no longer sent
  to the web gateway (the plan's second open question; recommended in the log, and to be done with (e));
- (d) 2026-10-10: three hosted bots walked on the game port with the tally clean; a rock made something a
  bot there can see; and a bot seen to mine on the game port as through the gateway (8692 units against
  8690). The two transports' rows for a thing in space were then read side by side, and three gaps like the
  rock's found. Each is a step, in this order, each with what a retail client is told found first (the
  recordings, then the decompiled client), built into `src/gamePort/spaceProjection.js` or what feeds it,
  and seen live on both transports side by side:
  - (d1) a drone's row: whose it is and what it is doing (`controllerID`, `controllerOwnerID`,
    `droneActivity`, `targetEntityID`), which the client has from its drone service's notices. The Drones
    panel, the overview and the mining bot read them;
  - (d2) what kind of NPC a ship is (`npcEntityType`: a pirate, CONCORD, a drifter), which the client tells
    from the type's group and its owner. The overview, the tactical view, a ship's stance and the fleet's
    companions read it;
  - (d3) a ship that is a compression facility (`compressionFacility`), which the client has from the slim
    item's `compression_facility_typelists`. The mining bots' compression step reads it;
  - then a gas cloud's row on each transport, the fleet's companions, the Factory and the training flows;
- (e) then, after (d1) to (d3), `gameport` made the default with `gateway` kept selectable (`EVEJS_PILOT_TRANSPORT`), the
  suite's tests that count on the old default put right, and the operator told;
- (f) the removals the plan lists after that have no setting to undo them: they wait for the operator to have
  run on the default, and Phase 6 (one WebSocket in place of the routes and the event stream) is begun
  meanwhile.

## 2026-10-10 — a drone on the game port says whose it is and what it is doing, and a launch waits for its drones

Commit `2fbf14f`, pushed. Next's head: step (d1) of Phase 5.

**What was missing.** The gateway's space snapshot says four things of every drone: which ship
flies it, whose that ship is, what the drone is doing, and on what. The game port's said none.
The page's Drones panel takes a drone for the pilot's by the first of them; so does the route
that lists a pilot's drones in space.

**What a client is told** (the recordings first: nine have drones, and `OnDroneStateChange` is
in each as an entry of a ballpark update, never a packet of its own).

- `OnDroneStateChange(itemID, ownerID, controllerID, activityState, typeID,
  controllerOwnerID, targetID)`: on Tranquility an entry of `DoDestinyUpdate`, a list of the
  seven, beside the `AddBalls2` that brings the drone. michelle's park keeps it
  (`stateByDroneID`, 1496) unless the drone is neither the session's character's nor
  controlled by the session's ship: then it is forgotten, and "control lost" is said.
- A whole state's `droneState` (`Park.SetState`, 970) fills the same table, a row a drone.
- `OnDroneActivityChange(droneID, activityID, activity)` (1520) is kept beside it.
- So a client knows these things of its own drones, and nothing of another pilot's.
- This server sends the state both ways: the entry, and a notice of its own by `charid`
  (which michelle also takes, 265). The states are the client's `entityIdle` to
  `entitySalvaging`.

**What was built.**

- The park keeps the drones' states as michelle's does, from the whole state, the entry and
  the notice (`destiny/park.js`, `pilotSpace.js`).
- A drone's row on the game port says `controllerID`, `controllerOwnerID`, `droneActivity`
  (the gateway's words for the states) and `targetEntityID` where the park was told, and null
  for each where it was not (`spaceProjection.js`).
- The launch route waits for its drones on the game port, up to three seconds, a quarter at a
  time (`/api/bridge/drones/launch`).

**A second fault the live check found.** With the rows mended, the launch's own answer on the
game port still listed nothing launched: a launched drone is a ball the next ballpark update
brings, after `LaunchDrones` has answered, where the gateway reads the server's scene and
finds it there already. The page reads "nothing launched" as a launch that failed. Four
seconds on, both transports listed both drones.

**Proof.**

- 7 new tests: 4 of the park, the row and the feed (the entry is Tranquility's; the whole
  state is the recording's own, with rows put in as the server fills them), 3 of the launch.
  Seen to fail on the commit before: 6 (the seventh says a gateway pilot's launch does not
  wait, which was so before).
- 37 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time. One survived at first: a
  notice with no arguments was passed over either way, and only the report of an error told
  the two apart. The test now reads that nothing was reported; all 37 are caught.
- Suite: 10085 tests, 10061 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **On both transports, by script,** from a store saved first and a Venture staged for Test
  Two with two Hobgoblin I in its bay, that state saved too: undock, both drones launched,
  the space snapshot read. The drones' rows through each BFF were the same field for field:
  this ship's, the pilot's, "idle", no target, full shield, armour and hull. Before the
  change the game port's rows had none of the four.
- **The launch's answer, on the game port, on the committed code:** both drones listed in
  space, each controlled, as the gateway's answer lists them. No `[PKT] ERR`.
- The store was put back after (the same as the copy), both copies deleted.

**Not seen.**

- A whole state with a drone in it, live: a pilot who logs off in space with drones out comes
  back with none on grid, on either transport. The rows of a whole state are tested as the
  server fills them.
- A drone doing anything but idling: fighting, mining, returning. The words are tested state
  by state; a drone was not sent at anything.
- Another pilot's drone on grid, which the gateway describes and the game port now cannot.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Of another pilot's drone the game port says nothing.** The gateway says whose ship flies
  it and what it is at. A client is not told, and the game port's row is the client's. The
  overview shows such a drone with no controller.
- **A launch that brings nothing takes three seconds to say so** on the game port, where it
  was immediate. A launch that works answers as soon as its first drone is in the park.

**Not done.** (d2) and (d3): what kind of NPC a ship is, and a compression facility.

## 2026-10-10 — a ship nobody flies on the game port says what kind it is, and an NPC's Hulk is an NPC's

Commit `fd1f032`, pushed. Next's head: step (d2) of Phase 5.

**What was missing.** The gateway's space snapshot says of a ship nobody is flying which kind
it is: "concord", "npc" or "drifter". The game port's said nothing. The page reads the word in
five places (the overview's threat, a ship's stance, the tactical view, what a category hides,
the fleet's companions), and takes a kind it cannot read for a hostile one, so the law at a
gate was a threat on the game port.

**What a client is told** (the recordings first: 27 of them have the threshold).

- The ship's type, so its group. The overview keeps a table of NPC groups with the police's
  (182), CONCORD's (301), the customs officials' (446) and the faction navies' (288) apart
  from the pirates' (`state.py`, `GetNPCGroups`).
- On the slim item, `hostile_response_threshold` and `friendly_response_threshold`. Above
  nought the ship is hostile whatever the pilot's standing; otherwise the pilot's standing
  with its faction is set against the threshold (`npcs/client/entitystandings.py`). On
  Tranquility a pirate comes with 11 and 11, the law with -11.
- Whose it is: an owner above the system's own and below the players' is an NPC
  (`idCheckers.IsNPC`; `state.py` 778, the overview 968). It is not told the server's word.

**The first rule was wrong, and the server's own data showed it.** I built the kind from the
group alone and saw it live at two gates on both transports, the same. Then each of the
server's 5794 NPC profiles was set beside what the rule would call it: 142 differed. 136 are
ships of the law's groups that the server calls an NPC and sends as hostile (its catalogue of
every NPC type, put out by the GM console), and 6 are Drifter Battleships. The gates had only
shown the 21 profiles where the two agree.

**What was built.**

- The law's word is kept for a ship of the law's groups that is not sent as hostile; a
  Drifter Battleship is told by its group; anything else is "npc" (`spaceProjection.js`,
  `npcKindOf`). Set beside the server's profiles again: the server's own word for 5788, and
  the six drifters.
- A ship of the Ship category that an NPC owns is a ship nobody is flying. The live walk found
  it: this server flies the ORE mining fleet's Hulk as the Hulk's own type, and the game port
  said it was nobody's NPC where the gateway said it was.

**Proof.**

- 2 new tests. One is the recorded trip's own bytes: eight customs officials at Jita's gate
  (group 446, thresholds -11 and -11) and seven of CONCORD's at Perimeter's (groups 301 and
  182, -11 and 11), each the law's. The other is the table, case by case. Both seen to fail
  on the commit before.
- 24 ways of breaking it were tried, four at a time; all caught.
- Suite: 10087 tests, 10063 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **On both transports, by script,** from a store saved first: Test Two undocked, warped to a
  planet, and had the GM console put out four ships. What each BFF's snapshot called them:

  | ship | sent with | gateway | game port |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | the ORE fleet's Venture (group 1764) | -5 | NPC, "npc" | NPC, "npc" |
  | the ORE fleet's Hulk (the Ship category) | -5 | NPC, "npc" | NPC, "npc" (before: not an NPC) |
  | a CONCORD Police Officer from the catalogue (301) | 11 | NPC, "npc" | NPC, "npc" (the group alone: "concord") |
  | a Drifter Battleship (1310) | 11 | NPC, "npc" | NPC, "drifter" |

- **The law at two gates of Muvolailen, on the committed rule:** six ships on the game port
  (five of group 301, one of 182), each "concord". The gateway's walk of the same gates
  called its six "concord" too (the two walks did not meet the same ships).
- **In the browser, on the game port, on the committed code:** Test Two chosen on the page,
  undocked with the page's button, warped to the Annaro gate from the overview. The two
  CONCORD Police Officers there were rows with no mark, and no threat was listed. The GM
  console on the page then put out the catalogue's CONCORD Police Officer beside them: the
  same type and group, and that row alone was marked hostile and labelled as a pirate, in the
  list and in the threats above it, with "You are taking damage".
- The store was put back after each walk (the same as the copy), and the copies deleted.

**Measured, not mended.**

- **A ship nobody flies has no name on the game port.** The gateway's row has the server's
  name for it ("Mining Venture", "CONCORD Police Officer"); the slim item a client is sent
  has no name at all (the recorded gates' fifteen have none), and the game port's row says
  null. The page's overview shows the type's name for such a row ("CONCORD Police Officer"
  for each of the three in the browser). What a bot or another panel does with a row that
  has no name was not looked at.
- **Dock, pressed in the browser for a station 577,000 km off while that ship was shooting,
  did nothing to be seen.** The page asked for a warp twice and was refused both times
  (409), and showed no word of it. The header's Dock button the same. Why the warp was
  refused was not read.
- **The ORE mining fleet is a pirate to the page on both transports.** The server's word for
  it is "npc", and the game port's now the same. A client is sent -5 with it and does not
  show it as hostile. The page has no word for an NPC that is neither the law nor hostile, and
  a mining bot counts every "npc" ship as a reason to leave.
- `/npc 1 concord_police_cruiser` (one of the server's own law) was refused as not found, so
  the law was seen only where the server puts it.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The game port says "drifter" of a Drifter Battleship where the gateway says "npc".** The
  server never says "drifter" of anything; the gateway's own note lists it as a kind and the
  page has a word for it. Both are hostile to the page; only the label differs ("Drifter"
  against "Pirate"). It is the one place the two transports' kinds are meant to differ.
- **The kind follows the server's word, not the client's test of hostility.** By the
  threshold alone the ORE fleet would be the law's on the game port ("Police", no threat) and
  a pirate through the gateway. I kept the two the same and listed the fault for both.
- **An NPC's ship is told by its owner as well as its category.** A ship of a player's hull
  whose owner is an NPC corporation, a faction or an agent is taken for an NPC's. A player's
  ship is owned by its pilot on this server, so none is caught by it.
- **The pilot was not logged out with the page's button.** The page has one only while
  docked, and the pilot could not dock (above). I took the pilot off the page's list of who
  is online, put the store back and restarted both BFFs; the page then came up with nobody
  in.
- 33 older copies of the store from earlier in this session (1.9 GB) are still in the
  session's scratch folder. I left them: nothing needs them gone.

**Not done.** (d3): a ship that is a compression facility.

## 2026-10-10 — a ship that compresses ore says so on the game port, and the page compresses there

Commit `7f0546b`, pushed. Next's head: step (d3) of Phase 5, the last gap of the three found
when the two transports' rows were read side by side.

**What was missing.** The gateway's row for a ship running an industrial core and a
compressor says how far it reaches and which type lists it takes (`compressionFacility`).
The game port's said null of every ship, so the Mining panel's "Compress it" and the
compress-ore block of a bot found no facility there.

**What a client is told** (the recordings first: none has it, in any folder; so the
decompiled client).

- On the ship's slim item, `compression_facility_typelists`: a dict of type list to the
  range the ship takes that list at (`itemcompression/__init__.py`).
- `itemcompression/client/inSpaceCompression.py` reads it for the pilot's own ship (at no
  distance) and for any other ship that has it, is flown by a member of the pilot's fleet,
  and is within that list's range.
- This server puts it on the slim item while the core and a compressor run, and sends the
  slim item again when either starts or stops (`OnSlimItemChange`, which the game port's park
  already kept).

**What was built.** The row's `compressionFacility` on the game port, from the slim item's
dict: the widest range and the lists, in order, as the gateway's row has them; null where
the slim item has none (`spaceProjection.js`, `compressionFacilityOf`).

**Proof.**

- 1 new test: a ship turned into a facility by a slim item sent again, turned back, two
  lists at two ranges, the pilot's own ship, and what is not a dict. Seen to fail on the
  commit before.
- 13 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time; all caught, and again after
  the test's values were changed (below).
- Suite: 10088 tests, 10064 pass, 0 fail, 0 cancelled, 24 skipped.
- **On both transports, by script,** from a store saved first: Test Two given a Porpoise, a
  Medium Industrial Core I, a Medium Asteroid Ore Compressor I and heavy water, fitted,
  undocked, the core started, then the compressor. The own ship's row through each BFF:

  | | gateway | game port |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | nothing running | null | null |
  | the core running | null | null |
  | the core and the compressor | 66,000 m, list 334 | 66,000 m, list 334 |

- **In the browser, on the game port:** Test Two chosen on the page and undocked with its
  button. The Mining window said no support ship on the grid was compressing. The core and
  then the compressor were started from the page's own rack; the window then offered
  "Porpoise — your own ship" with the hold's two stacks. Compress pressed on 50 Scordite:
  the stack became 50 Compressed Scordite.
- The store was put back after each run (the same as the copy), and the copy deleted.

**Corrected on the way.**

- The test's values were first taken from an older note of ours (375,000 m, from July). The
  live run gave 66,000 m on both transports, and the test now has that. I did not look for
  why the range differs from July's.
- The first staging gave 5,000 heavy water, which does not fit a Porpoise's hold (the move
  was refused, and the core then refused to start for want of fuel). 300 fits.

**Not seen.**

- **Another pilot's ship as a facility.** The row is built the same for every ship, and
  tested for one that is not the pilot's, but no second pilot was on the grid.
- **The reading going away.** The compressor told to stop was still cycling six seconds
  later on both transports, and both rows still had the reading. The slim item sent again
  without it is tested.

**Measured, not mended.**

- **The page offers another pilot's facility whether or not that pilot is in the fleet.** A
  client offers one only if its pilot is a fleet member (`inSpaceCompression.py`, 26). The
  page's rule (`web/src/space/compression.ts`) is a ship, with the reading, that is not an
  NPC. The same on both transports.
- **The page offers Compress for a stack that cannot be compressed** (heavy water, beside
  the Scordite). A client lists what the facility's type lists take
  (`compress_in_space_controller.py`); the row carries the lists, and the page does not
  read them.
- **A module's button on the page's rack does not answer a plain click from a script**: it
  listens for the pointer going down and up. Nothing wrong for a person; a note for the
  next check (in the brief).

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The pilot was again not logged out with the page's button**: a ship with its core
  running cannot dock. I took the pilot off the page's list, put the store back and
  restarted both BFFs; the page came up with nobody in.

**Not done, and next.** The three gaps of step (d) are mended. Step (e), `gameport` made the
default transport with `gateway` kept selectable, is next, with (c2) beside it. The operator
has been told twice that it would follow (d1) to (d3).

## 2026-10-10 — the game port is the default, the gateway the way back; an image that could not start; and a pilot's call with no pilot refused

Commits `1dacbb6` and `d6d3de5`, pushed. Next's head: steps (e) and (c2) of Phase 5.

**For the operator, first.**

- **A chosen pilot now logs in on EveJS's game port (TCP 26000) unless you say otherwise.**
  `EVEJS_PILOT_TRANSPORT=gateway` puts every pilot back on the web gateway;
  `EVEJS_PILOT_TRANSPORT_OVERRIDES="name=gateway"` does it for one account. The BFF says
  which at start-up, and `npm run doctor` checks the game port and names the way back if it
  is shut.
- **Your container image is two months old and must be rebuilt** (`docker compose up --build
  -d`). An image built from the tree as it stood since the game port's transport went in
  could not have started; that is mended in the same commit (below).
- **`.env.example` does not name the setting.** I am not let read or change `.env` files
  here, so the README's Configuration section has it instead.

  among them (Farmer, docked in Jita; Zarik Yrjot, in space). The store was put back after.

**What was built: the default** (`1dacbb6`).

- `EVEJS_PILOT_TRANSPORT`, unset or empty, is `gameport` (`src/pilotTransport.js`). A BFF
  told `gateway` for everybody has no game port at all, as before.

  container; without that the way back could not have been taken there.

**A fault found on the way: the image had no `contracts/`.** The game port's transport reads
`contracts/evejs-web-bridge-contract.json` as it loads, the server loads the transport as it
starts, and the Dockerfile's last stage copied `src`, `scripts` and `web/src` only. I read
every relative require under `src/` against what the image is given: that one file was the
only one a running server needs and did not have. The Dockerfile and `.dockerignore` now
carry it, and a test reads both files against every such require
(`test/dockerImage.test.js`).

**What was built: a pilot's call with no pilot** (`d6d3de5`, step (c2)). The generic call
route, asked by an account that has chosen no pilot, sent everything but `charUnboundMgr` to
the web gateway, which made the call as a session naming the account and no character. For
an account on the game port the seam now refuses it itself (`accountCall` in
`src/pilotTransport.js`), with the gateway's own code and status for a call it refuses (403,
`CALL_NOT_ALLOWED`). An account on the gateway is answered as before.
