## 2026-10-10 — the standings asked by the page itself, a row opened asking for the one thing it wants

Commit `11f1592`, pushed. Next's head: the standings moved as the wallet was.

**What a retail client does** (the recordings first, then its code).

- In the Tranquility recordings (every folder searched by name) `GetCharStandings` is in ten
  files, `GetCorpStandings` in seven, `GetNPCNPCStandings` in nine,
  `GetStandingCompositions` in two and `GetStandingTransactions` in none. Read: the two
  lists are asked with nothing, at a login; the composition is asked as
  `GetStandingCompositions(500001, <the corporation>)`. No history was recorded.
- `standingsvc.py` 111: when the character is chosen the service asks for the NPCs'
  standings with each other (115), the character's (119), and its corporation's (126), the
  last not for a pilot in an NPC corporation, whose corporation's are taken to be none
  (118). It keeps them right from `OnStandingSet` and `OnStandingsModified`.
- 178: `GetStandingTransactions(fromID, toID)`, an entity's history with whoever, kept by
  the service for the two. 283: `GetStandingCompositions(fromID, toID)`.
- `standingsPanel.py` 86, 108, 111: a row opened asks for the history where it is the
  character's and for the composition where it is the corporation's. One, never both.
- Every caller in the client: the service's two, the panel's two, and
  `resourcewars/client/firstcompletiontracker.py` 36 (a history, of a corporation with the
  character).

**What the route did that a client does not.** `GET /api/bridge/standings?fromID=` asked
for both the history and the composition whichever row was opened. And on the game port
the two details went out unchecked: nobody had set them against the client's spelling.

**What was built.**

- **The standings' asking, written once** (`web/src/bridge/standingsReads.ts`): the two
  lists, the corporation's not asked for a pilot in an NPC corporation; a history; a
  composition. The flow uses it. A row opened asks for the one thing it wants, of the
  pilot or of its corporation, as the session has them.
- **The asking itself, and what fails a whole reading** (`web/src/bridge/ask.ts`). A route's
  request failed as a whole when the BFF was not reached, when it held no pilot or the
  pilot's session was gone, when the web session was not known, and when the flow had
  moved on to another pilot; only what the server answered one call with was that read's
  own failure. The page's own askings now tell the two apart the same way. The wallet's
  reads use it too.
- **A call the page makes for a pilot says so** (`pilot: true` on `POST /api/bridge/call`;
  `api.bridgeAsk` sets it). With no pilot held such a call is refused `NO_LIVE_SESSION`, as
  the route it stands in for refused. Before, the generic call with no pilot held was
  taken for the account's and tried as one.
- **On the game port the two lists, asked for by name, are answered from what the transport
  keeps** since the character was chosen (`src/gamePort/pilots.js`). Nothing is sent and
  nothing is counted, as when the route read them. Asked with any argument, or where
  nothing is kept, the call is sent as any call is.
- **The two details set against the client's spelling** (`src/gamePort/retailCalls.js`): two
  IDs and nothing else is the client's; anything else is sent as given and counted as
  differing.
- The route stands, with its tests. Nothing of the page's asks it.

**Proof.**

- 11 new tests; the flow's standings tests and the agents' now answer call by call. 59 ways
  of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time: all caught. Before the pass, one
  guard was found by reading to guard nothing (a kept list is never `undefined`) and taken
  out.
- With the sources of the commit before, 18 fail. Suite: 10189 tests, 10165 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped.
- **Side by side, live** (`standings-compare.mjs`; the route beside the page's own
  TypeScript asking through `/api/bridge/call`), on the game port and through the gateway,
  for Test Pilot (an NPC corporation, 1000044), Test Two (a player's, 98000000) and Farmer
  (a player's, 98000001):

  | | game port | gateway |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | the character's list, the corporation's, and why each failed | the same, all three | the same, all three |
  | asked for the pilot in an NPC corporation | one call; the corporation's none | one call; the corporation's none |
  | a history (`500001`, the character) | the same | the same |
  | a composition (`500001`, the corporation) | the same | one leaf differs of 29, and of 71: the time a cached call was made |
  | with no pilot held | route 409 `NO_LIVE_SESSION`; the page's asking 409 `NO_LIVE_SESSION` | the same |

  The game port's ledger after those three logins, each read by the route and by the
  page's asking: `GetNPCNPCStandings` 3, `GetCharStandings` 3, `GetCorpStandings` 2. One of
  each for a login, and two pilots in a player's corporation: neither the route nor the
  page's asking sent one. `GetStandingTransactions` 6; `GetStandingCompositions` 3, where
  six were asked of the BFF. Its answer through the gateway is a cached call's, and the
  transport keeps those; why three was not looked into further.
- **In the browser** (the default: the socket, the game port; Test Two docked). At the login
  the page asked for the two lists, once each, as a pilot's calls, in the socket's frames.
  The Standings window showed twelve rows, six of the character's and six of its
  corporation's. Its Refresh: the two lists asked once each. The character's Caldari State
  row opened: one call, `GetStandingTransactions(500001, 140000002)`, and the history on
  show. The corporation's Caldari State row opened: one call,
  `GetStandingCompositions(500001, 98000000)`, one asking for names, and two members on
  show with their standings. No `EventSource` was opened, and the route was not fetched.
- The game port's ledger for that browser session: `GetCharStandings` 1, `GetCorpStandings`
  1, `GetNPCNPCStandings` 1, where the page had asked for each list twice;
  `GetStandingTransactions` 1 and `GetStandingCompositions` 1, each now counted as the
  client's (`standingsvc.py` 178, 283). The whole ledger: 74 pairs, 77 calls the same as the
  client's and 17 reshaped to it, none unchecked.
- The page was logged out with its own button and left with nobody in; the store was put
  back and the copy deleted; both BFFs run the committed code.

**Measured and left.**

- **`GET /api/bots` was asked 24 times in 15.6 seconds** by the page with nothing being done
  and its 25 windows mounted. Not looked into.
- **Three generic calls went over HTTP** in the browser session and not on the socket. Which
  three was not read; the socket is opened at a token's third request.
- **One line in the BFF's log at the logout**: the gateway refused the event stream (404)
  and the session was ended. Seen before, with the status said twice.

**Not done.**

- **A history is asked for each time its row is opened.** The client keeps it for the two
  until told otherwise (`standingTransactionCache`).
- **Through the gateway the two lists are sent each time they are asked for**, as before:
  the keeping is the game-port transport's.
- **No recording has a history's call**, so its spelling is from the client's code alone.
- `scripts/bff-parity.js` still reads the route, which still stands.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A new word in the BFF's own protocol, `pilot: true`.** It is the page's to the BFF and
  never reaches the server. Without it the generic call is as it was. The other way was to
  have the page check for a pilot before asking, and the BFF is the one that knows.
- **What fails a whole reading was written down as five things, and the wallet made to
  follow it.** Before this, the wallet's reads failed as a whole only for a session gone;
  a BFF that could not be reached was each read's own failure, and the window said the
  wallet was read, with five errors.
- **The Standings window's Refresh sends nothing on the game port**, as it sent nothing when
  it read the route: the transport holds what the client's service holds, kept right by
  the server's notices. (The wallet's Refresh asks the server, since the page is what
  keeps the wallet.)
- **A detail asked any way but with two IDs is counted as differing**, not refused: the
  ledger is a measure, and the generic call carries what the page sends.
- **A detail that cannot be read still says why by the call's code**, as the route said it.

## 2026-10-10 — the skills' sheet sized and split; its first part: the queue asked for by name, and the server's clock told with a pilot's answers

Commit `c8de548`, pushed. Next's head: the skills moved as the standings were. That unit was
too big as written, and this is the first part of two.

**What the route is.** `GET /api/bridge/skills` is eleven lines, and is not a set of calls
handed on. For a pilot on the game port the sheet is made on the BFF
(`src/gamePort/skillSheet.js`, 155 lines) from three things:

1. five of the skill handler's reads as the transport keeps them (`pilotSkills.js`):
   the skills, the skills with the lapsed, the queue, the free points and, where a skill is
   in training, the character's attributes;
2. each skill type's name and group, and the two attributes the skill in training trains
   by, from the BFF's static data;
3. the server's clock as the pilot's session has it, for the points trained so far and for
   the page's countdown.

Through the gateway the sheet is the gateway's own snapshot, which no retail client asks for.

**What the page has not got**, measured by asking each read by name through
`POST /api/bridge/call` as Test Two on the game port:

- four of the five answered, from what the transport keeps;
- the queue's, `skillHandler.GetSkillQueueAndFreePoints`, was refused: 403
  `CALL_NOT_ALLOWED`. No list had it. It was a call the transport made of its own accord
  and no route asked by name;
- the server's clock comes to the page only inside a sheet a route has made.

**What a retail client does.** `skillQueueSvc.py` 117: the queue service asks
`GetSkillHandler().GetSkillQueueAndFreePoints()` once (`PrimeSkillQueue`) and keeps the
queue, right from `OnNewSkillQueueSaved`, `OnSkillQueuePausedServer` and the skills'
changes. The call's name is in seven of the Tranquility recordings' files. The client's
clock is its own, kept set by its connection, which is what the transport's session does
(`session.js`, `serverNow`).

**What was built.**

- **The queue's read is carried on the game port** (`GAME_PORT_ONLY_CALLS`,
  `src/gamePort/retailCalls.js`, with its entry against the client's line). A pilot's asking
  of it by name, with nothing, is answered from the queue and the free points as the
  transport keeps them, in the handler's own form, `(the queue, the free points)`; nothing
  is sent and nothing is counted. Asked with anything it is sent as any call is. Where no
  queue is kept it is asked of the handler, as the queue service would, and kept; several
  asking together are one asking.
- **A pilot's answer says the server's clock.** `POST /api/bridge/call`, for a pilot on the
  game port, answers with `serverNowMs`: the clock as that pilot's session has it
  (`pilots.serverNowMs`). An account's call, and a pilot's through the gateway, say none.
  The page's call hands it on (`callMethod.ts`); nothing reads it yet.
- The route, and everything the page shows, are as they were.

**Proof.**

- 5 new tests, and the test that pins the game port's own list says the new pair. 20 ways of
  breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time: all caught. Before that, one survivor:
  a check that a number which came as JSON is finite. It guards nothing and was taken out.
  Two guards beside a `catch` that already covers them were taken out by reading.
- With the sources of the commit before, 6 fail. Suite: 10194 tests, 10170 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped.
- **Live, on the game port** (Test Two; `skills-queue-probe.js`):

  | | the route's sheet | asked by name |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | the queue as chosen | none | none; free points 0 |
  | after a queue of one was saved (Afterburner to 4) | `[3450, 4]`, from 8000 to 45255 points, active | `[3450, 4, 8000, 45255]` |
  | the clock | 1791636973766 | 1791636973769, asked 3 ms later; 1 ms from this machine's |

  The game port's ledger afterwards: `GetSkillQueueAndFreePoints` 2, the login's and the
  transport's own after the save; the three askings by name added none. 37 pairs, 40
  calls, every one the same as the client's.
- **Through the gateway**: the queue's call is refused as before (403 `CALL_NOT_ALLOWED`),
  and an answer says no clock.
- **No browser check**: nothing the page shows or asks was changed in this part.
- The store was put back, which undid the queue, and the copy deleted; both BFFs run the
  committed code. The BFF's log: no error.

**6b's measure, counted** (`routes-survey.js <repo> list`). The BFF has 473 routes under
`/api/bridge` (365 POST, 108 GET). The page's `api.ts` names 140 of them in its code (90
POST, 50 GET), now that the wallet's and the standings' are not among them. Of the 50
GETs, 8 have a handler of 15 lines or fewer, 19 of 16 to 40, and 23 of more. A handler's
length is not its size: this one is 11 lines.

**Not done.** The second part, which is the page's: the sheet made in TypeScript from the
five reads, the types' names and attributes, and the clock; the flow moved onto it; the
two sheets side by side; the Skills window in the browser.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The unit was split**, and the second part is Next's head. The first is what the BFF had
  to carry before the page could ask at all.
- **The clock goes with each answer of the generic call**, one number, and not by a route
  of its own or at the socket's opening: it is then as fresh as the last thing the page
  asked, and costs nothing to keep.
- **The queue's call was added to the game port's own list, and the gateway's list in
  `eve.js` was left alone.** The gateway is the way back. Through it the page will read the
  route as it does now, which the second part has to provide for.
- **Free points that are not kept are answered as 0.** The queue service keeps them only
  where there are some, and this server answers 0 for none (`skillMgrService.js` 513).

## 2026-10-10 — the skills' sheet made in the page's own TypeScript, and set beside the route's leaf by leaf

Commit `96c0a09`, pushed. Next's head: the skills' sheet made by the page. This is the making
and the reads, proved against the BFF's; the flow is not moved onto them yet, which is the
third part.

**What was built.** Nothing of the page's uses either yet.

- **The sheet's making** (`web/src/bridge/skillSheet.ts`): what `src/gamePort/skillSheet.js`
  does, on the answers as the generic call hands them, where text is a string and a
  server's time is `{type:"long"}`. A level's points, the skill in training, its points at
  the pilot's rate since the queue began, the total with the lapsed and the free points.
  The sheet is in the form the route's is in, so the page's decoder reads either.
- **The reads** (`web/src/bridge/skillReads.ts`), as the client's skill and queue services
  make them, each with nothing: the queue first and alone, then the skills, the skills
  with the lapsed and the free points together, and the attributes only where a skill is
  in training. A read that fails fails the sheet. An answer that is no queue is a failure
  and not an empty queue. Where the queue's read is not carried, which is the web gateway,
  there is no sheet here and whoever asked reads the route's.
- **What a client knows of a type without asking** (`createSkillTypeFacts`): its name and its
  group's by `/api/names`, two names a type and no more than the route takes at once; the
  two attributes the skill in training trains by, by `/api/types/dogma`. Each is asked once
  and kept, since a type does not change. What was not answered is not kept.

**Proof.**

- **The two makings set side by side** (`test/gamePortSkillSheet.test.js`): the kept state of
  the recorded session at each of its 96 events, the BFF's making given it as it came off
  the wire and the page's given each read through `wireToBridgeJson`, at five readings of
  the clock each: 480 sheets, the same. Then 27 other cases: other attributes, types
  nothing is known of, free points past what a number holds, a queue with an end and no
  start, entries that say nothing of themselves. The same.
- 7 tests of the reads and of the page's own readings. 62 ways of breaking the two modules
  were tried, four of a file at a time. Three survived at first:
  - a check that a number is finite. What the page has came as JSON, where a number is.
    It was taken out, and its twin for a time with it;
  - two readings that cannot come off the wire as such (an entry whose arguments are no
    list, a queue entry with fields that is no KeyVal), which the side-by-side therefore
    cannot show. Each has a test now in the page's own, where its form can be written,
    and is caught.
- Without the two modules both test files fail to load: the tests have nothing older to be
  run against. Suite: 10203 tests, 10179 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on the game port** (`skills-compare.mjs`: the page's TypeScript asking through
  `POST /api/bridge/call` as a pilot, the facts from the static routes, the clock the
  answers say; the route's sheet read straight after):

  | | leaves | differ |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Test Two as chosen: 52 skills, 385,914 points, nothing queued | 633 | 1: the clock, 4 ms on |
  | with Afterburner to 4 saved and in training, 30 a minute | 641 | 1: the clock, 2 ms on |
  | four seconds on: 8002 points by the route, 8002 by the page | 641 | 1: the clock, 2 ms on |
  | Test Pilot: one skill, 500 points | 21 | 1: the clock, 4 ms on |

  Asked for the first sheet: the four reads, and 104 names. For the second: the five, and
  one type's two attributes. For the third: the five, and nothing of the static data.
- The game port's ledger for those two logins: 37 pairs, 72 calls, every one the same as
  the client's. Each of the handler's reads once a login, the queue's once more after the
  save; four sheets made by the page sent nothing further.
- **Through the gateway**: the queue's read is refused, the page's making says there is none
  here, and nothing else is asked.
- **No browser check**: nothing the page shows or asks was changed.
- The store was put back, which undid the queue, and the copy deleted; both BFFs run the
  committed code.

**A slip.** The first side-by-side was started the moment `store.sh` returned, and the
pilot's choosing was refused: the game server unreachable. `store.sh` waited for the web
gateway to answer; the game port opens a little after. It waits for both now.

**Measured.** Test Pilot has one skill and 500 points today. The brief says it has none.

**Not done.** The flow's reading of the skills moved onto this; the clock handed on by
`api.bridgeAsk`; the Skills window in the browser. The case of no skills at all is in the
tests alone.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The unit was split a second time.** Moving the flow means three test files that stand in
  for the route (it is named 13 times in `skillsFlow.test.ts`, which has 10 tests, 5 times in
  `freeSkillPointsFlow.test.ts`, which has 5, and once in `agentsFlow.test.ts`), and a third
  reader of the sheet (the drone range's skill levels) besides the window and the pause.
- **A sheet fails whole**, as the route's did, rather than showing with a part missing.
- **A skill's group is asked of the static data**, as its name is, and not read from the
  `groupName` this server puts in each skill's entry. The client has it from its install.
  Whether Tranquility's entries carry one was not looked at.
- **Names are kept for as long as the page lives.** They are the static data's and do not
  change while a server runs.

## 2026-10-10 — the Skills window reads the sheet the page makes itself

Commit `889150f`, pushed. Next's head: the flow moved onto the page's own sheet, the third
part of the skills.

**What was built.**

- **One reading of the sheet in the flow** (`readSkillSheetRaw`): the page's own, made from
  the skill handler's reads it asks for, with the types' names and the training skill's
  two attributes from the static data (`createSkillTypeFacts` over `api.resolveNames` and
  `api.fetchTypeDogma`). Where the queue's read is not carried, which is the web gateway,
  the route's sheet is read as before; and so it is with nobody chosen.
- **The Skills window and the reading after a pause use it.** `api.pauseSkillTraining` now
  only pauses.
- **The page has the server's clock.** `api.bridgeAsk` hands on what an answer says, and the
  flow keeps how far the server's is ahead of the browser's. The sheet's time, its
  countdown and the points of the skill in training are worked from that.
- The writes (a queue saved, points applied) still answer the route's sheet.

**Proof.**

- 5 new tests of the flow, with a pilot chosen: the sheet made from the reads and no route
  read; nothing in training and no clock said; the gateway's way; a read that fails; the
  pause both ways. The two agents' tests that open a mission's page now answer the skill
  reads call by call. The 15 older tests of the skills and the free points choose no
  pilot, and stay as tests of the route's way.
- 15 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time: all caught. Before the pass
  two things were taken out by reading: the clock forgotten when another pilot is chosen
  (every pilot of one BFF has one server's clock, and nothing could show the forgetting),
  and a filter for names left unanswered (only a structure's name ever is).
- With the sources of the commit before, 7 fail. Suite: 10208 tests, 10184 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped.
- **In the browser** (the default: the socket, the game port; Test Two docked):

  | what was done | what the page asked, in the socket's frames |
  | --- | --- |
  | the pilot chosen | the four reads, twice over (two windows want the sheet); 104 names in one frame |
  | "Queue IV" pressed on Afterburner's row | `POST /api/bridge/skills/queue` |
  | the window's Refresh | the five reads, and the two attributes of type 3450, once |
  | "Pause training" | `POST /api/bridge/skills/abort-training`, then the four reads |

  No frame and no fetch of `GET /api/bridge/skills` at any point; no `EventSource`. The
  window: 385,914 points, 52 skills, 16 groups; then "Afterburner IV, 20h 41m left", one
  place of 150 used; after the Refresh the row said 8,013 of 45,255, which is 26 seconds at
  30 a minute on the 8,000 it had; after the pause, "Training is paused" and the entry
  "paused".
- **The countdown ticks.** With nothing pressed the window said 20h 41m at 13:24:14 and at
  13:24:23, and 20h 40m at 13:24:35; the bar's width went 0.0518%, 0.0639%, 0.0786%.
- The game port's ledger for that session: each of the handler's reads once, the queue's
  twice (the login's and the transport's own after the save), the save and the pause once
  each. The page read the sheet four times and nothing more was sent. 77 pairs: 82 calls
  the same as the client's, 18 reshaped to it, none unchecked.
- **Through the gateway, in the browser** (the gateway BFF's own page, the same pilot after it
  was logged out of the other): the Skills window opened with two frames, the queue's read
  and then `GET /api/bridge/skills`, and showed the gateway's sheet: 52 skills, the queue
  of one, paused.
- Both pages were left with nobody in; the store was put back, which undid the queue, and
  the copy deleted; both BFFs run the committed code. The BFF's log: the one line at a
  logout seen before.

**Not done.**

- **The drone range's read of the pilot's skill levels still reads the route.** It is deep in
  a bot's run, and no test reaches it at all. It was moved and then put back: a line no
  test can fail is not moved on trust.
- **The sheet is read twice at a login**, by two windows, as the route's was. The transport
  sends nothing for the second; the page asks eight frames where four would do.
- **A queue saved or points applied land the route's sheet**, made on the BFF.
- So the route is still named by the page: for the gateway, for that one read, and behind
  the writes.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **With nobody chosen the flow reads the route**, which is the route's to refuse. That is
  why the older tests stand unchanged; with a pilot chosen, as the page always has when
  the window is open, it is the page's own.
- **A test account was signed in on the gateway BFF's page**, whose hangar was empty, by its
  own form, which says any password works. That page now remembers the account.
- **The clock is the server's, whichever pilot's answer said it.** It is kept across a
  change of pilot.

## 2026-10-10 — the Character Sheet's reads asked by the page itself, and its route no longer named

Commit `a684b32`, pushed. Next's head: the character sheet, sized and then moved.

**Sized first.** The route is 53 lines and made of four reads, each handed on, and one
making:

- `charMgr.GetPublicInfo3`, `charMgr.GetCharacterDescription`, `charMgr.GetHomeStationRow`:
  asked by name through `POST /api/bridge/call` as a pilot, each answered the same as the
  route's, on the game port and through the gateway;
- the clone: on the game port, `skillHandler.GetImplants` made into a clone on the BFF,
  each implant in the slot the static data has for its type; through the gateway,
  `charMgr.GetCloneInfo`, which the client never asks. `skillHandler.GetImplants` is
  carried by both.

So nothing was missing, and the page can ask the same way whichever transport its pilot
is on.

**What a retail client does.** In the Tranquility recordings (every folder searched by
name) `GetPublicInfo3` and `GetCharacterDescription` are in no file, `GetImplants` in
three, and `GetHomeStationRow` in one, a note, which says the sheet's home station is not
asked that way. From the client's code:

- `characterInfoWindow.py` 194: `GetPublicInfo3(itemID)`, the character named;
  `bioPanel.py` 28: `GetCharacterDescription(session.charid)`;
- `implantsBoostersPanel.py` 40 to 43: the sheet lists what the skill handler's
  `GetImplants()` answers (`skillsvc.py` 967), sorted by the slot each type's attribute 331
  says;
- `neocom/charactersheet.py` 59: `GetHomeStationRow()`, with nothing, kept by that service.
  Its callers are the map and the market's quote;
- **the sheet's own home station is another service's**:
  `characterOverviewElements.py` 88 reads `homestation.Service.instance().get_home_station()`,
  which asks `RemoteSvc('home_station').get_home_station()` once and keeps it until the
  server says it changed (`homestation/client/service.py`). The recording "Setting
  Character Home Station" has that call and its answer, a `StationData` of the station,
  its type, its system and whether it is a fallback. Asked by name today it is refused on
  both transports: no list carries it. This server has the service.

**What was built** (`web/src/bridge/characterSheetReads.ts`, and the flow onto it).

- The four calls, the character named where the client names it, asked together and each
  failing by itself; what fails a whole reading fails the sheet.
- The clone made by the page: the implants as answered, each known by its type and put
  in the slot its type's attribute says, under the server's own key. A type's slot is
  asked of the static data once (`POST /api/types/dogma`) and kept. An answer that is not
  implants is the clone's failure, and never an empty clone.
- `api.loadCharacterSheet` is gone. The route stands, and nothing of the page's asks it,
  through the gateway either.

**Proof.**

- 4 tests of the reads; the flow's 5 tests now choose a pilot and answer call by call,
  and 4 more are new (the clone made of implants, each other read failing alone, nobody
  chosen, the session gone). 26 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time.
  Two survived at first: the reading of a dict, which needed a case that cannot come off
  the wire and has one now, caught; and an error's code that is the default anyway, taken
  out.
- With the sources of the commit before, 10 fail. Suite: 10216 tests, 10192 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped.
- **Staged for it**: no test pilot had an implant. Two were given to Test Two and plugged in
  through the BFF's own routes (`implant-stage.js`): types 9899 and 9941.
- **Side by side, live** (`charsheet-compare.mjs`), for Test Two with its two implants and
  Test Pilot with none:

  | | game port | gateway |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | the public info (54 leaves), the bio, the home station (49) | the same, both pilots | the same, both pilots |
  | the clone, as answered | the same (21 leaves; 5 with no implants) | differs: the route's is `GetCloneInfo`'s |
  | the implants as the page reads them | 9899 in slot 1, 9941 in slot 2, both ways | the same, both ways |
  | what only `GetCloneInfo` says | not said by either | home station, clone station and 0 jump clones by the route; not said by the page |

- The game port's ledger: `GetPublicInfo3` and `GetCharacterDescription` are counted the

## 2026-10-10 — the sheet's home station asked as the client's own sheet asks it

Commit `ba37865`, pushed. Next's head: the sheet's home station asked as the client's own
sheet asks it.

**What a retail client does** (the recordings first, then its code).

- `get_home_station` is in eight of the Tranquility recordings' files. In "Logging In To
  Space" it is asked once at the login, of the service `home_station` by its name, with
  nothing; the answer is an object of the class `homestation.types.StationData` with four
  fields: `is_fallback`, `solar_system_id`, `id`, `type_id`.
- In "Setting Character Home Station" the server says `OnHomeStationChanged(<station>)` to
  the character, and the client asks `get_home_station()` again at once, before the
  setting's own answer is back.
- `homestation/client/service.py`: the service keeps the home station (67) until
  `OnHomeStationChanged` (163) or `OnHomeStationMovedFromStructure` (168), until a session
  change that has `corpid` in it (173), or until the session is reset.
  `characterOverviewElements.py` 88: the Character Sheet reads that service, and reads it
  again when the service says the home station changed.
- This server answers the same class with the same four fields, in the same order
  (`homeStationService.js` 75).

**What was built.**

- **The game port carries `home_station.get_home_station`** (its own list, and its entry
  against the client's line), asked of the service by name. The transport keeps the
  answer as the service keeps it: asked when something first wants it, answered from what
  is kept after, and let go at either notice and at a change of corporation, to another
  or to none. Asked with anything, it is sent as any call is.
- **The page's sheet asks it**, and reads the station out of the `StationData`
  (`bridge/characterSheet.ts`). Where the call is not carried, which is the web gateway,
  the sheet asks `charMgr.GetHomeStationRow` as before; any other failure is the home
  station's own, and the row is not asked for in its place.

**Proof.**

- 4 new tests (the keeping and the letting go; a home station that cannot be read; the
  page's fallback; the flow through a BFF that does not carry the call), and the tests of
  the reads, the decoder and the two lists say more. 26 ways of breaking it were tried,
  four of a file at a time. Two survived at first, both in the transport: the answer
  handed on as it came off the wire and not as JSON (the test read a field by a name that
  bytes and text both give), and what the server said not handed on with the answer. Each
  has an assertion now, and is caught. One was not tried at first, its text being in the
  file twice, and was tried with more of what is round it.
- With the sources of the commit before, 13 fail. Suite: 10220 tests, 10196 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped.
- **Live, by name, on the game port** before anything of the page's: asked twice, answered
  twice with `StationData` of station 60003760 in system 30000142, not a fallback, and
  counted once in the ledger against `homestation/client/service.py:67`.
- **Side by side** (`charsheet-compare.mjs`, Test Two): on the game port the page asks
  `home_station.get_home_station()` and reads station 60003760 from it, the station the
  route's row names; through the gateway the page asks it, is refused, asks the row, and
  has what the route has, leaf for leaf (49).
- **In the browser** (the default; Test Two): the Character Sheet asked the four calls, the
  third `home_station.get_home_station()`, at the login and again at its Refresh, and
  never the row. "Home station: Jita IV - Moon 4 - Caldari Navy Assembly Plant". The game
  port's ledger over the two logins of this check (the side-by-side's and the browser's):
  `get_home_station` 2, one a login, where it was asked for three times, once by the
  side-by-side and twice by the window. 75 pairs: 120 calls the same as the client's, 17
  reshaped, none unchecked.
- **Through the gateway, in the browser**: the service's call, then the row, and the same
  station on show.
- Both pages were left with nobody in; the store was put back and the copy deleted; both
  BFFs run the committed code.

**Not seen live.** The letting go at the server's word: nothing the BFF carries changes a
home station, and the page has no window for it. It is in the tests, with the notices as
the recording has them.

**Not done.**

- **The client asks for the home station at a login** (the recording has it), and the
  transport asks when the sheet first wants it. Which of the client's windows asks at the
  login was not found; it belongs with the login's other calls.
- The home station's candidates, its setting, and the time of the next remote change,

- The sheet shows the station by name. The client's shows the system and its security,

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Through the gateway the sheet asks a call that is refused, each time it is read**, and
  then the row. The page does not know its pilot's transport, and a refusal remembered
  would be wrong for a page whose next pilot is on the other.
- **Another call of the home station service's would not be answered from what is kept**,
  were the game port to carry one: only the one read is the service's keeping.

## 2026-10-10 — the agents' journal asked by the page itself, and a bot's reading of it given a test

Commit `5c2e1f1`, pushed. Next's head: the journal, sized and then moved.

**Sized first.** The route is one read. For a pilot on the game port it answers the journal
as the transport keeps it (`journalKept`); otherwise it asks `agentMgr.GetMyJournalDetails()`.
Asked by name through `POST /api/bridge/call`, that call is carried by both transports.

**What a retail client does.** `GetMyJournalDetails` is in 28 of the Tranquility recordings'
files. In the client every caller is the journal service (`journal.py` 312 and 331, the
whole, by the service's name with nothing; 325, one agent's part, on that agent's
moniker), and every window that wants the journal reads that service
(`GetMyAgentJournalDetails`: the docked agents, the research browser, the job board's
missions, the mission tracker). So the window reads what the route was written against,
and the transport already keeps it as the service does (`pilotJournal.js`).

**What was built.**

- **The game port answers the call by name from what it keeps**: asked with nothing, the
  journal is made right first (the whole if none is kept, a marked agent's part
  otherwise) and answered in the form the call answers in. Asked with anything, or where
  what the server answered was no journal, the call goes on as any call does.
- **The page asks it** (`web/src/bridge/journalReads.ts`): the Agents & Missions window, the
  mission bot's reading of the world, and the bots' macros. `api.loadJournal` is gone, and
  the route is named by nothing of the page's, on either transport.

**Proof.**

- 5 new tests: the read; the transport's answering by name, and where no journal is kept;
  the flow's asking, and never the route; and **the mission bot's reading through the real
  flow, which no test had reached**. It starts the bot over a faked BFF and watches its
  first reading ask for the journal and land it.
- The flow's tests that read the journal, in three files, now answer the page's own call.
  They name it as what it is (`agentMgr.GetMyJournalDetails()`, asked with nothing as a
  pilot's), and a request of the old route keeps its own path and is answered by nothing:
  a flow gone back to the route would fail them.
- 17 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time. Two survived at first: a
  call of the same name on another service answered with the journal, and the mission
  bot's reading not made at all. Each has a test now, and is caught.
- With the sources of the commit before, 42 fail. Suite: 10225 tests, 10201 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped.
- **Side by side, live** (`journal-compare.mjs`), for Test Two (one mission offered) and Test
  Pilot (none): the same on the game port (13 leaves and 2) and through the gateway (15
  and 3). The game port's ledger for those two logins: the call 2, one a login; the
  route's reading and the page's two askings sent nothing.
- **In the browser** (the default: the socket, the game port; Test Two): the journal read at
  the login by one frame, the call as a pilot's. The window showed the offer from Antaken
  Kamola. "Accept" pressed in the page: the action, then the journal's call twice (the
  server's word of the change, and the accepting's own reading), and the window said
  "Active (1): Accepted". No frame and no fetch of the route; no `EventSource`.
- The ledger for that session: the journal's call twice, the whole at the login and the
  agent's own part after the acceptance, where the page asked three times. 80 pairs: 154
  calls the same as the client's, 16 reshaped, none unchecked.
- **Through the gateway, in the browser**: one frame of the same call, and "Active (1)".
- Both pages were left with nobody in; the store was put back, which undid the acceptance,
  and the copy deleted; both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: the page's code names 138 of the BFF's routes under `/api/bridge` (48 reads).

**Measured and left.**

- **The BFF said once, during the browser's session, that the chat server did not answer the
  corporation's join** for the pilot. Not looked into.
- **After an acceptance the page reads the journal twice**: once for the server's word and
  once of the accepting's own accord. The transport sends one call for the two.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The bot's reading was given a test and moved**, where the drone range's reading of the
  skills, which also had none, was put back two units ago: the mission bot can be started
  in a test with what a faked BFF already answers.
- **The tests name the journal's read by the call and not by a path.** A stand-in that
  answered the new call under the old route's name would have passed with either.
- **A mission was accepted on a test pilot** from the page, to see the journal made right at
  the server's word, and undone by putting the store back.

## 2026-10-10 — crimewatch's states and the clone's grade asked by the page itself

Commit `e21134c`, pushed. Next's head: the short reads that are one call handed on, several
in a unit. Two were taken, which are read together as a pilot comes online.

**Sized first** (`routes-survey.js`, and each handler read).

| route | what it is | taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the crimewatch states | one call, and the BFF's own clock put beside the answer | yes |
| the clone's grade | one call on the game port; "none to give" through the gateway | yes |
| the saved fittings | one call, read by a bot's refit block alone, which no flow test reaches | no |
| the formations | one call, read with two other routes by the scanner | no: with the scanner |
| the corporation's assets | a making, by a helper | no |

**What a retail client does.** `GetClientStates` is in 36 of the Tranquility recordings'
files, as the call a bind of crimewatch carries; the client's service has the states from
then and changes them at the server's notices (`crimewatchSvc.py` 89). `GetCloneGrade` is
in none of the recordings; the client's own code asks it as the account comes onto the
session and keeps it (`clone_grade_svc.py` 125), and this server's log of a retail
client's login has it. Both were read against the client in earlier units, and the
transport keeps both as the client's services do.

**What was built.**

- **The two reads** (`web/src/bridge/crimewatchReads.ts`, `cloneGradeReads.ts`), each the
  service's own call with nothing, by the generic call. The flow asks them where it asked
  the routes. Where the clone grade's call is not carried, which is the gateway, there is
  no grade, as the route said. `api.loadCrimewatch` and `api.loadCloneGrade` are gone.
- **The timers are counted against the server's clock as the page has it**: what the answer
  of the crimewatch call itself has just said. An answer that says no clock is shown all
  the same, against the clock the page last had; before, a route's answer with no clock
  was an error.
- **A gateway pilot's answer says a clock too**: the BFF's own, which is what the route put
  beside the states. On the game port it is the pilot's session's, as before.

**Proof.**

- 3 new tests (the two reads; states that come with no clock said); the flow's tests of
  both, the choosing's test and the BFF's test of the clock say what is so now. The
  socket's tests, which asked for the clone's grade as their example of a route's read,
  ask for the saved fittings.
- 15 ways of breaking it were tried, four of a file at a time: all caught.
- With the sources of the commit before, 14 fail. Suite: 10228 tests, 10204 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped. (The first run of the whole suite had one failure: a test of the choosing
  that lists every generic call made at it, in a file the unit's own runs had not
  included.)
- **Side by side, live** (`online-compare.mjs`, Test Two):

  | | game port | gateway |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | crimewatch's states | the same | the same |
  | the clock the answer says | 2 ms after the route's, 1 ms from this machine's | 4 ms after the route's, 3 ms from this machine's |
  | the clone's grade | 1 by both | none by both: the route says so, the call is refused |

  The game port's ledger for that login: each call once, with nothing more sent for the
  route's reading or the page's.
- **In the browser** (the default; Test Two): at the login two frames, the two calls as a
  pilot's, and no fetch of either route. Undocked from the page, the states were read
  again by one frame and the header said "In Space, Safety Full"; docked again from the
  header. No `EventSource`.
- **Through the gateway, in the browser**: the same two frames at the login, the grade's
  refused, and the pilot online all the same.
- The ledger over the three logins of this check, one of which undocked and docked:
  `GetClientStates` 6, `GetCloneGrade` 3. 82 pairs: 199 calls the same as the client's, 49
  reshaped, none unchecked.
- Both pages were left with nobody in; the store was put back and the copy deleted; both
  BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: the page's code names 136 of the BFF's routes under `/api/bridge` (46 reads).

**A slip.** One change to a test file was made by a one-line stream edit and not by a
patch script. It was three plain words replaced throughout; it was read back, and the
file's tests pass.

**Not done.** The saved fittings, the formations, and the others on Next's list.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A gateway pilot's answers say the BFF's clock.** Without it, moving the crimewatch read
  would have left a page on the gateway counting timers against the browser's own clock,
  where the route had it counting against the BFF's.
- **States with no clock said are shown.** A session that cannot say the time is no reason
  to hide the pilot's safety level.
- **The pilot was undocked and docked again** to see the safety level on show, in high
  security space and with nothing else done.

## 2026-10-10 — the scanner's reads sized, and one of them found to be no read of the scanner's at all

Commit `964c083`, pushed. Next's head: the scanner's reads.

**Sized first.** The scanner's loading read three routes, and they are three kinds of thing.

| route | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/bridge/formations` | one call, `beyonce.GetFormations()`, handed on |
| `GET /api/bridge/scan-full-state` | `scanMgr.GetFullState()` made, on the game port, on the object `GetSystemScanMgr()` answers, which the BFF binds and holds; by name through the gateway. Asked by name on the game port it is counted as differing from the client's |
| `GET /api/bridge/scanner/state` | no call at all: the probes and the launcher as the BFF keeps them from the server's notices |

Also read and not taken: the agents' table (the route decodes the whole table down to
the station's agents), the repair quotes (a guard for structures, then the call), the
mining scan (a check that the pilot is in space, then the call).

**What a retail client does with the first.** `beyonce.GetFormations()` has one caller in
the client: `michelle.py` 324, as the ballpark is made, which loads what it answers into
the ballpark. They are the ballpark's formations. The probe scanner has its own
(`probescanning.formations`, in its install) and asks the server for none. The transport
already asks for the ballpark's as it makes one (`pilotSpace.js`).

So the page's scanner was making a call its retail counterpart never makes, for a readout
the client's scanner has not got. The readout said so of itself: "reference data only; no
supported route applies them to probes", or, live, that the shapes were behind a cache
reference it could not fetch.

**What was done.** The read is out of the scanner's loading, and the "Formation reference"
readout out of the Scanner window, with the slice's field, the view, the decoder nothing
else used, and their tests. 455 lines out and 19 in, by the commit's own count. The route
stands; nothing of the page's asks it.

**Proof.**

- The scanner's flow tests answer its two reads and throw at any other fetch, so a
  request for the formations, by the route or by the call, fails them. The window's test
  says the window says nothing of formations. Put back, each is caught (3 ways tried).
- With the sources of the commit before, 4 fail. Suite: 10224 tests, 10200 pass, 0 fail,
  24 skipped (four fewer tests than before: five that were the readout's and the
  decoder's are gone, and one is new).
- **In the browser** (the default; Test Two, undocked from the page): the Scanner window's
  Refresh asked two frames, `scan-full-state` and `scanner/state`, and showed "16 scannable
  results", nine of them anomalies. Nothing was asked for formations in the whole session,
  by frame or by fetch, and the window says nothing of them. Docked again from the header.
- The game port's ledger for that session: `beyonce.GetFormations` once, counted as the
  client's at `michelle.py:324`, which is the transport's own asking as the ballpark was
  made; `scanMgr.GetFullState` twice, on the system's scan manager. 80 pairs: 90 calls the
  same as the client's, 34 reshaped, none unchecked.
- The page was left with nobody in; the store was put back and the copy deleted; both
  BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: the page's code names 135 of the BFF's routes under `/api/bridge` (45 reads).

**Not done.**

- **`scan-full-state` and `scanner/state`.** The first wants a call asked by name to be made
  by the transport on the object the client makes it on, which the BFF's routes do today
  with handles of their own. The second is the transport's keeping with no call behind it:
  for the page to have it, either the keeping moves to the page, which hears the same
  notices, or the page is given a way to read what the transport keeps.
- The other reads sized above.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A readout was taken out of the Scanner window.** It showed nothing a pilot could use, by
  its own words, and the client's scanner has nothing like it. It is the first thing this
  loop has removed from the page rather than moved.
- **The decoder and its tests went with it**, since nothing else read them. The route and
  the BFF's side are as they were.

## 2026-10-10 — the first write made by the page, and a way round the write check found and closed

Commit `836fff6`, pushed. Next's head: one small write made by the page, to work out what a
route's checking and confirming become.

**What the route did.** `POST /api/bridge/skills/abort-training` is two things: it checks the
page said `confirm: true` (`requireWriteConfirmation`), and it makes
`skillHandler.AbortTraining()` with nothing by `dispatchBridgeWrite`, which is
`heldTopLevelCall`: a pilot must be held, the held session must be the current one, and a
pilot being exported or whose release is not verified is refused. Nothing is read again by
the route; the page re-reads its sheet.

**What a retail client does.** The queue panel's Pause
(`skillQueuePanelNew.PauseTraining`) calls `skills.AbortTrain()` where a skill is in
training, which is the handler's `AbortTraining()` with nothing (`skillsvc.py` 796). It asks
the pilot nothing first. It then commits its queue unactivated, which with the queue
unchanged sends nothing (`skillQueueSvc.CommitTransaction` 147). `AbortTraining` is in two
of the recordings' files. So the page's Pause is one call, as the client's is.

**What a write's route becomes.** The generic call makes a write only when three things
hold, and refuses it as before otherwise (403 `BRIDGE_WRITE_REQUIRES_DEDICATED_ROUTE`):

| said or checked | what it stands for |
| --- | --- |
| `pilot: true` | the write is a pilot's; with none held, 409 `NO_LIVE_SESSION` |
| `confirm: true` | the page means it: what the route's confirmation was |
| the pair is on `PAGE_WRITE_PAIR_KEYS` (`src/bridgeCallPolicy.js`) | the BFF's own say over which writes the page may make by this way |

It is then made by `heldTopLevelCall`, as the route makes it, so every check a held pilot's
write is under is the same one. The list has one pair. A pair put on it that is not a write
stops the BFF as it starts. On the page: `api.bridgeDo` beside `api.bridgeAsk`, and
`web/src/bridge/skillWrites.ts` (`pauseTraining`). The route stands; nothing of the page's
asks it.

**What stays a route's.** Not built, but settled enough to size the rest by:

- The generic call hands the page's arguments on as they come. So a write belongs on the
  list only where the server's handler checks what it is given against the session, and
  trusts no identity the caller supplies. `AbortTraining` takes nothing. Each write is read
  for this before it is listed.
- A route that does more than confirm and call (builds its arguments from what the BFF
  holds, reads again and answers a sheet, guards on something only the BFF knows) is sized
  first, as the reads were.

**A defect found on the way, in the BFF, and closed.** The breakage pass left one survivor:
taking the two `typeof` checks out of `isPageWritePair` was caught by nothing. Reading why
led to the write check itself. The generic call took `service` and `method` as whatever the
JSON gave it. `isBridgeWritePair` answers false for anything that is not text, and further
on the name was made into text: the gateway's client did `String(service || "")`, and a
list of one name is that name as text.

Measured on the committed code before the fix, with a skill in training:

| asked | through the gateway | on the game port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{service: ["skillHandler"], method: "AbortTraining"}`, nothing else said | 200, and the write made | 502 `CALL_FAILED`, after passing the list of calls |

So through the gateway any write on the BFF's list could be made by the generic call with
no confirmation and with the page's own arguments, by naming its service as a list. EveJS's
own gateway refuses a call whose names are not text (`normalizeWebCallRequest`), so nothing
of the server's is at fault and nothing of it was changed. Closed in three places, each
with its test written first and watched failing:

- the route refuses a call whose service or method is not text, or is empty: 400
  `INVALID_REQUEST`, before anything is asked;
- the game port's list of calls (`assertAllowed`) takes two names as text and nothing else;
- the gateway's client sends what is not text as no name, and no longer makes it into one.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 8 new. With the sources of the commit before, 11 fail (ten tests and the one file
  that cannot load without the new module).
- Breakages: 32 across the two passes (18, then 14 for the text checks), each caught. The
  first pass's survivor is the one above, caught now by the list-named cases.
- Suite: 10232 tests, 10208 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport** (Test Two; a queue of two saved by the route):
  - a list for the service or for the method, with or without `pilot` and `confirm`, and an
    empty service: 400 each. The skill was still in training after all of them;
  - the write with nothing said, with `pilot` alone, with `confirm` alone, and with
    `confirm` said as the text "true": 403 each. Another write of the handler's with all
    said (`ApplyFreeSkillPoints`): 403;
  - with no pilot chosen: 409;
  - paused by the route, started again, paused by the page's write: the two sheets after
    are the same, and both answers carry the server's `OnServerSkillsChanged`. A pause with
    nothing in training answers 200 and null by either way.
- **In the browser, on both pages** (Test Two, docked): the Skills window's "Pause training"
  sent one frame, `POST /api/bridge/call` with `skillHandler.AbortTraining`, `args: []`,
  `pilot: true`, `confirm: true`, then re-read its sheet; the window said "Paused
  training." and offered "Start training". Nothing asked `/api/bridge/skills/abort-training`
  in either session. On the gateway's page "Start training" was pressed first and seen to
  start it.
- The game port's ledger: `skillHandler.AbortTraining` 5 times, counted the same way
  whether the route made it (2) or the page's write (3). 75 pairs; 162 calls the same as
  the client's, 20 reshaped, none unchecked. The gateway BFF's: the call 5 times, each on a
  held pilot.
- The store was put back and the copy deleted; Test Two's queue is empty again, as it was.
  Both pages were left with nobody in. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: the page's code names 134 of the BFF's routes under `/api/bridge` (45
reads, 89 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- The route's sheet (`GET /api/bridge/skills`) through the gateway still marks a paused
  queue's first skill as in training; the page's own sheet does not. It is in the list
  already.
- The gateway client's test, as first written, sent nothing and swallowed the reason. It
  was written again as the file's other tests are and passes, and fails against the old
  line. Why the first writing sent nothing was not found.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The generic call is no longer read-only.** `docs/bridge-wire-contract.md` said every
  write is refused there "even if the body supplies `confirm: true`". It now makes the
  writes on one short list, for a held pilot, when the page says it means them. This is
  what Phase 6b asks for (the page making the client's calls, with no route of its own
  for each), and the list is the BFF's to keep short. The contract is corrected to say
  what is so. If the operator would rather writes kept their routes, the list emptied
  puts it back: the route still stands.
- **Which writes may go on the list** is decided by reading the server's handler, as above,
  not by the route being short.
- **A call that names no text is refused with 400**, where it was passed on. Nothing of the
  page's or the bots' sends such a call: the whole suite passes with the check in.
- **The defect was fixed in the BFF and not handed to a sub-agent**, the server's side
  being already right.

61. The page's read of the map's stations: at every load of the station panel it asks the BFF for
    `map.GetStationInfo` and reads only whether the answer was the cached envelope, which on the game port it
    was not in three reads, while the BFF hands it the whole table (322 KB of JSON). Find what, if anything, shows that
    yes or no; then stop sending the table, or stop asking.

## 2026-10-10 — the page's writes sized, and a queue saved by the page with the client's own call

Commit `cea56d7`, pushed. Next's head: the page's writes sized, and the skills' own moved.

**The survey.** `writes-survey.js <repo> all` reads every `POST` route under `/api/bridge`
that the page names (89) for what its handler does. Sorted by what each hands its work to
(the helper's name, read off the survey; not every handler was read through):

| kind | routes | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a confirmation and one call by name | 7 | `fleet/apply`, `skills/apply-free-points`, `safety/set-level`, `planet/launch/delete`, `contracts/accept`, `gm/slash`, `fleet/broadcast/bubble` |
| a confirmation and one call on an object the BFF binds and holds | 26 | dogma's (overload, repair, the weapons' linking), the ballpark's, the inventory's, the fleet's, a planet's, the scan manager's, the drones' entity, a ship boarded or left |
| a flight command: the flight read, the call on the ballpark, the flight read again | 10 | stop, align, approach, orbit, keep at range, and the warps |
| a move between places, with a wait for the session's change | 4 | undock, dock, jump, a ship boarded from the hangar |
| not a write, or the session's own | 5 | `select`, `release`, `drone-recovery/ready`, and two reads asked by `POST` (`fitting/state`, `industry/preview`) |
| guards, more than one call, or a reading the answer carries | 37 | the market's four, industry's three, the inventory's moves, fitting, the modules, the targets, the drones, mail, the queue's save, and the rest |

So the short kind is 7 of 89. The largest kinds (26 and 10) are calls on an object the BFF
holds a handle for, which the generic call has no way to name: for those the transport
must make a call asked by name on the object the client makes it on, as it already does
for the services it keeps a moniker of (dogma's, the ship's, the skill handler's, the
corporation's). That is the same thing the scanner's `scan-full-state` waits for among the
reads.

**The queue's save: what the route did.** `POST /api/bridge/skills/queue` checks each
entry's shape, saves, and answers the route's sheet. On the game port the saving is the
transport's `saveSkillQueue`, built earlier from the recordings; through the gateway it is
`skillMgr.SaveNewQueue`, a pair of the gateway's own.

**What a retail client does.** One caller of `SaveNewQueue` in the client:
`skillQueueSvc.CommitTransaction` (153), `SaveNewQueue({place: (typeID, toLevel)},
activate=activate)` on the skill handler. Before it, for a queue that is to be started,
`TrimQueue` reckons each entry's time, which reads the attributes where they are not kept;
after it the panel opens a new transaction, which asks for the queue afresh, but after two
refusals. In two files of the recordings ("Apply Skill Points Flow").

What the panel says for `activate` was read this time and is **not** what the page says:

| the panel's | `activate` |
| --- | --- |
| the start button (`StartOrStopTraining`, nothing in training) | True |
| a changed queue saved (`SaveSkillQueue`, and at the panel's closing) | whether a skill is in training |
| after a pause | False, and only if the queue was changed |

The page says True for every save, as the route did on the game port: a paused queue
that is reordered starts training here and stays paused in the client. Left for the next
unit, and said at the top of the module.

**What was built.**

- The page's module (`web/src/bridge/skillWrites.ts`, `saveQueue`) makes the client's call:
  the whole queue as a dict by place from nought, `activate: true`, as a pilot's and as a
  write it means. It answers whether the save was made. The flow then reads its sheet as it
  reads it at any time. `Ask` takes a call's keywords now.
- The transport makes the save asked for by the handler's name as it makes the route's:
  one function for both (`saveOnHandler`), the attributes first, the save on the handler's
  own object, the queue again. The route's way is noted in the ledger as the client's own,
  the page's as the client's call asked by name (reshaped).
- `skillHandler.SaveNewQueue` is on the BFF's list of writes, on the page's own, on the
  game port's list of what it carries, and judged against the client's line.
- **Through the gateway the handler's save is not carried.** The call is refused (403
  `CALL_NOT_ALLOWED`) with nothing saved; `saveQueue` answers false and the flow asks the
  route. So the route is still named by the page, for that.

**The contract manifest.** The whole suite, run before the live check, failed one test:
`contracts/evejs-web-bridge-contract.json` pins the write list. Made again by its
generator, the diff was the pair, the count and the hash. But the same manifest said
`genericBridgeAllowsWrites: false`, written by the generator as a constant, and the test
held it against the word `false`: it has been untrue since `836fff6` and nothing said so.
The generator now writes whether the generic call makes any write, and which
(`genericBridgeWrites`), from the policy's own list; the test holds the manifest against
the policy. Watched failing first.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 9 new, and four of the flow's older ones rewritten (their stand-in saved by the
  route). With the sources of the commit before, 15 fail (14 tests and the file that
  cannot load).
- Breakages: 52 against the code as it stands, each caught. Two survived on the way and
  were read:
  - a check in the judge that no value off the wire could fail (what is not null and has
    the type `dict` is an object): taken out;
  - the attributes read "unless the save says it does not start the queue" against "only
    if it says it does": no test told them apart. A save that does not say is not the
    client's, and nothing of the client's is read for it. Made exact, with its test.
- Suite: 10241 tests, 10217 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on the game port** (Test Two): with no pilot 409; the save with nothing said,
  with `pilot` alone, with `confirm` alone: 403 each, and the gateway's own pair with all
  said 403. A queue of two saved by the route, emptied, saved by the page's write: the two
  sheets after are the same; so are the two after an emptying. The other order saved by
  the page's write trains the other skill. A level already trained is refused by each way
  with the same answer (409 `CALL_REFUSED`, `QueueCannotTrainPreviouslyTrainedSkills`), and
  the queue is as it was.
- **Live, through the gateway**: the page's write 403 `CALL_NOT_ALLOWED` four times, the
  sheet unchanged after each; the route saves, empties and refuses as before.
- **In the browser, on both pages** (Test Two, docked, the Skills window):
  - game port: "Queue IV" sent `POST /api/bridge/call` with `skillHandler.SaveNewQueue`, the
    dict `{0: (3394, 4)}`, `activate: true`, `pilot`, `confirm`; then the sheet's reads.
    The window said "Added Hull Upgrades IV to the queue" and showed it training. "Remove"
    sent the same call with an empty dict, and the queue was empty. The queue's route was
    not asked in the session;
  - gateway: each press sent the call, then `POST /api/bridge/skills/queue`, and the window
    said the same.
- The game port's ledger for the script: `skillHandler.SaveNewQueue` 7 times, 3 the same
  as the client's (the route's) and 4 reshaped (the page's); the queue asked for 8 times,
  once at the login and once after each save, refused or not; the attributes once. 37
  pairs: 48 calls the same, 4 reshaped, none differing or unchecked.
- The store was put back and the copy deleted; Test Two's queue is empty again. Both
  pages were left with nobody in. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: 134 routes named, as before (45 reads, 89 writes): the queue's route is
still named, for the gateway.

**Measured and left.**

- Through the gateway every save by the page now costs a refused call first, and the
  gateway BFF's log has a line for each (as for the queue's read).
- eve.js keeps a copy of the manifest of its own (`server/contracts/`): 351 write pairs
  against 357 here, the flag false. Its test holds it against its own allowlist alone.
  Not touched: nothing here reads it, and eve.js is not this loop's to push.
- Two patch scripts of this unit stopped part-way, each at a find I had written from
  memory (a comment's last word; a line that occurs twice). The helper writes a file only
  when every find for it is found, so no file was half-changed, but the files before it
  in the script were already written. Each was finished by a second script for the rest.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **Through the gateway the page falls back to the route**, rather than the gateway's own
  save being made a write of the page's. The gateway is the way back; its pair is not the
  client's call.
- **`activate: true` for every save, for now.** It is what the page did. The client's rule
  is the next unit, and changes what a pilot sees: a queue changed while nothing trains
  will be saved unstarted, with "Start training" to press.
- **A save that does not say `activate` gets nothing of the client's read for it first.**
- **The manifest says the generic call makes writes, and which.** Its flag was a constant
  that had become untrue.
- **eve.js's copy of the manifest was left as it is.**

## 2026-10-10 — whether a save starts the queue, read again from every caller; and a claim withdrawn

Commit `bcf13d5`, pushed. Next's head: the skills' rest, `activate` first.

**Withdrawn.** The entry before this one said the client's panel saves a changed queue
with `activate` set to whether a skill is in training, and that a paused queue reordered
"starts training here and stays paused in the client". The Next list was to build that.
It was read from the panel's two saves (`SaveSkillQueue`, `SaveQueueOnClose`) and not from
every caller. It is wrong, and building it would have made the page differ from the
client. The module's note and the entry against the client's line said the same and are
corrected.

**What the client does**, from every caller of `CommitTransaction`:

| what is done | where | `activate` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a skill added, removed or moved (each ends in `OnClientQueueModified`, which commits at once) | `skillQueueSvc.py` 278, 301, 322, 368, 383, 389 | True, and False where every training slot of the account is used |
| the panel's start button, nothing in training | `skillQueuePanelNew.StartOrStopTraining` | True |
| the panel's own save, at its closing or after a pause | `SaveSkillQueue`, `SaveQueueOnClose`, `PauseTraining` | whether a skill is in training, or False: but only a queue that differs from the one last committed is sent, and each change was committed as it was made |

`IsAllCharacterTrainingSlotsUsed` (859): one slot and one more for each entry
`userSvc.GetMultiCharactersTrainingSlots()` answers, against the account's OTHER
characters whose row in the selection screen's data has a skill in training; all are used
when the two counts are equal. Kept until `OnMultipleCharactersTrainingUpdated`. The
selection data is the character service's, kept from the selection screen (`ccSvc.py` 39).

In the recordings: `userSvc.GetMultiCharactersTrainingSlots` in five files, of four
logins. In the one read through ("Logging In") it is asked by the service's name with
nothing as the queue service starts, and answered `{}`.

**What the page did.** True for every save. That is the client's own word where the
account has a slot free, which is every account of this server as it is staged (measured:
`test2` has two extra slots, three in all, for three characters). Where an account's one
slot is held by another character, the server refuses a started save
(`UserAlreadyHasSkillInTraining`), so on the page no change of the queue could be saved at
all there; the client saves it, unstarted.

**What was built.**

- `web/src/bridge/trainingSlots.ts`: the reckoning, from the client's two reads in its
  order, kept as the service keeps it, and let go at the server's word and with another
  character.
- The game port carries `userSvc.GetMultiCharactersTrainingSlots`, judged against the
  client's line (nothing sent with it).
- The transport keeps the selection screen's data from the choosing and answers
  `charUnboundMgr.GetCharacterSelectionData` by name from it, with nothing sent.
- `saveQueue` takes whether the save starts the queue. A change says what was reckoned;
  the start button says True and asks nothing of the slots.
- Through the gateway the user service's read is not carried: nothing is reckoned, and a
  change is saved started by the route, as before.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 10 new. With the sources of the commit before, 8 fail (7 tests and the file that
  cannot load).
- Breakages: 45, each caught. One check was taken out on reading (a held pilot always has
  the selection data: it is kept by the choosing that makes the pilot held).
- Suite: 10251 tests, 10227 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, as the server is** (game port, Test Two): the slots answer two extra; nobody
  else trains; every slot used: false. A save started and a save unstarted are each made,
  the second leaving the queue with no start.
- **Live, staged**: the account's extra slots cleared in a copy of the store
  (`slots-store.js`), that copy put in, and Test Three given a queue by the route. Then,
  as Test Two: the slots answer `{}`; the selection data kept from the choosing has Test
  Three with a skill in training; every slot used: true. A started save is refused by the
  page's write and by the route alike (409 `UserAlreadyHasSkillInTraining`), nothing
  saved. An unstarted save is made and the queue is kept with no start; so is an emptying.
- **Nothing sent for the kept read**: three askings of the selection data by name left the
  ledger's count at 9; the three askings of the slots beside them took theirs from 3 to 6.
- **In the browser, staged, game port** (Test Two, the Skills window): "Queue IV" sent
  `userSvc.GetMultiCharactersTrainingSlots`, `charUnboundMgr.GetCharacterSelectionData`,
  then `skillHandler.SaveNewQueue` with `activate: false`; the window said "Added Hull
  Upgrades IV to the queue", showed it paused, and offered "Start training". That button
  sent the save with `activate: true` and nothing of the slots; the server refused, and
  the window said another character on the account is training. "Remove" asked the two
  reads again (the server had said the account's training changed) and saved the empty
  queue unstarted. The queue's route was not asked.
- **Gateway page, staged**: "Queue IV" sent the slots' read (refused), the page's save
  (not carried), then the route, which the server refused: the window said another
  character is training, and nothing was queued. As it was before this unit.
- The game port's ledger for the staged run: 77 pairs, 168 calls the same as the client's,
  21 reshaped, none differing or unchecked; the slots three times, each the client's own.

**6b's measure**: 134 routes named, as before.

**Measured and left.**

- The client asks the slots at every login. The page asks when a change first wants
  them, and the transport does not ask at the choosing. It belongs with the login's calls.
- Through the gateway, on an account whose slots are used, a change of the queue is
  refused where the client would save it unstarted.
- Not built, of what the client does around a commit: the save made again unstarted after
  `SkillInQueueOverAlphaSpTrainingSize`; the clone grade's check before a started save
  (`_CheckCloneGradeRestrictions`); the selection data read again where the client forces
  it.
- An account's extra training slots are in the store's `accounts` rows
  (`multiCharacterTrainingSlots`). Two accounts have any, the ones with IDs 1 and 2 (the
  second is `test2`): two each.

**Slips.**

- A test of mine hung a test run for its whole 400 seconds: its stand-in held an answer
  back and never gave the second asking one. The run was stopped by its own command line
  (one process, by its ID). The test now answers every asking after the first, and says
  how long it will wait (`{ timeout: 5000 }`), since a breakage of the reads' order would
  hang it again and the breakage tool is not to be time-limited from outside.
- After the store was put back and its copies deleted, I ran the staging script itself to
  confirm, which saves and empties a queue: Test Two trained Afterburner for a few seconds
  more than in the store I had saved. Both queues were then read with the reading probe
  and are empty. The copy was already gone, so this stands.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The page does as the client's queue service does**, which changes what a pilot sees
  only on an account whose training slots are all used by its other characters: a change
  of the queue is saved, unstarted, where it was refused.
- **The start button starts the queue whatever was reckoned**, as the client's does, and
  the server's refusal is what is said.
- **The store was staged by editing a copy of it** (the account's extra slots cleared) and
  put back after.
