## 2026-10-10 — free skill points put into a skill by the page itself, with the client's own call

Commit `0c81ff1`, pushed. Next's head: the free points applied.

**What the route did.** `POST /api/bridge/skills/apply-free-points` checks that the page
said `confirm` and makes `skillHandler.ApplyFreeSkillPoints` with the skill and the points
the page sent. One of the seven that are a confirmation and one call by name.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. It has three ways of spending free
points, and three calls:

| the client's | the call | on the page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a skill's own menu, "apply skill points" (`skillQueueSvc.UseFreeSkillPoints`, 926, from the menu built at 915): asks how many, offering what the next level wants | `skillHandler.ApplyFreeSkillPoints(skillTypeID, pointsToApply)` (`skillsvc.py` 886) | the "Apply … SP" button on a skill's row |
| the queue panel's and the apply window's "to the queue" | `GetFreeSkillPointsAppliedToQueue()`, then `ApplyFreeSkillPointsToQueue()` | not there |
| the apply window's "to these skills" | `GetFreeSkillPointsAppliedToSkills(list)`, then `ApplyFreeSkillPointsToSkills(list)` | not there |

For the first, the client's skill service (`skillsvc.ApplyFreeSkillPoints`, 867 to 888)
has the free points first, asking where it has none; sends nothing for a skill in
training, one not known, more points than are held, or none; caps the points at what the
fifth level wants; and takes what the handler answers for the free points left.
In the recordings the call is in one flow ("Apply Skill Points Flow", once). Its bytes:
made on the handler's own bound object, with two whole numbers (81032 and 908) and no
keyword but the macho version. The note beside the recording has it answering 109092.

The page's button offers what the next level wants, or what is held if that is less
(`freeSkillPointsPlan`), and is not shown for a skill in training: the menu's entry with
the amount it offers, and no asking.

**The server's handler** (`skillMgrService.Handle_ApplyFreeSkillPoints`): the character is
the session's; the skill must be one it knows and not the one in training; the points are
capped at what the skill can take and refused if more than are held. It takes no one's
name. So the pair may be one of the page's own.

**What was built.**

- The page's module makes the call (`applyFreePoints`) and hands on what the handler
  answers; the flow reads that as the receipt, as it read the route's.
- `skillHandler.ApplyFreeSkillPoints` is on the BFF's list of the page's own writes.
  Either transport carries it, so there is no asking of the route in its place, and the
  route is no longer named by the page.
- **The call had no entry against the client's line.** On the game port it was counted
  unchecked whenever it was made, by the route as well. It has one now: one skill and how
  many points, each a whole number above nought, and nothing else.
- The transport does around the call what the client's skill service does: the free
  points read first where none are kept, and the answer kept as the points left.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 5 new. The flow's five older tests run against a stand-in that answers the call
  where it answered the route; two of them had what they assert changed. With the sources
  of the commit before, 8 fail (7 tests and the file that cannot load).
- Breakages: 21, each caught.
- Suite: 10256 tests, 10232 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport** (Test Two, with 5000 free points set in a copy of the store):
  - the write with nothing said, with `pilot` alone, with `confirm` alone: 403 each, and
    the points as they were;
  - 100 points by the route, then 100 by the page's write, into Afterburner: each answers
    the points left (4900, then 4800 on the game port), each moves the skill by 100, and
    each answer carries the server's `OnFreeSkillPointsChanged`;
  - a skill not known, and more points than are held: refused by each way with the same
    answer (409 `CannotApplyFreePointsDoNotHaveSkill`, `CannotApplyFreePointsNotEnoughRemaining`);
  - no points: 200 by each way, the points left unchanged. The client never sends that.
- **In the browser, on both pages** (Test Two, the Skills window showing "Unallocated"):
  "Apply 1,165 SP" on a skill's row sent `POST /api/bridge/call` with
  `skillHandler.ApplyFreeSkillPoints`, the skill and 1165, `pilot` and `confirm`; the
  window said "Applied 1,165 skill points", the unallocated points fell by that, and on
  the game port's page the skill's row showed its next level reached. The route was not
  asked in either session.
- The game port's ledger for the script: the call 8 times, 6 as the client's (reshaped:
  asked by name, made on the handler) and 2 differing, which are the two with no points.
  34 pairs; 34 calls the same, 6 reshaped, 2 differing, none unchecked.
- The store was put back, confirmed by a probe that only reads (no free points, an empty
  queue, the three skills as they were), and then its copies deleted. Both pages were left
  with nobody in. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: 133 routes named (45 reads, 88 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- With free points held, the two transports' sheets do not agree on the total: the game
  port's (the page's own, and the route's there) said 390,914 with 5000 free and did not
  move as 200 were applied; the gateway's said 386,114 and rose by what was applied. One
  counts the free points and the other does not. What the client's own total counts was
  not looked at.
- The client's other two ways of spending free points are not on the page.
- The page's button has no asking of how many; the client's menu asks.

**Slips.**

- The commit says the flow's five tests were "rewritten for the call". Two had their
  assertions changed; all five run on the changed stand-in. Written here as counted.
- I wrote a reading probe over a scratch file of the same name (`sheet-read.js`) without
  looking at what was there. Nothing in the brief or this log names the older one.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The page's third write goes by the generic call on both transports**, with no route
  behind it, because both carry the pair.
- **The entry against the client's line counts a call with no points as differing.** The
  client sends none such; the server answers it and spends nothing.

## 2026-10-10 — the ship's safety level set by the page itself, with the client's own call

Commit `2783179`, pushed. Next's head: the safety level set.

**What the route did.** `POST /api/bridge/safety/set-level` checks that the page said
`confirm`, checks that the level is 0, 1 or 2 (400 `INVALID_SAFETY_LEVEL` otherwise), and
makes `crimewatch.SetSafetyLevel` with it. The second of the seven that are a confirmation
and one call by name.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. One thing makes the call: the
crimewatch service (`crimewatchSvc.SetSafetyLevel`, 343), on the moniker for where the
pilot is; it then has the level it set as the level and asks nothing. Three things call
the service:

| the client's | when |
| --- | --- |
| the safety button's selector (`shipSafetyButton.py` 480) | a level no lower than the one now, pressed: at once |
| the selector's Confirm (660) | a lower level, pressed: a Confirm appears beside it, and that sets it |
| a tutorial's action (`nodegraph/client/actions/crimewatch.py`) | not a pilot's doing |

A level that is locked is not pressed at all. The asking before a lower level and the
locks are the selector's; the page's selector does both already (`SafetyChooser.svelte`),
from an earlier unit. This unit is the call it ends in.

**The recordings have none of it.** `SetSafetyLevel` is in no file of any folder. Its form
is from the client's code alone.

**The server's handler** (`crimewatchService.Handle_SetSafetyLevel`): the character is the
session's; the level is made a whole number and held between none and full, and what is no
number is full. It takes no one's name. So the pair may be one of the page's own, and a
level that is none of the three cannot be stored whatever is sent.

**What was built.**

- The page's module makes the call (`web/src/bridge/crimewatchWrites.ts`); the flow keeps
  the level it set as the level, as before. Either transport carries the pair, so the
  route is no longer named by the page.
- `crimewatch.SetSafetyLevel` is on the BFF's list of the page's own writes.
- The entry against the client's line judges the call: one of the three levels, and
  nothing else. It said "same" for anything before.
- **What the route checked is not checked by the generic call**, which hands on what it
  is given. A level of 7 by the route: 400. By the generic call: sent, made full by the
  server, counted as differing. The transport kept whatever level a set named as the level
  the client has; after a call that is not the client's it now lets what it kept go, and
  the next reading asks the server. Otherwise the page would have been shown 7.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 4 new. The flow's stand-in answers the call where it answered the route, and
  counts any asking of the route; two assertions follow. With the sources of the commit
  before, 8 fail (7 tests and the file that cannot load).
- Breakages: 20, each caught.
- Suite: 10260 tests, 10236 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport** (Test Two, docked; the two outputs are the same line for
  line):
  - the write with nothing said, with `pilot` alone, with `confirm` alone: 403 each, and
    the level as it was;
  - to 1 by the route, to 0 by the page's write: each read back as the level, twice;
  - to 7: the route 400; the page's write 200 answering 2, and the level read back 2;
  - after a logout and a login the level last set (1) is the level; put back to 2.
- **In the browser, on both pages** (Test Two, undocked from the header, since the badge
  is the ship's): "Safety Full" opened the selector. Partial, a lower level, sent nothing
  and showed "Confirm Partial" and "Cancel" with the three levels unpressable; Confirm sent
  one frame, `POST /api/bridge/call` with `crimewatch.SetSafetyLevel`, `[1]`, `pilot` and
  `confirm`; the badge said Partial and the selector shut. Full, a higher level, was sent
  at once and the badge said Full. Crimewatch was not read after either, and the route was
  not asked. Docked again from the header, and logged out.
- The game port's ledger, script and browser: `crimewatch.SetSafetyLevel` 7 times, 6 as
  the client's (reshaped) and 1 differing, which is the 7. 83 pairs; 160 calls the same,
  40 reshaped, 1 differing, none unchecked.
- The store was put back, confirmed by probes that only read (the level 2, docked where
  it was, no free points, an empty queue), and then its copy deleted. Both BFFs run the
  committed code.

**6b's measure**: 132 routes named (45 reads, 87 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- The server does not hold a level locked: it sets what it is sent, in any system and for
  any clone. The locks are the selector's alone, in the client as on the page.
- The tutorial's setting of the level is not on the page.

**Slip.** For the second time in two units I wrote a scratch file over one of the same
name without looking (`break-safety.js`, the breakage list of the earlier safety unit).
Nothing names it. From here a scratch file's name is looked for before it is written. Of
those written after it in this unit two were looked for first; the others were new when
written, by the tool's word, and had not been looked for. (Corrected: this said all were.)

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The level's check moved from the BFF to the server**, for a call made by the generic
  call. The page's own code sends one of three; anything else is the server's to make
  something of, which it does safely.
- **After a set that is not the client's the transport forgets what it kept**, and does
  not keep the level named.

## 2026-10-10 — a contract taken on by the page itself, and a defect of the server's found and fixed on the way

Commit `e1fa602`, pushed. In eve.js: `378ef753f`, committed on `main` and **not pushed**
(eve.js is not this loop's to push). Next's head: a contract accepted.

**What the route did.** `POST /api/bridge/contracts/accept` checks that the page said
`confirm` and makes `contractProxy.AcceptContract` with the contract's ID made a number and
`forCorp` made true or false. The third of the seven that are a confirmation and one call.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. One thing makes the call: the contracts
service (`contracts.AcceptContract`, 345 to 430). Before the call it reads the contract
(kept five minutes), looks at the stations it starts and ends at (a structure it may not
enter is asked about), counts the jumps, sets a courier's volume against the ship's hold,
and asks the pilot yes or no on what is paid and got. Then
`GetContractProxySvc().AcceptContract(contractID, forCorp)` (422); it clears its lists, and
the details window reads the contract again. Two buttons call the service: Accept
(`contractsDetailsWnd.py` 516) and Accept for the corporation (528), which is added only
for a character whose `corprole` has the Contract Manager role (93, 249, 326).

**The recording.** `AcceptContract` is in three files, one flow ("Receiving and accepting a
contract for item"). Its bytes: to the proxy by its name, `(233598633, False)` and the
macho version, answering a DBRow.

**The server's handler, and a defect.** `Handle_AcceptContract` hands the two on to
`prepareContractAcceptanceRequest`. With `forCorp` true that took the session's
corporation for who accepts and its wallet for who pays, and nowhere asked whether the
character has the role. The file has the role's check and uses it for failing, rejecting
and the issuer's authority; not for accepting. So any member of a player corporation could
accept a contract for it, and its wallet paid. It was so by the route as well, which hands
`forCorp` on as it comes.

That is a defect of the server's a retail client could be made to use, so a sub-agent was
given it, in the eve.js checkout as it stands (no branch, no worktree, no push, the six
files of other sessions left alone). It found the reading right, and found more than I
had: the acceptance's fingerprint is the corporation's, so a pending acceptance for the
corporation could be replayed by any member, and it put the check ahead of that. Its test
was watched failing first (the corporation's wallet at 925 where 1000 was wanted). The fix
is nine lines. I read the diff, ran its test file myself (10 pass), and saw it live below.

**What was built here.**

- The page's module makes the call (`web/src/bridge/contractWrites.ts`, `acceptContract`)
  and reads which contract was accepted off the row the server answers; no row is a
  decline. The flow asks for the character, never for the corporation. Either transport
  carries the pair, so the route is no longer named by the page.
- `contractProxy.AcceptContract` is on the BFF's list of the page's own writes, and has
  its entry against the client's line, where it had none.
- The route's acknowledgement decoder is gone with the route's asking.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 3 new; the module's two for the old decoder rewritten for the call; the flow's
  five answered by the call, one with its assertions changed. With the sources of the
  commit before, 9 fail (8 tests and the file that cannot load).
- Breakages: 20 caught. One more form survived and comes to the same (`>= 0` for `> 0`:
  nought is answered as nought either way). A default that could never matter was taken
  out on reading.
- Suite: 10263 tests, 10239 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport** (contracts made for the purpose: Test Pilot issues item
  exchanges of 1000 of a mineral for 100 ISK; the two outputs differ in nothing but how
  my probe printed a balance):
  - the write with nothing said, with `pilot` alone, with `confirm` alone: 403 each;
  - one taken by the route and one by the page's write, as Test Two: each answers the
    contract's row (finished, accepted by Test Two, not for the corporation) with the
    same two notices, and 200 ISK left the wallet for the two;
  - taken already: 409 "This contract is not available to accept" by each way; a contract
    that is not there: 200 with no row by each way;
  - each read again: finished, accepted by Test Two;
  - **for the corporation, with the fix loaded**: Test Two, a member without the role,
    409 "Only a Contract Manager can accept a contract for the corporation"; Test Three,
    who has the role, was let on and refused at the next check, the corporation's wallet
    not having 100 ISK.
- **In the browser, on both pages** (two more contracts made for Test Two alone): the
  Contracts window showed them offered; "See details", then "Take this on…" sent nothing
  and asked, showing "You pay 100.00 ISK"; "Yes, take this contract on" sent one frame,
  `POST /api/bridge/call` with `contractProxy.AcceptContract`, the contract's ID and
  `false`, `pilot` and `confirm`; the lists and the contract were read again and it showed
  finished, with one fewer waiting. The route was not asked.
- The store was put back, confirmed by probes that only read (no contract in the world,
  the sheet as it was), and then its copy deleted. Both BFFs run the committed code.
  EveJS runs with the fix loaded.

**6b's measure**: 131 routes named (45 reads, 86 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- **A contract cannot be made by its route on the game port.** `POST
  /api/bridge/contracts/create` answers 400 `CALL_INVALID` there: the route hands the
  call a plain object, which cannot be sent. Through the gateway it works, and the
  staging went that way. The page does not make contracts, so nothing of the page's is
  broken by it. `contractProxy.CreateContract` has no entry against the client's line
  (5 counted unchecked).
- The two transports answer a cash balance asked by the generic call in different forms.
  The page's decoder reads either; my probe printed one as an object.
- The sub-agent reported four more of the same shape in the server, which it has now
  been given: a contract MADE for the corporation by any member (its hangar's items and
  its wallet: the serious one), a courier the corporation accepted COMPLETED by any
  member, and two reads for the corporation it had not settled against the client. Its
  report will be in the next entry.

**Slips.**

- The first live run went on after its staging had failed, and asked the server six
  times with no contract's ID; they are the six "differing" in the game port's ledger.
  The script stops now where a contract was not made.
- A flow test of mine failed as first written (its stand-in answered another contract's
  details than the one the server named), and I ran the breakage pass before running the
  test: the flow's five were "not tried" until it was put right and run again.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The server's defect was fixed by a sub-agent and committed in eve.js, unpushed.**
  `378ef753f` is one commit ahead of `origin/main` there, for the operator to push or not.
- **The write went on the page's list only once that fix was in and seen live.**
- **The page still accepts for the character alone.** It is not told the session's roles.
- **The siblings were given to the same sub-agent**, each to be its own commit, tests
  first, and the two reads only where the client's own gate is found.

    was not in three reads, while the BFF hands it the whole table (322 KB of JSON). Find what, if anything, shows that
    yes or no; then stop sending the table, or stop asking.

## 2026-10-10 — a planetary launch's record removed by the page itself

Commit `12885f1`, pushed. Next's head: a planetary launch removed.

**What the route did.** `POST /api/bridge/planet/launch/delete` checks that the page said
`confirm` and makes `planetMgr.DeleteLaunch` with the launch's ID. The fourth of the seven
that are a confirmation and one call.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. One thing makes the call: the journal's
list of launches (`journal.py` 456 to 465). Remove on a row takes the row off the list,
calls `sm.RemoteSvc('planetMgr').DeleteLaunch(launchID)`, and asks for the launches afresh.
It asks the pilot nothing first. The call is in none of the Tranquility recordings (every
folder searched): its form is from the client's code alone.

**The server's handler**, read for whose launch it removes, since the ID is the caller's
to name. `Handle_DeleteLaunch` hands the store the launch's ID and the session's
character; the store marks the launch deleted, and answers false where the launch has an
owner who is not that character. A launch that is not there, or is deleted already,
answers true. It removes the record alone: the container and what is in it stay in space.
No notice came with an answer, live.

**What of the page's removes a launch.** One thing: a bot's collecting of one
(`collect-launches`), which warps to the container, takes what is in it, reads the
container again, and removes the record only if it read empty. No window of the page has a
Remove. So the thing to prove was the bot's run, and its test was written first.

**What was built.**

- The page's module makes the call (`web/src/bridge/launchWrites.ts`, `removeLaunch`), as
  a pilot's and as a write it means. The flow's collecting step calls it where it called
  the route. Either transport carries the pair, so the route is no longer named by the
  page (`api.ts`, `deleteLaunch` gone).
- `planetMgr.DeleteLaunch` is on the BFF's list of the page's own writes, and has its
  entry against the client's line, where it had none: the one launch and nothing else.
- The contract manifest made again by its generator.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 5 new. The flow's two first (`web/src/app/launchCollectorFlow.test.ts`: a
  one-block bot over a stand-in BFF; the container emptied, read again, then the call, and
  the route never asked; a container not emptied keeps its record), the first watched
  failing on the old code, its order ending at the route. Then the module's one, the
  BFF's one for the write and one for the entry's form; and the list of the page's writes
  pinned at six. With the sources of the commit before, 4 tests fail and the module's
  file cannot load; the flow's second passes there too, being what did not change.
- Breakages: 14, all caught.
- Suite: 10268 tests, 10244 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport**, with three launch records put into a copy of the store
  (two of Test Two's and one of another character's); the two outputs are the same line
  for line:
  - the write with nothing said, with `pilot` alone, with `confirm` alone: 403 each, and
    the two still listed;
  - the first removed by the route and the second by the page's write: each answers
    true, and the list read after each has one fewer;
  - another character's launch: false by each way; read after, it was still listed for
    its owner;
  - a launch that is not there, and one removed already: true by each way.
  The game port's ledger for that run: `planetMgr.DeleteLaunch` 8 times, each `same`;
  35 pairs, nothing differing. `GetMyLaunchesDetails` went to the server 3 times for 4
  askings: the transport keeps the answer and lets it go at a removal.
- **In the browser, on both pages**, with a real launch each time: 300 units put into
  Test Two's command centre in a copy of the store, launched by the BFF's own route (a
  container in space, the export tax paid), and a one-block bot saved. Test Two undocked
  from the header; Bot Manager, Pilots, the bot chosen, "Run here". The bot asked to warp
  to the launch, read the container, moved the one stack to the hold, read the container
  again, and sent one frame, `POST /api/bridge/call` with `planetMgr.DeleteLaunch`, the
  launch's ID, `pilot` and `confirm`. The route was not asked. The bot ended ("The
  program finished"), and the pilot's launches read empty after, on each page. The game
  port's ledger after its run: 86 pairs, 163 calls, 125 `same` and 38 `reshaped`,
  `DeleteLaunch` once and `same`. The gateway's tally has the pair once, by the generic
  call.
- The store was put back and confirmed by a probe that only reads (Test Two docked where
  it began, which is not where the run left it; no launches), then its copies deleted.
  The check's bot was removed from each BFF's library. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: 130 routes named (45 reads, 85 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- **The server's owner check is skipped for a session with no character.** `deleteLaunch`
  refuses another owner's launch only where the owner it is handed is above nought, and
  the handler hands it `session && session.characterID`. Whether a session at the
  selection screen can have a call sent to `planetMgr` at all I have not shown. The BFF
  does not let one (an account with no pilot held is refused all but the selection
  screen's service, and the write wants `pilot`). Given to the sub-agent to establish
  first and fix only if it is real; its report will be in the next entry.
- The Bot Manager's row for the pilot said the station it had left while the header said
  "IN SPACE", on both pages, for the whole run.
- "Recent runs" read 0 on the game port's page straight after the tab's run ended. Read
  once; not looked into (it may count the server's runs alone).
- Three bots named "Courier run (game-port check)" of earlier runs are in the game port
  check BFF's library. Left.

**Slips.**

- The staging script failed twice before it staged: a name read before it was made, and
  rows keyed without the separator the store puts between a map's name and a child's key
  (U+001F, which a printed key does not show), so the server read none of them.
- The first live run was made on that empty staging and went on asking of launches that
  were not there. Its output was thrown away, and the script now stops where the pilot's
  launches are not the two staged.
- "Run here" did nothing the first time, and I waited on it: the start asks through the
  browser's `confirm`, which the hidden pane answers "no" with nothing shown. I read the
  row's code, answered the confirm in the page (its text kept: "This run may move,
  consume, or expose items; change planetary colonies."), and pressed again.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The write went on the page's list once the server's handler was read** for whose
  launch it removes, and another character's launch was seen refused live by both ways.
- **The possible defect of the server's went to the sub-agent as a question first**, with
  the checkout's rules as before. eve.js is four commits ahead of `origin/main`, unpushed.
- **The bot's start was confirmed by a script in the page**, which is pressing OK on the
  page's own question.
- **A real launch was made for the browser's proof**, on each transport, and undone with
  the store.

## 2026-10-10 — a launch removed by a session with no character: the server's, found real and fixed

No commit of code here. In eve.js one more commit on `main`, **not pushed**: `ccf788b7b`.
With the four before it, eve.js is five commits ahead of `origin/main`.

**What the sub-agent was given**: the reading of the entry before this one (the store
refuses another owner's launch only where it is handed an owner above nought), to establish
first whether a session with no character can reach `planetMgr` at all, and to fix only if
so, test first.

**What it found.** It is reachable, and nothing stops it. After a login the session's
character is nought, and every frame goes to the dispatcher, which looks the service up by
the name in the packet and calls it; the service's base checks anything only where a
character exists. So an account at its selection screen could name any pilot's launch and
have it marked deleted. The store's `deleteLaunch` has the one caller. A launch with no
owner cannot be made by the code as it stands.

**The fix** (`ccf788b7b`): one condition taken out of `deleteLaunch`, so that a launch
that has an owner is removed for that owner only, whatever the caller hands in. Its test
sends the call through the real dispatcher from a session with no character, and was
watched failing first (the launch gone from its owner's list).

**Checked here.** The diff read: one line of source out, a comment in; the rest the test.
Its test file run through that repository's runner: `planetMgrService`, 35 pass. Its six
files of other sessions are as they were.

**Seen live**, EveJS restarted on the commit, three launch records staged in a copy of the
store as before:

- an account logged in on the game port with no character chosen (a script of mine, by the
  transport's own session) names Test Two's launch: answered `false`, and Test Two's list
  still has both. A launch that is not there: `true`, as for anyone;
- the chosen character's run of the entry before, on the game port: the same line for
  line (the route's and the page's write each remove one; another's is `false` and still
  listed for its owner; missing and removed already are `true`).

Not seen live: the same session's call before the fix. The sub-agent's test is what shows
that.

The store was put back, confirmed by probes that only read (no launch for either pilot),
and its copies deleted.

**What it reported beside**, not fixed:

- **`planetMgr.GMCleanupExpiredLaunches` has no check of a role.** The caller names an age
  and, if it likes, an owner; no owner means every owner. Any session could mark deleted
  every pilot's launches older than a day. The client never calls it.
- `GMAddCommodity` puts goods in the caller's own pin with no check of a role; the GM
  reads answer for any planet and any owner named.
- `getLaunch` has the same skipped check; its one caller is the warp to a launch, and no
  effect was found for a session with no character.
- More widely: nothing between a socket and a service asks whether a character is chosen,
  so any handler that hands a store the session's character, where the store reads nought
  as "no filter", has this shape. Only `planetMgr` was looked at.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The GM verbs went back to the same sub-agent as a question first**: what this server's
  rule for a GM verb is, what the client's gate is, and who calls them without a role
  today. It is to fix only where the server has a rule these fall outside of, and to
  change nothing if GM verbs are open on purpose here, which would be the operator's to
  decide.
- `ccf788b7b` is for the operator to push or not, with the four before it.

## 2026-10-10 — the planet service's GM verbs, which asked for no role: the server's rule found, and the six held to it

No commit of code here. In eve.js three more commits on `main`, **not pushed**:
`2b8f1adce`, `5dadba7b0`, `a3745875a`. With the five before them, eve.js is eight commits
ahead of `origin/main`.

**What the sub-agent was given**: its own report of the entry before this one, as a
question first. What is this server's rule for a GM verb; what is the client's gate for
each; who calls them without a role today; what a development account is by default. To
fix only where the server has a rule these fall outside of, and to change nothing if GM
verbs are open here on purpose.

**What it found.**

- **The server has a rule, and one helper for it**: `hasStaffAccountRole(session)`
  (`accountRoleProfiles.js`), used by the QA tools' slash command, the force-state `/pos`
  commands and the node graph, the first two added for this very reason. Three other GM
  verbs check a role themselves. What is open on purpose is chat and slash commands as a
  class: `/giveitem` and the rest run for any account.
- **The client's gates**: `GMAddCommodity` and three of the reads are behind
  `session.role & ROLE_GML`; `GMCleanupExpiredLaunches` and `GMGetPlanetDiagnostics` the
  client never calls.
- **Callers here**: one test, from a session with no role. No harness, script or gateway
  list; nothing in this repository.
- **A development account is a staff account unless saved otherwise** (`isGM` missing is
  true; made accounts are written true). Only an account saved `isGM: false` is refused.

**The fixes**: one helper in the planet service, asked first by each of the six.
`2b8f1adce` the cleanup (its test: another pilot naming the owner, and a session with no
character, both refused and the launch still listed); `5dadba7b0` `GMAddCommodity` (21
units where 12 were wanted, before); `a3745875a` the four reads. Each test watched failing
first. One existing test now carries the role its scenario implied; no assertion changed.

**Checked here.** The diffs read: the helper, and one line at the head of each of six
handlers. The test file run through that repository's runner: `planetMgrService`, 38 pass.
Its six files of other sessions are as they were.

**Seen live**, EveJS restarted on the commits; in a copy of the store the account `test`
saved `isGM: false` and three launches three days old staged (two of Test Two's, one of
Test Pilot's); each asked by a session of mine on the game port with no character chosen:

- as `test`: the four reads, `GMAddCommodity`, and the cleanup both for a named owner and
  for every owner: each refused, "This planet command requires a staff account". Both
  pilots' launches as they were;
- as `rrfarmer`, a staff account as saved: the cleanup of Test Two's launches older than a
  day answers scanned 2, deleted 2; Test Two's list is empty and Test Pilot's has its one.

Not seen live: `GMAddCommodity` and the reads answered for a staff account with a planet
(the test has them); the refusals before the fix (the tests have those).

The store was put back and confirmed by reads alone (no launch for either pilot; `test`
answered a GM read again), and its copies deleted.

**What it reported beside**, not fixed then:

- `structureAssetSafety.MoveEjectTimeGM` takes any wrap's ID and a number of days, reads
  no session and checks no role; the client's gate is `ROLE_GML`.
- `shipCosmeticsMgr.GMExpireSkinLicense` checks no role, and expires only the caller's own.
- A grep of mine for the handlers named as GM verbs finds three more it had not named:
  `GMReimburseBounties`, `GMClearBountyCache` and a bare `GM`.

**Slip.** A test of mine for the next unit left a companion flying when its assertion
failed, and its file's process never ended: the run sat for 400 seconds until I stopped
that one process by its command line. The test stops its companion whatever happens now.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The five GM-named handlers left went to the same sub-agent**, bounded to those five:
  each read, the client's gate found, and gated by the same helper only where it checks
  nothing and touches what is not the caller's own; one commit each, test first.
- **Chat and slash commands were left open**, as the server's own commits say they are
  meant to be: an account that is not staff can still give itself items by them. That is
  the operator's to decide, and is said here so that it is seen.
- The eight commits in eve.js are for the operator to push or not.

## 2026-10-10 — a fleet applied to and a broadcast to the bubble, by the page itself; and a companion seen flying in the tab

Commit `82a21e8`, pushed. Next's head: the fleet's two.

**What the routes did.** `POST /api/bridge/fleet/apply` checks `confirm` and makes
`fleetProxy.ApplyToJoinFleet` with the fleet's ID made a number and `autoAccept` made true
or false. `POST /api/bridge/fleet/broadcast/bubble` checks `confirm` and makes
`fleetMgr.BroadcastToBubble` with the name, the scope, the item made a number, and the type
left empty where none came. The fifth and sixth of the seven that are a confirmation and
one call.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller.

- **Applying** (`fleetSvc.ApplyToJoinFleet`, 1898 to 1910). In a fleet already it refuses
  its own (`FleetYouAreAlreadyInFleet`), and for another asks to change and leaves first.
  Then it notes the fleet it expects an invitation from and calls
  `sm.ProxySvc('fleetProxy').ApplyToJoinFleet(fleetID, autoAccept)`. A true answer is "the
  boss must approve" (`FleetApplicationReceived`); otherwise an invitation comes
  (`OnFleetInvite`), which it accepts unasked where the invitation says `autoAccept`, and
  asks the pilot about where not. Four callers: the fleet finder's button and its row
  (`fleetfinder.py` 373, `fleetFinderEntry.py` 71) and a fleet's link (1920), all with
  False; the Agency's join window, after its own yes, with True
  (`joinFleetConfirmation.py` 25).
- **Broadcasting to the bubble** (`SendBubbleBroadcast`, 992 to 998). It must hold a
  fleet's object and be in space; it must not be inside its own wait (962 to 981: two
  seconds since its last broadcast of the same name, a third of that since one of
  another; the time is kept before the call is made); the name must be one it knows. Then
  `sm.RemoteSvc('fleetMgr').BroadcastToBubble(name, self.broadcastScope, itemID, typeID)`.
  Five callers, none giving a type: the three calls for repair with the pilot's own ship,
  Target and HealTarget with an item (1039 to 1055).

**The recordings.** Neither call is in any folder of them.

**The server's handlers**, read for what each trusts. An application is the session's own
character's, to a fleet that is advertised and open to it; the flag only rides the
invitation. A broadcast is the session's own character's in the session's own fleet; the
name must be one of the server's, the scope is held to a number, and the item and the type
are handed on to the members as they came, as a client's are. The server keeps the
client's wait itself and answers false inside it.

**What of the page's makes them.** Applying: the Companions window (a fleet's name typed
for an op), a bot's join-by-name block, and the mining support's command run. Broadcasting:
the companion, which calls a ship out by Target when it is warp scrambled and is no
commander. The mining support's branch is reached by no run as the code reads: its fleet
reading hands its decider no adverts, and the decider applies only to one it sees
advertised. It was changed with the others and has no test.

**What was built.**

- `web/src/bridge/fleetWrites.ts`: `applyToJoinFleet(act, fleetID, autoAccept)`, which
  reads the call's own answer, and `createFleetBroadcasts(act)`, whose `toBubble` keeps
  the client's wait and asks nothing inside it. The flow's call sites go by them. The
  page applies with True from all three: who applies there has said yes already.
- Both pairs on the BFF's list of the page's own writes (eight now), each with its entry
  against the client's line and a judge: an application names one fleet and a yes or no,
  from a session in no fleet; a broadcast one of the five names, a scope, the item and no
  type, from a session in a fleet.
- The two routes' askings out of `api.ts`; the route's acknowledgement decoder gone.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 15 written first, and the module's two for the route's decoder gone with it
  (13 more in the suite). The flow's (`web/src/app/fleetApplyFlow.test.ts`: a bot
  joining by name over a stand-in BFF, the finder read, the page's call, the invitation
  accepted, the route never asked; an application the boss must approve followed by no
  acceptance; the flow's own application) and the companion's (a plain member scrambled
  calls the tackler out by the page's call) were watched failing on the old code. The
  module's eight, the BFF's one for the two writes and two for the entries' forms. With
  the sources of the commit before, 8 fail and the module's file cannot load.
- Breakages: 59, all caught.
- Suite: 10281 tests, 10257 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport** (Test Pilot forms a fleet and advertises it through the
  gateway BFF; Test Three, docked beside it at Jita, is the member, on the game port and

  - the boss's approval wanted: True by each way, the member listed as asking, and the

  - both in space off the station: Target on the boss's ship by the route and by the

## 2026-10-10 — the handlers named as GM verbs that were left: one more held to the rule, one left for the operator

No commit of code here. In eve.js one more commit on `main`, **not pushed**: `c3fe5e6c8`.
eve.js is nine commits ahead of `origin/main`.

**What the sub-agent was given**: the five handlers named as GM verbs that the entries
before had not reached, bounded to those five; each to be read, the client's gate found,
and gated only where it checks nothing and touches what is not the caller's own, or where
the client's own gate is a staff role.

| the handler | what it found | done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `structureAssetSafety.MoveEjectTimeGM` | **real**: it takes any wrap's ID and a number of days and moves that wrap's eject time, reads no session and checks no role; the client shows it only to `ROLE_GML` (`assetSafetyEntry.py` 48) | **not fixed**: the shared harness calls it from a pilot with no role (`harness/verbs/structures.js` 269, two scenarios). The gate is one line once the harness gives that pilot a role |
| `shipCosmeticsMgr.GMExpireSkinLicense` | expires one of the caller's own SKIN licences, with no check; the client's gate is `ROLE_GML` (`skinPanel.py` 624) | `c3fe5e6c8`: for a staff account only, its test watched failing first |
| `bountyProxy.GMReimburseBounties`, `GMClearBountyCache` | each adds a line to a list in memory that only a test reads, and answers nothing | left: they change and show nothing |
| `contractProxy.GM_ExpireContract` (the fifth: there is no bare `GM`) | the same, answering false; it is on the web gateway's list | left |

Beside these it saw `shipCosmeticsMgr.GiveSkin`, which gives the caller any SKIN with no
check of a role and is offered by the client from the same GM menu. Not named as a GM
verb, and not touched.

**Checked here.** The diff read: the helper's import and one check at the head of the
handler; the rest its test. Its test file run through that repository's runner:
`shipCosmeticsSkinLicense`, 2 pass. Its six files of other sessions are as they were.

**Seen live**, EveJS restarted on the commit, the account `rrfarmer` saved `isGM: false`
in a copy of the store: asked by a session with no character chosen, it is refused,
"Expiring a SKIN license this way requires a staff account"; a staff account is answered
(nothing, having no character). The store was put back with the fleet's.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **`MoveEjectTimeGM` is left as it is, and is the operator's.** Fixing it means changing
  the harness other sessions share (their uncommitted files are in that part of the
  tree), and which way the harness should give a pilot a role is theirs to say. Until
  then any session can move any asset-safety wrap's eject time.
- **`GiveSkin` was not sent back.** It is one more of a kind already shown here; a sweep
  of every handler the client offers only from a GM menu is a piece of work to be asked
  for, not slipped in beside a fleet's calls.
- The nine commits in eve.js are for the operator to push or not.

## 2026-10-10 — a module overloaded and cooled by the page itself: the first of the writes on a bound object

Commit `431b964`, pushed. Next's head: the first of the 26.

**Sized first.** Seven of the page's routes go by one helper (`dispatchBoundDogmaWrite`): a
confirmation, then one call on a dogma object the BFF binds for itself, beside the dogma
location the transport already keeps as godma keeps it. The page names six of them:
overload on and off, a repair started and stopped, all weapons linked and unlinked. This
unit is the overload's two. The repair's and the weapon banks' are next.

**What the routes did.** `POST /api/bridge/dogma/module/overload` and `.../stop-overload`
check `confirm` and make `Overload(moduleID, effectID)` or `StopOverload(moduleID, effectID)`
on the BFF's own dogma object. The page sent the module alone, so the effect went as 0.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. Godma makes both (`godma.py` 2074 and
2119): the call on the dogma location bound for where the pilot is, then its own pending
states. The module's button calls godma (`shipmodulebutton.py` 215 to 249): it looks
through the module's effects for the one of the overload category and does nothing if there
is none; then Overload for a module not overloaded, StopOverload for one that is or is on
its way. A rack's button asks for the whole rack (`OverloadRack`), which the page has not.

**The recordings.** Two, one in each of two files (GoneBerserkLevel1, TheBlockadeLevel1):
the module button pressed, and on the dogma location's object `Overload` with the module
and effect 3001; each time the server answers the user error
`DontHaveThermoDynamicsSkill`, `skillLevel` 1. `StopOverload` is in none.

**The server's handlers**, read for what they trust. Each takes the ship the session is
flying and refuses a module not fitted to it (`DeniedShipChanged`), offline, burnt out, or
with no overload effect; a pilot with no Thermodynamics is refused. The effect only picks
among the module's own overload effects; with 0 the module's own is taken.

**What was built.**

- The page makes the calls (`web/src/bridge/dogmaWrites.ts`, `setOverload`) with the
  module's own overload effect named. What a type's effect is the client has in its own
  static data; the page asks the BFF's copy, once for a type, and keeps the answer
  (`GET /api/types/overload-effects`, `staticData.getOverloadEffectID`: no call of the
  server's). A module with no such effect, or one not fitted to the ship, is not asked of
  the server at all, as the client has no button for it.
- Both pairs on the BFF's list of the page's own writes (ten now), asked of the dogma
  service by its name: the game port makes each on the dogma location it keeps. Each has
  its entry against the client's line, where it had none. The transport knows a module's
  own overload effect from godma's priming: a call that names none (the routes') is given
  it, and one that names another is counted as differing.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 21 new, the flow's five first (`web/src/app/overloadFlow.test.ts`: overloaded
  and cooled by the page's calls with the effect named and asked for once; a module with
  no overload effect, one not fitted, an effect that cannot be read, and an answer that is
  no effect's ID, each sending nothing), watched failing on the old code. With the sources
  of the commit before, 16 fail and the module's file cannot load.
- Breakages: 61; 60 caught, and one that comes to the same (a check of the kind that the
  whole-number check beside it makes again; it is there for the type checker). Three
  checks nothing could tell from their absence were taken out before the pass.
- Suite: 10302 tests, 10278 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport**, in the server's prepared ship off Jita; the route and the
  page's write answer alike at every step, and but for one notice so do the transports:
  - each write with nothing said, `pilot` alone, `confirm` alone: 403;
  - with no Thermodynamics (the game port's first run): `DontHaveThermoDynamicsSkill` by
    each way, which is what Tranquility answered;
  - with it: the route overloads one module and the page's write another; each answers
    the module's ID, and the ship's snapshot lists the module. Again for one overloaded:
    the same answer. Each cools its module, and the list follows;
  - the effect named by the route as the client names it: the same;
  - an effect that is not the module's overload effect: "cannot be overloaded" by each;
    a module that is not there, and the ship itself: `DeniedShipChanged` by each.
  The game port's ledger: the page's calls `reshaped` (asked by name, made on the
  moniker), the route's with no effect `reshaped` to the module's own, the route's with
  it `same`, and the twelve made wrong on purpose `differs`.
- **In the browser, on both pages**: a module held on the rack sent `GET
  /api/types/overload-effects` for its type, then `POST /api/bridge/call` with
  `dogmaIM.Overload`, the module and effect 3174, `pilot` and `confirm`; the tile read
  "Overloaded: running hot and taking damage". A second hold sent `StopOverload` with the
  same two and no second asking for the effect, and the tile read as before. Neither
  route was asked.
- The store was put back and confirmed by reads alone (neither pilot has Thermodynamics),
  and its copy deleted. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: 134 routes named by the whole path (51 reads, 83 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- Through the gateway an overload's answer carries `OnGodmaShipEffect` alone; on the game
  port `OnModuleAttributeChanges` comes with it. By the route and by the page alike.
- What the page says for `DontHaveThermoDynamicsSkill` was not looked at in the browser.
- The client keeps four states for a module's overload (two of them pending); the page
  keeps the server's word of overloaded or not, and sends by that.
- The client's lock on overloading (a setting) and its rack-wide button are not the
  page's.
- Of a type with two overload effects the static data's word is the first as the type
  lists them. The client takes the first its own dictionary gives.

**Slips.**

- My transport test first wanted `same` for a call asked by name and made on the moniker.
  The transport counts every such call `reshaped`, with the client's arguments or not,
  and an older test says so. That older test used `Overload` as its example of a call
  nobody had read against the client; it uses `OverloadRack` now, which is still unread.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **A static route was added for the effect** (`/api/types/overload-effects`), beside the
  one for cycle times: it is the client's static data, not a call of the server's.
- **A module with no overload effect is refused by the page**, in the page's words, where
  the server's refusal used to be shown.
- **The transport gives a call that names no effect the module's own**, so the route,
  which still stands, is the client's call on the game port too.
- **The unit was kept to the overload.** The weapon banks' handlers take a ship's ID from
  the caller; whose ship they will act on is to be read before that pair is moved.
- Thermodynamics was given to two pilots for the checks, and went with the store.

## 2026-10-10 — a module's repair, begun and ended by the page itself; and that the page's repair had mended nothing

Commit `766627e`, pushed. Next's head: the module's repair.

**What the routes did.** `POST /api/bridge/dogma/module/repair/start` checks `confirm` and
makes `InitiateModuleRepair(moduleID)` on the BFF's own dogma object. `.../repair/stop`
makes `StopModuleRepair(moduleID)`; the page had a function for it that nothing called.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. A repair is two calls, and both are
godma's (`godma.py` 2225 to 2262).

- `RepairModule(itemID)`: `InitiateModuleRepair(itemID)` on the dogma location. An answer
  of False ends it there. Otherwise godma notes the module and the time, and starts a
  thread that waits the repair's time: the module's damage over the character's repair
  rate is the minutes, cut to whole milliseconds, and a second more.
- When the wait is over, and the module is still the same beginning's, **godma itself
  calls `StopModuleRepair(itemID)`**. It calls it too at Cancel Repair, and for every
  repair it began when the session changes station, system, ship, character or structure
  (`ProcessSessionChange`, 1156 and 1199).
- The module's button offers Repair for a module with damage that is not being repaired,
  and Cancel Repair for one that is (`shipmodulebutton.py` 497 to 505); a bank's slaves
  are repaired with their master. Several at once go by `InitiateModuleRepairMany`.

**The recordings.** Neither call is in any folder of them.

**The server's handlers**, read for what they trust and for when the module is mended. A
repair is begun only in space, for a damaged module the session's character owns, fitted
to the ship it is flying and not running; the paste comes out of that ship's hold, and the
repair is kept with the session. **The module is mended in `StopModuleRepair` and nowhere
else**: by the time since the beginning at the rate kept with it. Nothing on the server
ends a repair.

**So the page's repair mended nothing.** It began one, the paste went, and nothing ever
ended it. Seen live below, by the route as it stood.

**What was built.**

- `web/src/bridge/dogmaWrites.ts`: `repairWaitMs(damage, rate)`, godma's arithmetic; and
  `createModuleRepairs(act)`, godma's keeping of the repairs it began. `begin` makes the
  first call and arms the second for when the time is up; `end` and `endAll` make the
  second at once. A beginning that was ended and begun again is not ended by the first
  one's time.
- The flow's `repairModule` goes by it. The time comes from what godma was primed with
  (the module's hit points, the character's repair rate) and the ship's reading of the
  damage, a share of those hit points. Where it cannot be worked out nothing is begun,
  so that no paste goes for a repair nobody would end. A module being repaired is not
  begun again. At a session's change that names one of godma's five, every repair begun
  is ended. When a repair ends the ship is read again.
- Both pairs on the BFF's list of the page's own writes (twelve now), asked of the dogma
  service by its name, each with its entry against the client's line.
- Both routes' askings out of `api.ts`.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 18 new, the flow's six first (`web/src/app/repairFlow.test.ts`), watched failing
  on the old code. With the sources of the commit before, 10 fail and the module's file
  cannot load.
- Breakages: 52, all caught in the end. Four got through the first time (the module
  taken for the first item godma was primed with; the hit points, the damage and a rate
  of nought not looked for) and are caught since the flow's test was made to tell them.
- Suite: 10320 tests, 10296 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport**, in the server's prepared ship off Jita, its mid rack heated
  by running the drive overloaded until modules were damaged (16% each), with 200 of
  paste in the hold. The route and the page's write answer alike at every step, and so
  do the transports:
  - each write with nothing said, `pilot` alone, `confirm` alone: 403;
  - a repair begun by the route and one by the page's write: True each, and 4 of the
    paste go for each (200, 196, 192). Begun again: True, and no more goes;
  - **twelve seconds on, with neither ended, both modules are as damaged as they were**;
  - ended by the route and by the page's write: True each, and each module is mended by
    the same share (0.164 to 0.114);
  - ended again, a module with no damage, and a module that is not there: False by each;
  - with no paste in the hold (the first run, below): the user error
    `NotEnoughRepairMaterialToFinishAllRepairs` by each.
  The game port's ledger: the routes' calls `same`, the page's `reshaped` (asked by name,
  made on the moniker), nothing differing.
- **In the browser, on both pages**, a pilot left in space with damaged modules and
  paste: the rack listed them, "16% damaged", each with Repair. Repair on one sent `POST
  /api/bridge/call` with `dogmaIM.InitiateModuleRepair`, the module, `pilot` and
  `confirm`, and the list stayed as it was. With nothing pressed, the page then sent
  `StopModuleRepair` for the module (between 36 and 53 seconds after on the game port's
  page, between 33 and 45 through the gateway's; the time worked out is 40), and the
  module was gone from the damaged. Neither route was asked.
- The store was put back and confirmed by reads alone (Test Pilot docked in its own ship
  with no prepared ship and no paste; Test Three with no Thermodynamics), and its copy
  deleted. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: 132 routes named by the whole path (51 reads, 81 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- **The BFF goes on holding the ship it last boarded by its own route.** A hull boarded
  for the pilot by a slash command is not the one its "hold" means: paste moved "into the
  hold" by the transfer route went into the ship left in the hangar. (`readHeldFlight`
  says so of itself: the active ship is the board route's.) Whether a ship lost in space
  leaves the same behind was not tried. The staging chooses the pilot afresh now.
- The page has no Cancel Repair, and no word on the rack that a module is being
  repaired: Repair pressed again says so in the action's line.
- A repair in progress when the tab closes is not ended; the client's is ended by its
  session's change, and a client that goes away leaves the same behind.
- A bank's slaves are not repaired with their master, and several are not begun at once.
- The time is worked out from the hit points godma was primed with and the ship's reading
  of the damage. Godma reads the damage itself, as an attribute of the module's; the two
  were not set side by side.
- After the drive's run the pilot was far from the station: the dock asked at the end of
  the game port's run answered 409, and that page's pilot was left approaching the
  station and not logged out by its button. The BFF's restart and the store's putting
  back cleared it.

**Slips.**

- The first live run began with the paste in the wrong ship (above), and so measured
  only the refusal for want of paste. Kept as that.
- My arithmetic for one test's expected figure was wrong by a millisecond (a third of a
  minute is exactly 20000 here); the test said so, and has figures that are cut.
- I wrote one change to a scratch script through the shell again. It went in whole, and
  was not the way.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **This is a fix of the page, and was committed as one**: a repair by the page now
  mends the module, where it took the paste and did nothing.
- **Where the repair's time cannot be worked out the page begins nothing**, and says so.
- **Every repair begun is ended at a session's change**, as godma's are, though that
  mends less than waiting would have.
- Thermodynamics, paste and a prepared ship were given to two pilots, and modules
  damaged by heat, for the checks. All of it went with the store.

    and three change nothing. Left: `structureAssetSafety.MoveEjectTimeGM`, which moves any

## 2026-10-10 — a ship's weapons linked and unlinked by the page itself; a server that let any pilot regroup any ship's; and the game port's own banks after a call by name

Commit `4bd05a7`, pushed. In `eve.js`, `515ebd911` (local, not pushed, as the rule has it).
Next's head: the weapon banks.

**What the routes did.** `POST /api/bridge/dogma/weapons/link-all` checks `confirm` and
makes `LinkAllWeapons(shipID)` on the BFF's own dogma object, with the ship the BFF holds
as the session's. `.../unlink-all` makes `UnlinkAllModules(shipID)` the same way. The
page named no ship.

**What a retail client does**, from every caller. One button makes both
(`groupAllIcon.py` 28 to 39), through the dogma location (`clientDogmaLocation.py` 793 to
803), each with `session.shipid`.

- Where some weapon could still be grouped (`CanGroupAll`) the click is
  `LinkAllWeapons(shipID)`; otherwise it is `UnlinkAllModules(shipID)`. With the "lock
  modules" setting on, the click does nothing.
- **Once the server has answered, the client sets its own banks**: to the link's answer
  (each master with its slaves), and to none after the unlink, whatever that answered.
- It then notes the time. The button is dead until two seconds have gone since the last
  request of its kind was answered, each kind with a time of its own.
- The button is there only where some groupable kind of weapon has more than one online.

**The recordings.** Neither call is in any folder of them. `LinkWeapons(shipID, master,
slave)`, which links two by hand, is, riding the dogma location's bind, with the ship's
banks as its answer.

**The server's handlers, and a defect.** All seven weapon-bank calls took the ship from
their first argument, and the banks are kept by the ship's ID with no owner beside them.
**Any session could group or break up the weapons of any pilot's ship by naming it.** The
BFF's routes hid that by naming the ship themselves; a page that names the ship, as a
client does, would not have.

- Given to the sub-agent, with a failing test asked for first. Its test (in
  `server/tests/moduleGroupingParity.test.js`) has an owner with one bank of two guns and
  two loose ones, and sends each of the seven naming that ship from another pilot flying
  its own ship and from a session with no ship. Before the fix, by its report, all
  fourteen changed the owner's banks (16 pass, 1 fail).
- The fix (`515ebd911`): one place decides the ship for all seven. A call naming a ship
  other than the one the session is flying, or made by a session flying none, is refused
  before a bank is read or written. A call naming the session's own ship, or none, goes
  as before. I read the change and ran the file: 17 pass, 0 fail.
- **It chose to refuse, not to do nothing**: a quiet answer is one the client then sets
  its banks from. And it refused a session with no ship, because the server answers a
  placeholder ship for one, which would have left that one item open to all of them.
- Seen live after it, below. I did not see the defect live before the fix: its test did.

**What was built.**

- `web/src/bridge/dogmaWrites.ts`: `createWeaponGrouping(act)`. `linkAll(shipID)` and
  `unlinkAll(shipID)` make the calls and keep the client's wait: a request inside two
  seconds of one of its kind being answered is not made. A refusal starts no wait.
- The flow's `setWeaponBanks` goes by it, naming the ship the pilot is flying (the
  fitting's, or the snapshot's where no fitting is read). With no ship known nothing is
  asked. A request held by the wait is said in the action's line.
- Both pairs on the BFF's list of the page's own writes (fourteen now), asked of the
  dogma service by its name, each with its entry against the client's line: a call
  naming a ship other than the session's is counted as differing.
- **The game port sets its own banks from a grouping call's answer where the call was
  asked by name.** It did so for a call on a handle, which is how the routes asked. Found
  live (below), then a test seen failing, then one line.
- Both routes' askings out of `api.ts`.

**Proof.**

- Tests: 12 new, and two older ones made longer. The flow's four first
  (`web/src/app/weaponBanksFlow.test.ts`), watched failing on the old code. With the
  sources of the commit before, 10 fail and the module's file cannot load.
- Breakages: 41, all caught in the end. One got through the first time (a failed unlink
  starting the wait) and is caught since its test asks twice.
- Suite: 10332 tests, 10308 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped.
- **Live, on each transport**, in the server's prepared ship with three guns of one kind
  (`/probe2`), off Jita. The route and the page's write answer alike at every step, and
  so do the transports:
  - each write with nothing said, `pilot` alone, `confirm` alone: 403, and no bank;
  - linked by the route: the answer is one master with two slaves, and the ship reads a
    bank of three. Unlinked by the page's write: an empty answer, and no bank. Linked by
    the page's write: a bank of three. Linked again: the same answer. Unlinked by the
    route, and again by each: empty, and no bank;
  - **a ship that is not there, and another pilot's ship with its own bank of three,
    each named by the page's write: 409, in the server's words, for the link and for the
    unlink; the other pilot's bank of three as it was after each**, and the asker's own
    untouched.
  The game port's ledger: the routes' calls `same`, the page's `reshaped` (asked by name,
  made on the dogma location), the four that named another ship `differs`.
- **The first run on the game port showed the ship still reading a bank of three after
  the page's unlink had been answered.** The server had no bank; the game port's own
  were not set, because that was done only for a call on a handle. Fixed, and the run
  made again: none after the unlink, three after the link.
- **In the browser, on both pages**, a pilot in space in that ship. The rack's button
  read "Link weapons" or "Unlink weapons. 3 weapons banked." as the ship was. Pressed, it
  sent `POST /api/bridge/call` with `dogmaIM.LinkAllWeapons` or `UnlinkAllModules`, the
  ship's ID, `pilot` and `confirm`, and read the other way after each. A third press
  inside two seconds of the last link's answer sent nothing, and the action's line said
  it had been done a moment ago. After the wait it linked again. Neither route was asked.
  Each pilot was docked from the header and the page logged out by its button.
- The store was put back and confirmed by reading the pilots' rows on the page (Test
  Pilot docked in its own ship, Test Three in its capsule, no prepared ship), and its
  copy deleted. Both BFFs run the committed code.

**6b's measure**: 130 routes named by the whole path (51 reads, 79 writes).

**Measured and left.**

- **The rack's rule is not the client's.** It shows the button where the high rack has
  more than one module of any kind, and sends the unlink where any module is banked. The
  client shows it where a groupable kind has more than one online, and sends the link
  wherever something could still be grouped. They part on a ship partly banked (the
  client links the rest; the rack unlinks all) and on a ship whose high slots hold no two
  weapons of a kind.
- The client's "lock modules" setting is not on the page.
- The wait is kept by the tab. Two tabs of one pilot each keep their own.
- Linking a ship already linked is answered with its banks, not refused.
- **`LoadAmmo` and `UnloadAmmo` take the ship from their first argument in the same
  words** (the sub-agent's note; `moduleOperation.js` 3541 and 3823). Whether what they
  check further down holds for a ship that is not the caller's is not established.
  Neither is on the page's list. To be read before either goes on.
- The server answers a placeholder ship (140000101) for a session with none, in the
  dogma service, the inventory broker and the ship service. Whether an item of that ID
  is in a store was not looked at.
- A comment in the web gateway's runtime (2774 to 2777) still says these calls wait on a
  fix. Not changed.
- `server/tests/groupedTurretFxParity.test.js` is red before the fix and after it, by
  the sub-agent's run with the old handler put back: its activation is refused for want
  of ammunition.
- A pilot controlling a structure names the structure; that case was not run.
- On the gateway's page, choosing the pilot asked `charUnboundMgr.GetCharacterSelectionData`
  by HTTP and not by the socket. One asking, seen once.

**Slips.**

- I had read that the client sets its banks from the answer, and had not looked for
  where the game port does the same for a call asked by name. The live run said so.
- I asked the breakage tool for a part numbered nought. It ran nothing and said so.

**Decisions taken in the operator's place.**

- **The two pairs went on the page's list only once the server's fix was in and seen
  live.** With the server as it was, a page naming the ship would have opened every
  ship's banks to every pilot.
- The refusal of a session with no ship, which the sub-agent added beyond what was
  asked, is kept.
- **Where no ship is known the page asks nothing**, and says so.
- The rack's own rule for which call to send was left as it is, and written down.
- `eve.js` is ten commits ahead of its origin and not pushed.
- A prepared ship was given to two pilots and flown off Jita for the checks. All of it
  went with the store.
